The markers are pervasive. I've mapped exactly where they live. Here's the plan.

## What the spec loses (implementation status)

The spec keeps its **protocol contract** (the full semantic surface, ID allocations, reserved/unallocated ranges, wire conventions) but drops everything about "is it implemented today":

- **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** — remove the status legend, the `Status` column from the A/B/C mapping tables, the ✅/🚧 in section headings (`### Text — ✅ TEXT 0x01` → `### Text — TEXT 0x01`), the inline 🚧 next to property IDs (`IMAGE_SOURCE (🚧 0x1002)` → `IMAGE_SOURCE (0x1002)`), and reword the reserved-ranges table (`Implemented/draft primitive drawing nodes` → `Primitive drawing nodes (allocated)`; the `unallocated` / `reserved–never reused` rows stay — that's ID authority, not implementation).
- **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** — remove the status legend, the `Status` column in the 5 modifier tables, and the ✅/🚧 in the property-ID catalog (replace with allocation ranges: `allocated` vs `unallocated`); reword `Layout drafts` → `Layout properties (allocated)`. Keep the `0x2011 unallocated/reserved` note.
- **`spec/EVENTS.md`** — remove the status legend, the `Status` column in the event + listener-bit tables, reword reserved ranges (`Implemented core events` → `Core events (allocated)`), and **delete the stale "host → guest batches … not yet implemented" line** (we confirmed network duplex already exists end-to-end).
- **`spec/OPCODE.md`** — strip the `**Draft.**` prefixes on `SET_DATE`, `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE` (the rows stay — they're protocol-defined; "Draft." was implementation status).
- Replace the three removed legends with one shared note: *"Implementation status is tracked per implementing project (see `status.md` in each crate), not in this specification."*

## What's new: `status.md` per implementing project

- **`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/status.md`** — the protocol surface present in `constants.rs` (all component types, properties, commands, event commands, listener bits) + what's encoded/decoded (TREE/STYLE/META/EVENT, `Event` enum 0x01–0x07, the two-way event arena, `SET_DATE`/0x08–0x0D as constants-only, conformance vectors).
- **`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/status.md`** — components → GTK widgets (stacks/text/button/grid/scroll/zstack/spacer/image), properties applied, events wired (pointer only today; TOGGLE/SLIDER/TEXT_FIELD native tokens + value/text events still Tier 2).
- **`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`** — every component rendered, every property applied, event-surfacing `data-*` attrs.

## Questions
1. **status.md scope** — just `pathland-core` + the two renderers, or also the other Rust crates (`pathland-view`, `pathland-view-native`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-core-transport`) and the Java/TS projects (`pathland-view` Java, Angular)?
2. **AGENTS.md** — its quick-reference component table carries `(draft)` annotations (same implementation-status category). Clean those too and point at `status.md`, or leave the agent guide as-is?
3. Keep the `**Status:** Draft` document headers in the spec files (spec-document maturity, not implementation status) — I'll keep them unless you object.
1: All of it. 2: Point to status files. 3: Yes

All three answered. Here's the final plan.

## Phase A — Purge implementation status from the spec

Each spec file keeps its **protocol contract** (semantic surface, ID allocations, reserved/unallocated ranges, wire conventions) but drops all "implemented today" info:

- **`PRIMITIVES.md`** — delete the status legend; drop the `Status` column from the A/B/C mapping tables; strip ✅/🚧 from section headings and inline property refs (`IMAGE_SOURCE (🚧 0x1002)` → `(0x1002)`); reword the reserved-ranges table (`Implemented/draft …` → `… (allocated)`, keeping `unallocated` + `reserved–never reused` rows); purge implementation-status notes (e.g. "Until `IMAGE_SOURCE` is implemented…", "the Java DSL currently materializes `ZStack` as `COMMENT`" → moves to status files).
- **`MODIFIERS.md`** — delete the legend + `Status` columns (5 modifier tables + property-ID catalog); reword range descriptions (`Layout drafts` → `Layout properties (allocated)`); drop "the reference `value_type_for`/`forProperty` helpers are aligned with it" → "The canonical value type per property."
- **`EVENTS.md`** — delete the legend + `Status` columns (event + listener-bit tables); reword reserved ranges; **delete the stale "host → guest batches … not yet implemented" line**.
- **`OPCODE.md`** — strip `**Draft.**` prefixes on `SET_DATE`/`ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`; drop "today" from the `ENUM` value-type note.
- Add to each file a shared note: *"Implementation status is tracked per implementing project (`status.md` in each crate/library), not in this specification."* Keep the `**Status:** Draft` document headers (spec maturity, per your yes).

## Phase B — `status.md` per implementing project (~12 files)

Content template: purpose → **Implemented** (components/properties/commands/events it defines, encodes, or renders) → **Not implemented / gaps** → **Verified by** → Last updated.

| `pathland-render-gtk` | Widget map (stacks/text/button/grid/scroll/zstack/spacer/image); props applied; pointer events. Gap: TOGGLE/SLIDER/TEXT_FIELD native tokens + value/text events (Tier 2). |
| `pathland-render-html` | All components, all props, composite mode, `data-*` event attrs, `SET_DATE`. |
| `pathland-view` (Java) | DSL, signals/computed/effects, emitter, `PLPL` codec, FFM ring, `State`. |
| `pathland-render-html` (Java) | SSR renderer surface. |
| `lib/angular` | ngui renderer, `decoder.ts`, `event-encoder.ts`, replay-on-connect. |

**Not getting status.md** (they don't implement the protocol): the demos (`pathland-render-gtk-demo`, `pathland-quarkus-demo`, `pathland-spring-boot-demo`, `pathland-demo-views`), `pathland-state-redis` (state store), `pathland-view-processor` (JSR269 codegen). Flag if you want them anyway.

Point at the status files: strip the `(draft)` annotations from the quick-reference tables, and add a one-line pointer next to the crate list ("implementation status: see `<crate>/status.md`").

## Phase B — `status.md` per implementing project (~12 files)

## Phase C — AGENTS.md

- **New agent duty (per your addition):** add an explicit rule — in the Implementation Guidelines — that **whenever an agent lands protocol or renderer changes, it MUST update the affected project's `status.md`** (component/property/command/event coverage, encoder/renderer surface, tests), so the status files never go stale.

import re

def strip_status(text):
    lines = text.split('\n')
    out = []
    in_table = False
    status_idx = None
    for line in lines:
        if line.lstrip().startswith('|'):
            cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip('|').split('|')]
            if not in_table:
                if 'Status' in cells:
                    status_idx = cells.index('Status')
                    in_table = True
                else:
                    out.append(line)
                    continue
            # separator row
            if all(re.fullmatch(r'[-: ]+', c) for c in cells):
                cells.pop(status_idx)
                out.append('| ' + ' | '.join(cells) + ' |')
                continue
            if status_idx < len(cells):
                cells.pop(status_idx)
                out.append('| ' + ' | '.join(cells) + ' |')
            else:
                out.append(line)
        else:
            in_table = False
            status_idx = None
            out.append(line)
    return '\n'.join(out)

for path in ["spec/PRIMITIVES.md", "spec/MODIFIERS.md", "spec/EVENTS.md", "spec/OPCODE.md"]:
    s = open(path).read()
    s = strip_status(s)
    # heading markers: "### Text — ✅ `TEXT` 0x01"
    s = re.sub(r' — [✅🚧] ', ' — ', s)
    # inline draft/status markers on property IDs
    s = s.replace('(🚧 ', '(')
    # standalone inline status glyphs left in prose
    s = s.replace(' ✅ ', ' ')
    s = s.replace('✅*', '')
    s = s.replace('**Draft.** ', '')
    s = re.sub(r'\s*[✅🚧]\s*', '', s)
    open(path, 'w').write(s)
    print("processed", path)
PY

# pathland-core — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The **protocol core**: 16-byte opcode, SPSC ring buffers (both directions),
bump arenas (both directions), memory layout, typed events, and the golden
conformance vectors. The protocol contract is defined in `spec/`; this file
tracks what this crate implements.

## Implemented

- **Component types** (`constants.rs::component_type`): the full grouped map —
  `TEXT 0x01, IMAGE 0x02, COLOR 0x03, SHAPE 0x04, DIVIDER 0x05, SPACER 0x06,
  PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07, GAUGE 0x08, VSTACK 0x10, HSTACK 0x11, ZSTACK 0x12, GRID
  0x13, SCROLLVIEW 0x14, LAZY_VGRID 0x15, LAZY_HGRID 0x16, LAZY_VSTACK 0x1B,
  LAZY_HSTACK 0x1C, BUTTON 0x20, TEXT_FIELD 0x21, TEXT_EDITOR 0x22, TOGGLE
  0x24, SLIDER 0x25, STEPPER 0x26, DATE_PICKER 0x27, PICKER 0x28, MENU 0x29,
  COLOR_PICKER 0x2A, COMMENT 0x7F`.
- **Properties** (`property_id`): the stack/text/styling/semantic catalog
  (`SPACING`…`PADDING_LEFT`, `BORDER_*`, `FONT_*`, `COLOR`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`,
  `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`, `Z_INDEX`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ROLE`/`STATE`,
  `ENABLED`, `SELECTED`, `EVENT_LISTENERS`, `VALUE`/`MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE`,
  `LABEL`/`PROMPT`, and the draft `SHAPE_KIND`, `STEP_VALUE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`,
  `IS_SECURE`, `PROGRESS`, `IS_INDETERMINATE`, `SELECTION`, `COLOR_VALUE`,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `PICKER_STYLE`, `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`,
  `IMAGE_SOURCE`).
- **Commands**: `TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move (append = `u32::MAX`);
  `STYLE` `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`/`SET_TEXT`/`SET_DATE`; `META`
  `RESET`/`ENVIRONMENT`.
- **EVENT commands (constants)**: `POINTER_DOWN/MOVE/UP`, `KEY_DOWN/UP`,
  `VALUE_CHANGED`, `TEXT_CHANGED`, plus the draft `FOCUS_CHANGED`,
  `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`.
- **Listener bits**: 0–9 (`POINTER_*`, `KEY_*`, `FOCUS`, `EDITING`, `SUBMIT`,
  `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`).
- **Typed `Event` enum**: pointer/key/value/text events (commands 0x01–0x07).
- **Shared linear memory**: 80-byte header, guest→host ring, host→guest event
  ring, guest arena, host→guest **event arena** (two-way string section — a
  host `send_event(TextChanged)` round-trips text over the shared ring).
- **Conformance vectors** (`conformance.rs`): TREE/STYLE/META/EVENT golden
  bytes; `cargo test` enforces them.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Draft commands 0x08–0x0D and `STYLE::SET_DATE` are **constants only** — no
  typed `Event` variants, no `Guest::set_date` helper (renderers decode the raw
  opcode fields themselves).
- `ENVIRONMENT` (`META`) is a constant only (no viewport plumbing).

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-core` — conformance vectors, opcode round-trips,
arena, ring, event-ring (incl. shared-ring `TEXT_CHANGED` round-trip and
`META::RESET` event-arena recycle), randomized tests.

# pathland-engine — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The retained-tree **emitter**: the application's canonical UI tree and the
diff-based reactive emission into `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Retained tree** (`node.rs`): `Node` (id, component, children, properties,
  text/property signal bindings, app-side gestures).
- **Components** (`Component` enum): `VStack`, `HStack`, `Text`, `Button`,
  `Spacer` — mapped to `component_type` ids via `component_type_id`.
- **Diff emitter** (`engine.rs`): create/delete/insert/move deltas,
  property/text deltas, steady-state zero emission.
- **Reactive signals** (`signal.rs`): writable signals bound to node
  text/properties; `set_signal` re-emits only the bound nodes
  (`SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`).
- **Gestures**: `Tap` (app-side callback, never serialized).
- **`assign_ids`** (pre-order stable ids).

## Not implemented / gaps

- Only the five components above exist in `Component`; the full spec surface
  (Image, Color, Shape, Toggle, Slider, TextField, containers, …) has no
  engine-side component yet.
- Only `Tap` gesture; no computed-signal effects in the engine (Java has them).

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-engine` — emitter deltas, signals, `component_type_id`.

# pathland-core-transport — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The **transport** layer: the shared-memory ring owner and the network batch
codec (both directions). Protocol contract: `spec/OPCODE.md` (Transport).

## Implemented

- **`RingTransport`**: zero-copy SPSC shared-memory transport over the
  `pathland-core` linear memory — `next_frame` (guest→host frames as
  `OpcodeBatch`) and `send_input`/`drain_events` (host→guest raw inputs,
  including shared-ring `TEXT_CHANGED` text via the host event arena).
- **Network batch codec** (`batch.rs`, `net.rs`): `encode_batch`/`decode_batch`
  for guest→host frames and `encode_events`/`decode_events` for host→guest
  event batches (`HOST_TO_GUEST` direction flag, `TEXT_CHANGED` text in the
  batch string section). Both directions are fully wired at the codec level.
- **Batching policy** (`batching.rs`): time/size flush thresholds with arena
  delta tracking.
- **Conformance vectors 13/14** (`conformance.rs`): golden network-batch bytes.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No out-of-the-box duplex *server transport* (WebSocket/session plumbing) in
  this crate — the codecs exist; the Java demos (Quarkus/Spring) wire the
  browser↔server duplex.

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-core-transport` — ring round-trips (incl. zero-copy),
batch encode/decode both directions, batching policy, conformance vectors.

# pathland-render-gtk — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The **GTK4 renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto native GTK widgets
(shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Components → widgets** (`widget_kind`/`build_widget`):
  - `VSTACK`/`HSTACK` → `GtkBox` (with `SPACING`/`ALIGNMENT`/`PADDING`),
  - `TEXT` → `GtkLabel` (text + `FONT_SIZE`/`COLOR` via Pango),
  - `BUTTON` → `GtkButton` (label),
  - `GRID` → `GtkGrid` (row-major cells from child index + `WIDTH` column count),
  - `SCROLLVIEW` → `GtkScrolledWindow` (single child),
  - `ZSTACK` → `GtkOverlay`,
  - `SPACER` → expanding box,
  - `IMAGE` → `GtkPicture` (`IMAGE_SOURCE` from the frame string section).
  Unknown components → blank `GtkLabel`.
- **Container reconciliation** generalized to all containers (diff-guarded).
- **Host reader** (`host.rs`): `RenderTree` + resolved `STRING` properties.
- **Events**: pointer `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` via
  `GestureClick`/`EventControllerMotion`, driven by `desired_listeners`
  (buttons by default + `EVENT_LISTENERS`).

- **Tier 2 (pending)**: `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/`TEXT_FIELD`/`TEXT_EDITOR` native
  tokens, composite-override mode (controls with children), `VALUE_CHANGED` /
  `TEXT_CHANGED` emission, `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` event-gating.

`cargo test -p pathland-render-gtk` — layout mapping, container kinds,
`widget_kind`, string resolution (headless; widget construction is exercised

Here's the audit of the Rust crates against the spec.

## Synced (done in the earlier passes)

- **Semantic/control + binding properties** — `STEP_VALUE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `IS_SECURE`, `PROGRESS`, `IS_INDETERMINATE`, `SELECTION`, `COLOR_VALUE`, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `PICKER_STYLE`, `SHAPE_KIND`, `IMAGE_SOURCE`, `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE` (+ `value_type_for`).
- **EVENT commands 0x01–0x0D and listener bits 0–9** (constants), two-way event arena, both transport directions.

## Not in sync — gaps

**1. `constants.rs` is missing ~30 modifier-catalog properties** (allocated in `MODIFIERS.md`, absent from Rust):
- Layout: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN_WIDTH`…`MAX_HEIGHT` (0x0012–0x0017), `FIXED_SIZE_H/V`, `LAYOUT_PRIORITY`, `ASPECT_RATIO`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`.
- Text: `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `FONT_WIDTH`, `KERNING`, `TRACKING`, `BASELINE_OFFSET`, `LINE_SPACING`, `TEXT_CASE`, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`.
- Effects: `SHADOW_COLOR/RADIUS/X/Y`, `BLUR_RADIUS`, `SATURATION`, `CONTRAST`, `BRIGHTNESS`, `GRAYSCALE`, `HUE_ROTATION`, `COLOR_MULTIPLY`, `COLOR_INVERT`.
- Transform/interaction: `ROTATION_DEGREES`, `SCALE`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`.

**2. `value_type_for` diverges from MODIFIERS' canonical mapping** for existing props: `VISIBLE`, `ENABLED`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` should be `U8` (impl returns `F32`); the new U8/COLOR props (`UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`, `COLOR_INVERT`, `COLOR_MULTIPLY`, `SHADOW_COLOR`, …) will need mapping once added.

**3. Draft commands are constants-only** — `Event` covers 0x01–0x07; `FOCUS_CHANGED`/`EDITING_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`/`SCROLL`/`WHEEL`/`DATE_CHANGED` (0x08–0x0D) and `STYLE::SET_DATE` have no typed `Event` variants, no `Guest::set_date` helper (renderers decode raw opcode fields).

**4. `pathland-render-gtk` (the biggest coverage gap)** — Tier 2 not done:
- Components render as **blank labels**: `TOGGLE`, `SLIDER`, `TEXT_FIELD`, `TEXT_EDITOR`, `COLOR`, `SHAPE`, `DIVIDER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`, `GAUGE`, `LAZY_*`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER`, `PICKER`, `MENU`, `COLOR_PICKER`.
- Properties not applied: `VISIBLE`, `OPACITY`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_*`, `FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_FAMILY`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `Z_INDEX`.
- **No `VALUE_CHANGED`/`TEXT_CHANGED` emission** and **no `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` event-gating** (the spec's event-guard rule).
- **Composite Override Mode** (controls with children) not implemented.

**5. `pathland-view-native`** — `property_value_type` returns `F32` for STRING-valued props (`LABEL`, `PROMPT`, `FONT_FAMILY`, `IMAGE_SOURCE`); only 5 components in the flat world.

**6. Coverage gaps (ID-correct, but surface missing):** `pathland-view` (Rust DSL: 5 views + 8 modifiers), `pathland-engine` (`Component` = 5), `pathland-core-capi` (raw ring only). Also the spec's **enum value codes** (e.g. `TOGGLE_STYLE=Switch=0`) have no Rust constants — values are used inline.

- **Tier C (DSL/C-ABI breadth):** extend `pathland-view`/`pathland-engine`/`pathland-view-native` with more components + STRING-property plumbing.

pub fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
    match prop {
        property_id::COLOR
        | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR
        | property_id::BORDER_COLOR
        | property_id::COLOR_VALUE
        | property_id::COLOR_MULTIPLY
        | property_id::SHADOW_COLOR => value_type::COLOR,
        property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS | property_id::BORDER_EDGES => value_type::U32,
        property_id::SELECTED
        | property_id::IS_SECURE
        | property_id::IS_INDETERMINATE
        | property_id::VISIBLE
        | property_id::ENABLED
        | property_id::CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS
        | property_id::UNDERLINE
        | property_id::STRIKETHROUGH
        | property_id::COLOR_INVERT
        | property_id::ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING
        | property_id::FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL
        | property_id::FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL => value_type::U8,
        property_id::LABEL | property_id::PROMPT | property_id::FONT_FAMILY | property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE => {
            value_type::STRING
        }
        property_id::LINE_LIMIT
        | property_id::SELECTION
        | property_id::ACTION_ID
        | property_id::BINDING_ID => value_type::U32,
        _ => value_type::F32,
    }
}

# pathland-render-gtk — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The **GTK4 renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto native GTK widgets
(shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Components → widgets** (`widget_kind`/`build_widget`):
  - `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` → `GtkBox` (spacing/alignment/
    padding/content-margins),
  - `TEXT` → `GtkLabel` (text, `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`COLOR` via Pango),
  - `BUTTON` → `GtkButton` (label; composite body when it has children),
  - `GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` → `GtkGrid` (row-major cells from child
    index + `WIDTH` column count),
  - `SCROLLVIEW` → `GtkScrolledWindow` (single child),
  - `ZSTACK` → `GtkOverlay`,
  - `SPACER` → expanding box, `IMAGE` → `GtkPicture` (`IMAGE_SOURCE`),
  - `TOGGLE` → `GtkSwitch`/`GtkCheckButton`/`GtkToggleButton` by `TOGGLE_STYLE`
    (`SELECTED` ↔ active),
  - `SLIDER` → `GtkScale` (`VALUE`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`STEP`),
  - `TEXT_FIELD` → `GtkEntry` (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`IS_SECURE`),
  - `TEXT_EDITOR` → `GtkTextView` (multi-line),
  - `COLOR` → `GtkDrawingArea` (solid fill), `SHAPE` → `GtkDrawingArea`
    (`SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER` → `GtkSeparator`,
  - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `GtkProgressBar`/`GtkSpinner`,
  - `GAUGE` → `GtkLevelBar`, `STEPPER` → `GtkSpinButton`,
  - `DATE_PICKER` → `GtkCalendar`, `PICKER` → `GtkDropDown` (option children +
    `SELECTION`), `MENU` → `GtkMenuButton`, `COLOR_PICKER` → `GtkColorButton`.
  Unknown components → blank `GtkLabel`.
- **Container + composite reconciliation** (diff-guarded): stacks/grid/scroll/
  overlay children, and **Composite Override Mode** for `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`MENU`
  with children (custom body wrapped in the native button shell).
- **Style properties**: `VISIBLE`, `OPACITY`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`,
  `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `PADDING` + per-edge, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`/
  `COLOR`/`RADIUS`, `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_WEIGHT` (CSS provider), `COLOR`,
  `FONT_SIZE`.
- **Events**: pointer `POINTER_DOWN`/`MOVE`/`UP` via `GestureClick`/
  `EventControllerMotion` (`EVENT_LISTENERS`-driven), plus **value/text events**
  (`VALUE_CHANGED` from toggle/slider/picker, `TEXT_CHANGED` from text field)
  **gated by `BINDING_ID`** (transport-aware event guards), sent through the
  two-way event arena.

## Not implemented / gaps

- `SHAPE` `Path`/rounded rendering is an approximation (rectangle/circle fill).
- `MENU` renders a menu button without a popover item list.
- No `ACTION_ID`-only gating (events require `BINDING_ID`).
- Composite bodies attach to button-like controls only; other controls ignore
  children.
- `LAZY_*` renders eagerly (no GTK windowing).

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-render-gtk` — layout mapping, `widget_kind` (full
component map), container/composite kinds, string resolution, value type
mapping (headless; widget construction is exercised without a display).

# pathland-engine — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The retained-tree **emitter**: the application's canonical UI tree and the
diff-based reactive emission into `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Retained tree** (`node.rs`): `Node` (id, component, children, properties,
  text/property signal bindings, app-side gestures).
- **Components** (`Component` enum): the full spec set — `VStack`, `HStack`,
  `ZStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Divider`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextField`, `TextEditor`,
  `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker` — all mapped to
  `component_type` ids via `component_type_id`.
- **Diff emitter** (`engine.rs`): create/delete/insert/move deltas,
  property/text deltas, steady-state zero emission.
- **Reactive signals** (`signal.rs`): writable signals bound to node
  text/properties; `set_signal` re-emits only the bound nodes
  (`SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`).
- **Gestures**: `Tap` (app-side callback, never serialized).
- **`assign_ids`** (pre-order stable ids).

## Not implemented / gaps

- Only `Tap` gesture; no computed-signal effects in the engine (Java has them).
- No `strings` map on `Node` for STRING-valued properties (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/
  `FONT_FAMILY`/`IMAGE_SOURCE`) — the DSL cannot yet emit them.

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-engine` — emitter deltas, signals, `component_type_id`.

All three tiers complete, each committed separately, workspace green (190 tests) throughout.

- **`7976701` — Tier A (protocol surface):** added the ~30 missing modifier properties to `constants.rs`, aligned `value_type_for` (U8/COLOR/STRING/U32), added typed `Event` variants for drafts 0x08–0x0D (`FocusChanged`…`DateChanged`), `Guest::set_date`, and network round-trip tests.
- **`c247f0a` — Tier B (render-gtk):** full spec coverage — native-token controls (Toggle/Slider/TextField/TextEditor), draft components (Color/Shape/Divider/ProgressView/Gauge/Stepper/DatePicker/Picker/Menu/ColorPicker), composite override mode, `VALUE_CHANGED`/`TEXT_CHANGED` emission gated by `BINDING_ID`, and style properties (visibility/opacity/size/background/border/fonts).
- **`cb40abf` — Tier C (DSL/engine/C-ABI):** the `Component` enum + DSL authoring surface for all components + a broader modifier set, and `view-native` mapping the full component set with the canonical value-type mapping.

One known gap (documented in the status files, not a spec mismatch): STRING-valued properties (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY`/`IMAGE_SOURCE`) need a `strings` map on the engine `Node` + arena-string emission before the Rust DSL can author them — flagged as the next piece if you want it.

### Visual Element: `Color`

`Color` in Pathland must mirror SwiftUI's dual identity as both a **View** and a **ShapeStyle / Parameter**:

1. **`Color` as a Standalone View:**
   - `Color` implements the `View` interface. 
   - When instantiated directly inside a layout hierarchy (e.g., `Color("#FF0000")`), it acts as a layout element.
   - **Sizing Behavior:** It is layout-greedy—it expands to occupy all available space offered by its parent container unless explicitly constrained by frame/size modifiers.

2. **No Direct `.color()` Modifier:**
   - There is NO top-level `color` modifier. 
   - Instead, `Color` values are passed as *arguments* into modifiers that accept color or style types (e.g., `.foregroundStyle(Color)`, `.background(Color)`, `.border(Color)`).

Research complete. This is indeed **app-layer + renderer**, not protocol — the protocol already models both identities (`COLOR` component 0x03 as a view, `COLOR`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/`BORDER_COLOR` as value types), and `spec/MODIFIERS.md` already names the modifier `.foregroundColor(_:)`. Here's the current gap and the plan.

## Current state (verified)

| Layer | `Color` dual identity | `.color()` modifier | `COLOR` view sizing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rust DSL** | ✗ — `Color` is only a *modifier* struct; the component is `ColorView` | ✗ has `.color(u32)` (user says no) | — |
| **Java DSL** | ✓ — `record Color(int argb) implements View` already | ✗ has `.color(Color)` | — |
| **render-html** | — | — | ✗ not greedy (`<div background-color>` collapses to 0 in a flex stack) |
| **render-gtk** | — | — | ✓ greedy (`GtkDrawingArea` hexpand/vexpand) |

Two bonus findings: Java `Color.render()` emits `IMAGE` + `BACKGROUND_COLOR` (spec says the `COLOR` component 0x03 + `COLOR` property — but that change collides with Java's legacy `TEXT=0x0003`, so it must wait for the Java ID-sync); and the Rust DSL's `.color()`/`.background(u32)`/`.border(u32, w)` take raw `u32` instead of a `Color` value.

## Plan

### A. Rust DSL (`pathland-view`)
1. Make `Color(pub u32)` the **dual-identity type** (Copy value *and* `impl View` building `Component::Color` with `COLOR`); delete `ColorView` (name frees up).
2. **Remove** the `Color` modifier struct and `.color(u32)` sugar — no top-level `.color()`.
3. Modifiers accept `Color` values: `.foreground_color(Color)` (new), `.background(Color)`, `.border(Color, width)`.
4. Update the DSL tests + `pathland-render-gtk-demo` (`text(...).color(0xFF...)` → `.foreground_color(Color(...))`).

### B. Java DSL (`pathland-view`)
1. Rename `.color(Color)` → `.foregroundColor(Color)` (+ the reactive overload); update `BorderedButtonStyle`/callers.
2. `Color` keeps its dual identity (already correct).
3. **Defer** `Color.render()` → `Components.COLOR` to the Java ID-sync pass (0x03 collides with legacy `TEXT`).

### C. Renderers (`COLOR` view layout-greedy)
- render-html: give the `COLOR` node greedy CSS (`flex:1;align-self:stretch`), with explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (via `style_css`) still constraining.
- render-gtk: already greedy; verify size hints hold.

### D. Docs

`Color` in Pathland strictly mirrors SwiftUI: it is **NEVER a modifier**. It exists solely as a **View** and as a **Data Type**.

1. **`Color` as a View Node (Layout Tree):**
   - `Color` conforms to the View specification.
   - When instantiated inside a layout stack or container (e.g., `Color("#FF0000")`), it acts as a standalone visual element.
   - **Sizing Rule:** It is layout-greedy—it automatically expands to fill all available space offered by its parent container unless explicitly constrained (e.g., via a `.frame()` modifier).

2. **`Color` as a Data Type (Modifier Argument):**
   - `Color` is a value passed *into* modifiers that accept color or style types.
   - **Allowed Contexts:** `.foregroundStyle(Color)`, `.background(Color)`, `.border(Color)`, `.tint(Color)`.
   - **Conformity:** `Color` conforms to `ShapeStyle`, allowing it to be used anywhere a visual fill/style is expected.

3. **Parser & Generator Rules:**
   - **Strict Constraint:** Do NOT allow or generate a `.color()` modifier. 
   - **Deprecation Constraint:** Do NOT allow or generate `.foregroundColor()`. All foreground styling must use `.foregroundStyle()`.
   - **Node vs. Argument:** Treat `Color` as a **View** when present as a structural node in the UI hierarchy. Treat `Color` as a **Value** when inside a modifier's parameter list.

### Color — `COLOR` 0x03

`Color` mirrors SwiftUI's **dual identity**: it is both a **View** and a
**Data Type** — and it is **never a modifier**.

- **As a View**: a solid-color visual element. It is **layout-greedy** —
  it expands to fill all available space offered by its parent container
  unless explicitly constrained (e.g. by a `.frame`/size modifier). Its color
  is the `COLOR` property (0x100A, packed `0xAARRGGBB`, sRGB).
- **As a Data Type**: a `Color` value is passed *into* style-taking modifiers
  (`.foregroundStyle(_:)`, `.background(_:)`, `.border(_:)`, `.tint(_:)`), and
  can be used anywhere a visual fill/style is expected.
- **Constraint**: there is **no** `.color()` modifier, and `.foregroundColor(_:)`
  is deprecated — all foreground styling uses `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
- **Parser/generator rule**: treat `Color` as a **View** when it is a structural
  node in the UI tree; treat it as a **Value** when it appears in a modifier's
  parameter list.
- **Events**: none by default.
- **Renderer mapping**: GTK `GtkDrawingArea`/colored box (expands); HTML `<div>`
  with `background-color` (`flex:1;align-self:stretch` — greedy); ngui
  `ui-color`. The renderer paints the pixel fill.
- **Note**: `Color` is also a **property value** (`COLOR`,
  `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_COLOR`, `TINT`) — the node exists for when a
  color is a first-class view (backgrounds, fills, spacers).

**Rust DSL**: `Color(pub u32)` implements `View` (builds `Component::Color`, layout-greedy) *and* serves as a value; `ColorView` deleted; the `.color()` modifier and `Color` modifier struct removed. **Java DSL**: `.color(Color)` → `.foregroundStyle(Color)` (+ reactive); added `.tint(Color)`; updated `BorderedButtonStyle`, `CounterView`, `EmitterTest`.

**Renderer**: render-html's `COLOR` view is now layout-greedy (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch`) — render-gtk already was.

## Objective
- Implement the strict `Color` dual-identity design across the Pathland stack: `Color` is **never a modifier** — only a **View** (layout-greedy node) and a **Data Type** (argument to `.foregroundStyle`/`.background`/`.border`/`.tint`).
- Enforce: no `.color()` modifier anywhere; no `.foregroundColor()`; foreground styling must use `.foregroundStyle()` (Rust snake_case `.foreground_style`); add a draft `TINT` property; make the `COLOR` view layout-greedy in renderers.

## Important Details
- User decisions: (1) Rust method name = snake_case `.foreground_style(Color)`; (2) add `TINT` draft property; (3) MODIFIERS.md rename + Java `.color()` → `.foregroundStyle()` OK.
- Rust DSL uses snake_case (`.font_size`, `.corner_radius`); Java uses camelCase (`.foregroundStyle`).

1: # Pathland Core Modifiers
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core modifiers** the Pathland protocol must
12: support. In the protocol these are the **`STYLE` properties**: the constraint
13: properties and visual decorations carried by `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY`. The set
14: mirrors SwiftUI's core modifiers so that any SwiftUI-shaped UI can be expressed.
15: 
16: Like SwiftUI, modifiers in Pathland are **decoupled from views**: any modifier
17: applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a `VStack` alike). A
18: modifier that a particular renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** —
19: the property is still emitted; the renderer skips it. Application code composes
20: custom modifiers from these core ones.
21: 
22: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
23: - Wire format and value types: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
24: - Events: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)
25: 
26: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
27: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
28: > defines the protocol contract only.
29: 
30: ### Emission rules
31: 
32: Each modifier emits **one or more** `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY` opcodes — one per
33: underlying property. There is no compound-modifier opcode. Compound SwiftUI
34: modifiers (`.frame(width:height:alignment:)`, `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)`,
35: `.border(_:width:)`) are expanded into several `SET_PROPERTY` opcodes, exactly
36: as the existing `.frame` modifier already does (`WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` +
37: `ALIGNMENT`).
38: 
39: `SET_PROPERTY` packing (see OPCODE.md):
40: 
41: ```
42: A = nodeId
43: B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
44: C = value (f32 bit pattern / u32 / u8 / color / arenaRef)
45: ```
46: 
47: Only **changed** properties emit: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes
48: (diff-based reactive emission). `STRING`-valued properties carry their text in
49: the frame's string section; `C` holds the arena offset.
50: 
51: ### Value types (from `value_type`, u8)
52: 
53: | Value Type | Value | `C` encoding |
54: |------------|-------|--------------|
55: | `U8` | 0x01 | low byte of C |
56: | `U32` | 0x02 | u32 |
57: | `I32` | 0x03 | i32 |
58: | `F32` | 0x04 | f32 bit pattern |
59: | `STRING` | 0x05 | arenaRef (utf8) |
60: | `ENUM` | 0x06 | low byte of C |
61: | `COLOR` | 0x07 | packed `0xAARRGGBB` (sRGB) |
62: | `DESIGN_TOKEN` | 0x08 | arenaRef (token path) |
63: 
64: Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1.0` = `FILL` (expand to available), `-2.0` =
65: `HUG_CONTENT` (native intrinsic size).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 1. Layout
70: 
71: Arrangement and sizing. These map to the native renderer's layout knobs.
72: 
73: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
74: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
75: | `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` | `WIDTH` 0x100B, `HEIGHT` 0x100C, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002 | F32, F32, ENUM | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided axis/alignment |
76: | `.frame(minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:minHeight:idealHeight:maxHeight:)` | `MIN_WIDTH` 0x0012, `IDEAL_WIDTH` 0x0013, `MAX_WIDTH` 0x0014, `MIN_HEIGHT` 0x0015, `IDEAL_HEIGHT` 0x0016, `MAX_HEIGHT` 0x0017 | F32 | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided bound |
77: | `.padding(_:)`, `.padding(edges:)`, `.padding(_:edges:)` | `PADDING` 0x1011, `PADDING_TOP` 0x1012, `PADDING_RIGHT` 0x1013, `PADDING_BOTTOM` 0x1014, `PADDING_LEFT` 0x1015 | F32 | uniform → one; per-edge → per-edge |
78: | `.offset(x:y:)` | `OFFSET_X` 0x000E, `OFFSET_Y` 0x000F | F32 | two |
79: | `.position(x:y:)` | `POSITION_X` 0x0010, `POSITION_Y` 0x0011 | F32 | two |
80: | `.fixedSize()` / `.fixedSize(horizontal:vertical:)` | `FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL` 0x0018, `FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL` 0x0019 | U8 (0/1) | two (or one when axis-limited) |
81: | `.layoutPriority(_:)` | `LAYOUT_PRIORITY` 0x001A | F32 | one |
82: | `.zIndex(_:)` | `Z_INDEX` 0x100F | F32 | one |
83: | `.aspectRatio(_:contentMode:)` | `ASPECT_RATIO` 0x001B, `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | F32, ENUM | two |
84: | `.scaledToFit()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fit`=0) | one |
85: | `.scaledToFill()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fill`=1) | one |
86: | `.minimumScaleFactor(_:)` | `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR` 0x001D | F32 | one |
87: | `.spacing(_:)` (stacks) | `SPACING` 0x0001 | F32 | one |
88: | `Spacer` | — (implied by component) | — | none |
89: 
90: ### Semantics
91: 
92: - **`WIDTH` / `HEIGHT`**: size hints; the renderer maps them to its size
93:   request / `width`/`height` style. `FILL` (-1.0) expands to available space;
94:   `HUG_CONTENT` (-2.0) sizes to intrinsic content. Absence of a property leaves
95:   that axis to the native default.
96: - **`frame(min/ideal/max)`**: each provided bound emits its own property.
97:   Renderers map them to min/max/ideal size (GTK `set_size_request`, CSS
98:   `min-width`/`max-width`/`width`).
99: - **`PADDING` vs per-edge**: `PADDING` is uniform and shorthand; a per-edge
100:   modifier overwrites the edge only. Per-edge wins over uniform when both are
101:   present.
102: - **`ALIGNMENT` enum**: `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3.
103: - **`CONTENT_MODE` enum**: `Fit`=0 (aspect-fit within the bounds),
104:   `Fill`=1 (aspect-fill, cropped).
105: - **`OFFSET`** moves the element **after** layout without affecting layout
106:   (post-layout translation; GTK margins/translation, CSS `transform:
107:   translate`).
108: - **`POSITION`** is absolute placement within the parent (CSS `position:
109:   absolute; left/top`); the renderer resolves the anchor.
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## 2. Text Formatting
114: 
115: Apply to `Text`, `Label`, `Button` labels, and text-bearing controls. Renderers
116: map them to their native text attributes.
117: 
118: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
119: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
120: | `.font(.system(size:))` | `FONT_SIZE` 0x1007 | F32 | one |
121: | `.fontWeight(_:)` | `FONT_WEIGHT` 0x1008 | F32 (100–900) | one |
122: | `.font(.custom(name:size:))` | `FONT_FAMILY` 0x1009 | STRING | one (arenaRef) |
123: | `.italic()` / `.fontStyle(_:)` | `FONT_STYLE` 0x1017 | ENUM (`Normal`=0, `Italic`=1) | one |
124: | `.fontDesign(_:)` | `FONT_DESIGN` 0x1018 | ENUM (`Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3) | one |
125: | `.fontWidth(_:)` | `FONT_WIDTH` 0x1019 | F32 (0.5–1.5, 1.0 default) | one |
126: | `.kerning(_:)` | `KERNING` 0x101A | F32 | one |
127: | `.tracking(_:)` | `TRACKING` 0x101B | F32 | one |
128: | `.baselineOffset(_:)` | `BASELINE_OFFSET` 0x101C | F32 | one |
129: | `.lineSpacing(_:)` | `LINE_SPACING` 0x101D | F32 | one |
130: | `.lineLimit(_:)` | `LINE_LIMIT` 0x000B | U32 | one |
131: | `.multilineTextAlignment(_:)` | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` 0x000C | ENUM (`Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2) | one |
132: | `.truncationMode(_:)` | `TRUNCATION_MODE` 0x000D | ENUM (`Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2) | one |
133: | `.textCase(_:)` | `TEXT_CASE` 0x101E | ENUM (`None`=0, `Uppercase`=1, `Lowercase`=2) | one |
134: | `.underline()` | `UNDERLINE` 0x101F | U8 (0/1) | one |
135: | `.strikethrough()` | `STRIKETHROUGH` 0x1020 | U8 (0/1) | one |
136: | `.foregroundStyle(_:)` | `COLOR` 0x100A | COLOR | one |
137: | `.tint(_:)` | `TINT` 0x1030 | COLOR | one |
138: 
139: > **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` exists only as a **View** (a
140: > layout-greedy solid-color fill) and as a **Data Type** passed into
141: > style-taking modifiers (`.foregroundStyle(_:)`, `.background(_:)`,
142: > `.border(_:)`, `.tint(_:)`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier and
143: > `.foregroundColor(_:)` is deprecated — all foreground styling uses
144: > `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
145: 
146: \* `FONT_FAMILY` is a `STRING` property (arenaRef), matching SwiftUI, which
147: passes font families as string names (`.font(.custom("Georgia", size:))`).
148: 
149: ### Semantics
150: 
151: - **`FONT_WEIGHT`** is a numeric F32 on the 100–900 scale (`regular`≈400,
152:   `bold`≈700). Renderers map it to the nearest native weight.
153: - **`KERNING` vs `TRACKING`**: kerning adjusts per-glyph spacing at a
154:   point/em scale; tracking adds uniform letter spacing. Both are F32 points.
155: - **`LINE_LIMIT`** of 0 means unlimited.
156: - **`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`** differs from stack `ALIGNMENT`: it aligns the text block
157:   inside its own bounds (CSS `text-align`), not children of a stack.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 3. Appearance & Effects
162: 
163: Visual decoration. These never change layout; they decorate the element.
164: 
165: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
166: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
167: | `.background(_:)` | `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001 | COLOR | one |
168: | `.border(_:width:)` | `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `BORDER_WIDTH` 0x1003 | COLOR, F32 | two |
169: | `.border(_:width:edges:)` | `BORDER_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`, `BORDER_EDGES` 0x1016 | COLOR, F32, U32 (bitmask) | three |
170: | `.cornerRadius(_:)` | `BORDER_RADIUS` 0x1005 | F32 | one |
171: | `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)` | `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `SHADOW_RADIUS` 0x1022, `SHADOW_X` 0x1023, `SHADOW_Y` 0x1024 | COLOR, F32, F32, F32 | four |
172: | `.opacity(_:)` | `OPACITY` 0x100D | F32 (0–1) | one |
173: | `.blur(radius:)` | `BLUR_RADIUS` 0x1025 | F32 | one |
174: | `.saturation(_:)` | `SATURATION` 0x1026 | F32 (0–1) | one |
175: | `.contrast(_:)` | `CONTRAST` 0x1027 | F32 (0–1) | one |
176: | `.brightness(_:)` | `BRIGHTNESS` 0x1028 | F32 (−1–1) | one |
177: | `.grayscale(_:)` | `GRAYSCALE` 0x1029 | F32 (0–1) | one |
178: | `.hueRotation(_:)` | `HUE_ROTATION` 0x102A | F32 (degrees) | one |
179: | `.colorMultiply(_:)` | `COLOR_MULTIPLY` 0x102B | COLOR | one |
180: | `.colorInvert()` | `COLOR_INVERT` 0x102C | U8 (0/1) | one |
181: | `.clipped()` / `.clipsToBounds` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 | U8 (0/1) | one |
182: | `.clipShape(_:)` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 + `SHAPE_KIND` 0x0006 | U8 + ENUM | two (see note) |
183: 
184: ### Semantics
185: 
186: - **`BORDER_EDGES`** is a u32 bitmask: `TOP`=1, `LEADING`=2, `BOTTOM`=4,
187:   `TRAILING`=8 (direction-aware; see OPCODE.md). When `.border` has no `edges:`
188:   argument the renderer treats the mask as `ALL` (0xF).
189: - **`BORDER_RADIUS`** rounds all corners; a future per-corner variant would add
190:   `TOP_LEFT_*`/… properties.
191: - **`SHADOW`** is a compound: exactly four `SET_PROPERTY` opcodes. Missing
192:   fields default: color = token `color.shadow`, radius = 0, x = 0, y = 0.
193: - **`clipShape`**: `SHAPE_KIND` (0x0006, defined in
194:   [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md#5-shapes--paints)) selects the clip geometry;
195:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` (1) turns clipping on. A bare `.clipped()` is
196:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` with no shape.
197: - **Color effects** (`SATURATION`, `CONTRAST`, …) are renderer-owned filters;
198:   the renderer maps them to native filter APIs (CSS `filter`, GTK
199:   `GtkSnapshot` effects). They compose in the order applied.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 4. Transform
204: 
205: Geometric transforms applied after layout.
206: 
207: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
208: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
209: | `.rotationEffect(_:anchor:)` | `ROTATION_DEGREES` 0x102D | F32 (degrees, counter-clockwise) | one (anchor is renderer-token-owned) |
210: | `.scaleEffect(_:anchor:)` | `SCALE` 0x102E | F32 (uniform scale) | one (anchor is renderer-token-owned) |
211: 
212: ### Semantics
213: 
214: - Transforms do **not** affect layout; the renderer applies them as a
215:   post-layout visual transform (CSS `transform`, GTK `gtk_widget_allocate`
216:   transform).
217: - **Anchor** is renderer-token-owned (`.center` default); the protocol does not
218:   transmit anchors — the renderer owns presentation (see OPCODE.md design
219:   tokens). Non-uniform scale / 3D rotation are future extensions.
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## 5. Interaction & State
224: 
225: Semantic properties controlling whether and how an element responds to input,
226: plus accessibility. These are the "semantic" (`0x2000`) properties.
227: 
228: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property | Type | Emission |
229: | ------------------ | ------------------- | ------ | ---------- |
230: | `.hidden()` | `VISIBLE` 0x100E | U8 (0 = hidden) | one |
231: | `.disabled(_:)` | `ENABLED` 0x2003 | U8 (1 = enabled) | one |
232: | `.allowsHitTesting(_:)` | `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING` 0x102F | U8 (0/1) | one |
233: | `.controlSize(_:)` | `CONTROL_SIZE` 0x200C | ENUM (`Small`=0, `Regular`=1, `Large`=2) | one |
234: | `.focusable(_:)` | — (via `FOCUS` listener) | — | none (declares `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit 5) |
235: | `.accessibilityLabel(_:)` | `LABEL` 0x200A | STRING | one (arenaRef) |
236: | `.accessibilityRole(_:)` | `ROLE` 0x2001 | ENUM | one |
237: | `.accessibilityState(_:)` | `STATE` 0x2002 | ENUM | one |
238: 
239: ### Semantics
240: 
241: - **`VISIBLE`**: 0 hides the element entirely (removed from layout and hit
242:   testing by the renderer); 1 shows it. Diff-based emission means toggling
243:   visibility emits a single `SET_PROPERTY`.
244: - **`ENABLED`** is the inverse of SwiftUI `.disabled()`: 1 = interactive, 0 =
245:   disabled. Disabled controls do not emit events.
246: - **`.focusable`** has no property: the app requests focus events via the
247:   `FOCUS` listener bit (`EVENT_LISTENERS`, bit 5) and observes
248:   `EVENT::FOCUS_CHANGED` — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md).
249: - **`ROLE`/`STATE`** are accessibility enums; their enumerated values are
250:   defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#semantic-properties), not here. `STATE` is
251:   a semantic accessibility property — it never describes visual styling.
252: - **`LABEL`** is a `STRING` property (the accessibility label), distinct from a
253:   `TEXT_FIELD`'s caption label.
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## Property ID Catalog
258: 
259: ### Allocated property IDs
260: 
261: | Range | Group |
262: | ------- | ------- |
263: | `0x0001`–`0x0005` | Stack constraint (SPACING, ALIGNMENT, …, CONTENT_MARGINS) |
264: | `0x0006` | `SHAPE_KIND` (ENUM; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
265: | `0x000A`–`0x000D` | Text (TEXT, LINE_LIMIT, TEXT_ALIGNMENT, TRUNCATION_MODE) |
266: | `0x000E`–`0x001D` | Layout properties (allocated: OFFSET, POSITION, frame bounds, FIXED_SIZE, LAYOUT_PRIORITY, ASPECT_RATIO/CONTENT_MODE, MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR) |
267: | `0x001E`–`0x00FF` | Future layout/format properties (unallocated) |
268: | `0x1001`–`0x1016` | Styling (BACKGROUND_COLOR, BORDER_*, FONT_SIZE/WEIGHT/FAMILY, COLOR, WIDTH, HEIGHT, OPACITY, VISIBLE, Z_INDEX, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS, PADDING_*, BORDER_EDGES) |
269: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (STRING; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
270: | `0x1017`–`0x102F` | Text-format properties (allocated: FONT_STYLE/DESIGN/WIDTH, KERNING, TRACKING, BASELINE_OFFSET, LINE_SPACING, TEXT_CASE, UNDERLINE, STRIKETHROUGH), effect properties (SHADOW_*, BLUR, SATURATION, CONTRAST, BRIGHTNESS, GRAYSCALE, HUE_ROTATION, COLOR_MULTIPLY, COLOR_INVERT), ROTATION_DEGREES, SCALE, ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING |
271: | `0x1030` | `TINT` (COLOR) | — |
272: | `0x1030`–`0x10FF` | Future styling properties (unallocated) |
273: | `0x2001`–`0x200B` | Semantic (ROLE, STATE, ENABLED, SELECTED, EVENT_LISTENERS, VALUE, MIN_VALUE, MAX_VALUE, LABEL, PROMPT) |
274: | `0x2009`, `0x200C`–`0x2014` | Control properties (allocated: STEP_VALUE, CONTROL_SIZE, IS_SECURE, PROGRESS, IS_INDETERMINATE, SELECTION, COLOR_VALUE, DATE_PICKER_MODE, PICKER_STYLE) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md controls. Note: a `DATE_PICKER`'s date is set via the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (0x04), not a property; **`0x2011` is unallocated/reserved** (its former `DATE_VALUE` draft was dropped) |
275: | `0x2016`–`0x2018` | Binding/action properties (allocated: `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md semantic controls |
276: | `0x2015`, `0x2019`–`0x20FF` | Future semantic properties (unallocated) |
277: 
278: ### Reserved ranges
279: 
280: | Range | Use |
281: |-------|-----|
282: | `0x0003`, `0x0004` | Reserved (formerly JUSTIFICATION, PADDING) — MUST NOT be reused |
283: | `0x0007`–`0x0009`, `0x000E`+ high | Draft/future layout |
284: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (allocated) |
285: 
286: A renderer MUST ignore unknown property ids and continue decoding.
287: 
288: ### Default value type resolution
289: 
290: The canonical value type per property (the protocol's authoritative mapping):
291: 
292: - `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_COLOR`, `COLOR_MULTIPLY`,
293:   `SHADOW_COLOR`, `COLOR_VALUE`, `TINT` → `COLOR`
294: - `EVENT_LISTENERS`, `BORDER_EDGES` → `U32`
295: - `SELECTED`, `VISIBLE`, `ENABLED`, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`,
296:   `COLOR_INVERT`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `IS_SECURE`,
297:   `IS_INDETERMINATE`, `FIXED_SIZE_*` → `U8`
298: - `LABEL`, `PROMPT`, `FONT_FAMILY`, `IMAGE_SOURCE` → `STRING`
299: - `LINE_LIMIT`, `SELECTION`, `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID` → `U32`
300: - `ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`,
301:   `FONT_DESIGN`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `SHAPE_KIND`,
302:   `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `PICKER_STYLE`, `TOGGLE_STYLE` → `F32` (numeric enum code;
303:   see the appendix and [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#value-types))
304: - everything else → `F32`
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## Appendix: Enumerated values
309: 
310: Single authoritative source for every enum-valued property in the protocol.
311: A renderer or emitter MUST use these exact numeric codes. The code is carried
312: in the property value as an **f32 bit pattern** (`value_type::F32`) — see the
313: [value-type
314: conventions](./OPCODE.md#value-types) and the [default value type
315: resolution](#default-value-type-resolution).
316: 
317: | Property | ID | Values |
318: |----------|----|--------|
319: | `ALIGNMENT` | 0x0002 | `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3 |
320: | `SHAPE_KIND` | 0x0006 | `Circle`=0, `Rectangle`=1, `RoundedRectangle`=2, `Capsule`=3, `Ellipse`=4, `Path`=5 |
321: | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` | 0x000C | `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2 |
322: | `TRUNCATION_MODE` | 0x000D | `Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2 |
323: | `CONTENT_MODE` | 0x001C | `Fit`=0, `Fill`=1 |
324: | `FONT_STYLE` | 0x1017 | `Normal`=0, `Italic`=1 |
325: | `FONT_DESIGN` | 0x1018 | `Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3 |
326: | `TEXT_CASE` | 0x101E | `None`=0, `Uppercase`=1, `Lowercase`=2 |
327: | `CONTROL_SIZE` | 0x200C | `Small`=0, `Regular`=1, `Large`=2 |
328: | `DATE_PICKER_MODE` | 0x2013 | `Date`=0, `Time`=1, `DateAndTime`=2 |
329: | `PICKER_STYLE` | 0x2014 | `Menu`=0, `Segmented`=1, `Wheel`=2, `RadioGroup`=3 |
330: | `TOGGLE_STYLE` | 0x2018 | `Switch`=0 (default), `Checkbox`=1, `Button`=2 |
331: 
332: Non-`ENUM` scales:
333: 
334: - `FONT_WEIGHT` (0x1008) is a numeric F32 on the 100–900 scale
335:   (`regular`≈400, `bold`≈700), not an enum.
336: - `ROLE` (0x2001) and `STATE` (0x2002) are accessibility enums; their value
337:   sets are defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#semantic-properties) and are not
338:   reproduced here.

1: # Pathland Core Events
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core events** the Pathland protocol supports.
12: Events are the **raw inputs** a renderer reports about the user's interaction —
13: pointer motion, keys, value changes, text edits, scroll. Only the **core
14: events** are specified here; **gestures** (tap, long-press, drag, magnify,
15: rotate) are explicitly **out of scope** and are composed application-side from
16: the raw pointer events (see [Deferred: gestures](#deferred-gestures)).
17: 
18: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
19: - Modifiers (properties): [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
20: - Wire format: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
21: 
22: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
23: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
24: > defines the protocol contract only.
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Event model
29: 
30: Events flow **host → guest**. The renderer is the producer; the app/engine is
31: the consumer. Both directions of the protocol are binary and share the same
32: 16-byte opcode format; events are `EVENT`-category (0x03) opcodes.
33: 
34: ### Who emits what
35: 
36: - The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
37:   writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
38: - The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its
39:   bound `State` signals (which in turn re-emit `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`
40:   deltas).
41: - The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
42:   wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
43:   bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
44:   (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.
45: 
46: ### Transport-aware event guards (MUST)
47: 
48: Renderers **MUST** implement event guards to prevent network noise. A user
49: interaction — tap, text change, drag, value edit — **MUST NEVER** produce an
50: outbound event opcode unless the target node explicitly declared intent in **at
51: least one** of these ways:
52: 
53: 1. it set the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) bits, **or**
54: 2. it is a **value-bearing control** reporting by component type (`SLIDER`,
55:    `TOGGLE`, `PICKER`, `MENU`, `DATE_PICKER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, …), **or**
56: 3. it carries a bound callback property — `ACTION_ID` (0x2016) or `BINDING_ID`
57:    (0x2017) — that identifies where the interaction must be routed.
58: 
59: Interactions that match none of these are **dropped at the renderer**; they are
60: never serialized to the event ring or a network batch. This is the wire-level
61: guard: a `Button` tap with no `ACTION_ID`, no `BINDING_ID`, and no
62: `EVENT_LISTENERS` produces no events.
63: 
64: ### Target resolution
65: 
66: The renderer resolves `targetId` from its own rendered-output tree (its
67: `id → native element` map): the event's position is hit-tested against that
68: tree to find the deepest node with the matching listener bit. If no listener is
69: declared, the event is not reported.
70: 
71: ### Transport paths
72: 
73: | Path | Mechanism |
74: |------|-----------|
75: | Shared memory (desktop/native) | The host writes `EVENT` opcodes into the event ring (host → guest) at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains at `eventReadCursor`. Events are consumed as written (no frame batching). |
76: | Network batch (SSR → browser) | Host → guest batches use the `0x0001` direction flag of the `PLPL` batch format (see OPCODE.md Transport) |
77: 
78: ### Encoding
79: 
80: Every event is a 16-byte opcode:
81: 
82: ```
83: [Category=0x03][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
84: ```
85: 
86: `TEXT_CHANGED` is the exception: its payload is an offset into the host → guest
87: event arena (shared memory) or the batch's string section (network), so it is
88: only fully decodable with that string source (the same convention as
89: `STYLE::SET_TEXT`).
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## Core event catalog
94: 
95: ### Pointer
96: 
97: Pointer events carry a viewport-relative point in **logical points** (`B`=x,
98: `C`=y, f32).
99: 
100: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
101: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
102: | `POINTER_DOWN` | 0x01 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | press (basis of `onTapGesture`, `Button` action) |
103: | `POINTER_MOVE` | 0x02 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` (0x0001) / `HOVER_LEAVE` (0x0002) | hover/enter/leave, drag basis |
104: | `POINTER_UP` | 0x03 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | release (basis of `onTapGesture`) |
105: 
106: - **Flags**:
107:   - `POINTER_SECONDARY`: the secondary button (right mouse, long-press) rather
108:     than the primary.
109:   - `HOVER_ENTER` (bit 0 of `POINTER_MOVE`): the pointer just entered the
110:     node's bounds (is now hovering). `HOVER_LEAVE` (bit 1): the pointer just
111:     left. A plain move has neither bit set.
112: - **Listener bits**: `POINTER_DOWN` (bit 0), `POINTER_MOVE` (bit 1),
113:   `POINTER_UP` (bit 2).
114: - **Renderer**: attaches native press/hover recognition to the matching native
115:   element when the listener bit is set. Multiple pointer events may be reported
116:   for one physical gesture (down → several moves → up), all for the same
117:   `targetId` while the pointer stays over the node.
118: 
119: ### Keyboard
120: 
121: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
122: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
123: | `KEY_DOWN` | 0x04 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` (0x0002) | `onKeyPress(.down)` |
124: | `KEY_UP` | 0x05 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | `onKeyPress(.up)` |
125: 
126: - **`keyCode`**: a **canonical, platform-independent logical key code** (a
127:   renderer maps native scancodes/key-codes onto this canonical set). The
128:   canonical set (letters/digits/arrows/Enter/Tab/…) is renderer-shared and
129:   documented in the conformance vectors.
130: - **`modifiers`**: u8 bitmask — `Shift`=0x01, `Control`=0x02, `Alt`=0x04,
131:   `Meta/Super`=0x08.
132: - **`KEY_REPEAT`**: bit 1 of flags; set when the key is an OS auto-repeat.
133: - **Listener bits**: `KEY_DOWN` (bit 3), `KEY_UP` (bit 4).
134: - **Focus**: keyboard events are reported to the focused node (the node that
135:   most recently gained focus), or to the node that declared the listener and
136:   has keyboard focus. See `FOCUS_CHANGED` below.
137: 
138: ### Value
139: 
140: Value events carry a control's semantic value, resolved by the renderer from
141: its own native control geometry.
142: 
143: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
144: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
145: | `VALUE_CHANGED` | 0x06 | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`Toggle`/`Picker`/`Menu` binding changes |
146: 
147: - **Semantics per control** (see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) controls):
148:   - `SLIDER`/`STEPPER`/`GAUGE` — the numeric value in the control's range.
149:   - `TOGGLE` — 0/1 (checked state; the same value the app writes to
150:     `SELECTED`).
151:   - `PICKER`/`MENU` — the selected option/action-item index.
152:   - `COLOR_PICKER` — the packed `0xAARRGGBB` color reinterpreted as an f32 bit
153:     pattern.
154:   - `DATE_PICKER` uses the dedicated `DATE_CHANGED` event below (its value is
155:     two fields and does not fit `VALUE_CHANGED`).
156: - The app writes the received value into its bound `State`; the engine's
157:   signal flush re-emits the `SET_PROPERTY` delta back to the renderer (the
158:   renderer reflects its own native control).
159: - **No listener bit**: value-bearing controls are reported by the renderer by
160:   virtue of their component type, but still gated by the transport-aware event
161:   guards (a control without `BINDING_ID` reports nothing). The renderer owns
162:   the gesture (e.g. slider drag) that produces them.
163: 
164: ### Date
165: 
166: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
167: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
168: | `DATE_CHANGED` | 0x0D | targetId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | `DatePicker` value binding |
169: 
170: - The date is encoded as two 32-bit fields — `B` = **days since epoch**
171:   (signed I32; pre-1970 is negative) and `C` = **millis of day** (U32,
172:   0..86,400,000) — matching the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (OPCODE.md). No
173:   string/arena indirection: the event is fully inline. It works over the
174:   shared-memory ring today and will use the same inline encoding for host →
175:   guest network batches once that direction lands (see OPCODE.md Transport).
176: - **No listener bit**: like `VALUE_CHANGED`, reported by virtue of the
177:   component type.
178: 
179: ### Text
180: 
181: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
182: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
183: | `TEXT_CHANGED` | 0x07 | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | `TextField` value binding |
184: | `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 0x08 | targetId | focused (0/1) | 0 | — | `@FocusState` |
185: | `EDITING_CHANGED` | 0x09 | targetId | editing (0/1) | 0 | — | `TextField`/`Slider` `onEditingChanged` |
186: | `SUBMIT` | 0x0A | targetId | 0 | 0 | — | `TextField` `onSubmit` / `onCommit` |
187: 
188: - **`TEXT_CHANGED`**: the new text is a length-prefixed entry
189:   (`[u32 byteLength][bytes…]`). Over the **shared-memory ring** the renderer
190:   bump-allocates it into the host-owned **event arena** and `B` is its absolute
191:   offset (see OPCODE.md); over the **network** it lives in the batch's string
192:   section referenced by a *relative* `B` offset — exactly the `STYLE::SET_TEXT`
193:   dual convention. A bare opcode cannot resolve the text; batch-aware decoders
194:   (`pathland-core-transport`, Java `FrameCodec`, TS `decoder.ts`) resolve it.
195:   The event is reported on **every** edit, including intermediate edits, not
196:   only on commit.
197: - **`FOCUS_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 gained focus, 0 lost focus. The renderer reports
198:   it for nodes that declared the `FOCUS` listener bit (bit 5). Focus is what
199:   routes subsequent `KEY_*` events.
200: - **`EDITING_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 editing session began, 0 ended. Reported for
201:   nodes that declared the `EDITING` listener bit (bit 6).
202: - **`SUBMIT`**: the user committed the field (Enter). Reported for nodes that
203:   declared the `SUBMIT` listener bit (bit 7). `B` MAY carry the current text as
204:   a string-section offset (reserved for future use; 0 today).
205: 
206: ### Scroll
207: 
208: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
209: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
210: | `SCROLL` | 0x0B | targetId | offsetX (f32) | offsetY (f32) | — | `ScrollView` offset, `onScrollPhaseChange` |
211: | `WHEEL` | 0x0C | targetId | deltaX (f32) | deltaY (f32) | — | `onScrollWheelEvent` / trackpad |
212: 
213: - **`SCROLL`**: the content offset of a `SCROLLVIEW` (logical points), reported
214:   for nodes that declared the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8). The renderer
215:   reports the absolute offset after each scroll delta.
216: - **`WHEEL`**: raw wheel/trackpad deltas (logical points), reported for nodes
217:   that declared the `WHEEL` listener bit (bit 9). Renderers map native scroll
218:   deltas (GTK `GtkEventControllerScroll`, DOM `wheel`) onto x/y deltas.
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: ## Event listeners (`EVENT_LISTENERS`)
223: 
224: `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) is a u32 bitmask set via `SET_PROPERTY` (U32). Each
225: bit requests one raw-input event kind for the node:
226: 
227: | Bit | Mask | Event |
228: | ----- | ------ | ------- |
229: | 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` |
230: | 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` (incl. hover enter/leave) |
231: | 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` |
232: | 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` |
233: | 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` |
234: | 5 | `0x00000020` | `FOCUS_CHANGED` |
235: | 6 | `0x00000040` | `EDITING_CHANGED` |
236: | 7 | `0x00000080` | `SUBMIT` |
237: | 8 | `0x00000100` | `SCROLL` |
238: | 9 | `0x00000200` | `WHEEL` |
239: | 10–31 | — | reserved |
240: 
241: Convenience aliases (DSL-side): `POINTER = bits 0|1|2`.
242: 
243: DSL surfaces:
244:

- **`transport/Event.java`**: `public record Event(int command, int target, int flags, float x, float y, float value, String text)`; factories `Event.pointerDown(int target, float x, float y)`, `Event.pointerUp(int target, float x, float y)`, `Event.pointerMove(int target, float x, float y, int flags)`, `Event.valueChanged(int target, float value)`, `Event.textChanged(int target, String text)`; predicates `isPointerDown()`, `isPointerUp()`, `isValueChanged()`, `isTextChanged()`.

content.text:
Here's the full gap analysis of the Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) vs. `spec/`. The Java status.md lists only 3 items; the real gap set is larger.

## A. Protocol-breaking (wire correctness) — must fix first

| # | Gap | Detail |
|---|-----|--------|
| A1 | **Legacy component IDs** | `Components.java` still has the pre-renumber IDs (`HSTACK=0x0001, VSTACK=0x0002, TEXT=0x0003, BUTTON=0x0004, IMAGE=0x0005, SWITCH=0x0006, TEXT_FIELD=0x0007, SPACER=0x0008, SCROLLVIEW=0x0009, LIST=0x000A, GRID=0x000B, COMMENT=0x000C, CHECKBOX=0x000D, SLIDER=0x000E`). Spec + Rust core use grouped ranges (`TEXT=0x01, IMAGE=0x02, COLOR=0x03, SPACER=0x06, VSTACK=0x10, HSTACK=0x11, ZSTACK=0x12, BUTTON=0x20, TEXT_FIELD=0x21, TOGGLE=0x24, SLIDER=0x25, COMMENT=0x7F`). Java frames consumed by the Rust GTK renderer (via ring/transport) are **misread as the wrong components**. Delete stale `SWITCH`/`CHECKBOX`/`LIST`; add `COLOR, SHAPE, DIVIDER, PROGRESS_VIEW, GAUGE, ZSTACK, TEXT_EDITOR, TOGGLE, STEPPER, DATE_PICKER, PICKER, MENU, COLOR_PICKER, LAZY_*`; renumber all. |
| A2 | **`Color` not a `COLOR` node** | `Color.render()` emits `IMAGE` + `BACKGROUND_COLOR`. Spec says dual-identity View → `COLOR` (0x03) + `COLOR` property. Blocked by A1 (0x03 currently collides with Java's legacy `TEXT`); unblocks after the ID sync. |
| A3 | **`ValueTypes.forProperty` wrong types** | `VISIBLE`, `ENABLED`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` default to `F32` but spec says `U8`. Missing `IMAGE_SOURCE→STRING`, `SELECTION/ACTION_ID/BINDING_ID→U32`, and the U8 set (`UNDERLINE, STRIKETHROUGH, COLOR_INVERT, ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING, IS_SECURE, IS_INDETERMINATE, FIXED_SIZE_*`). |
| A4 | **`FontWeight` wire values** | Java: `LIGHT=0…BOLD=4`. Spec: `FONT_WEIGHT` is numeric F32 on the **100–900** scale (regular≈400, bold≈700). Emits wrong wire values. |
| A5 | **`Rectangle`/`ZStack` mis-mapping** | `Rectangle` → `IMAGE` (should be `SHAPE` 0x04 + `SHAPE_KIND=Rectangle(1)`); `ZStack` → `COMMENT` (should be `ZSTACK` 0x12). |

## B. Missing components/views

No view classes at all: `Shape`, `Divider`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid/HGrid/VStack/HStack`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker` (only bare IDs for a few). `List` should be removed entirely (spec made it a composite).

## C. Missing modifiers/properties (~45 property IDs, ~35 `View` methods)

- **Layout**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_WIDTH/HEIGHT` (0x0012–0x0017), `FIXED_SIZE_*`, `LAYOUT_PRIORITY`, `ASPECT_RATIO`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`
- **Text-format**: `FONT_STYLE/DESIGN/WIDTH`, `KERNING`, `TRACKING`, `BASELINE_OFFSET`, `LINE_SPACING`, `TEXT_CASE`, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`
- **Effects/transform**: `SHADOW_*`, `BLUR_RADIUS`, `SATURATION/CONTRAST/BRIGHTNESS/GRAYSCALE/HUE_ROTATION`, `COLOR_MULTIPLY`, `COLOR_INVERT`, `ROTATION_DEGREES`, `SCALE`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`
- **Semantic/controls**: `STEP_VALUE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `IS_SECURE`, `PROGRESS`, `IS_INDETERMINATE`, `SELECTION`, `COLOR_VALUE`, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `PICKER_STYLE`, `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`
- **Image**: `IMAGE_SOURCE`
- **Stale**: remove `PADDING_STYLE` (0x1006, not in spec)

## D. Missing events / listener bits

- `Commands.Listeners`: only `POINTER_*` + `KEY_*`; missing `FOCUS`(5), `EDITING`(6), `SUBMIT`(7), `SCROLL`(8), `WHEEL`(9).
- `FrameCodec.decodeEvents` doesn't decode `KEY_DOWN/UP` (0x04/0x05), `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED` (0x0D) — only pointer + `VALUE_CHANGED` + `TEXT_CHANGED`.
- No arbitrary `EVENT_LISTENERS` modifier (Rust has `pointer_events(mask)`); only `TapGestureView`.
- Missing `STYLE::SET_DATE` (0x04) command (needed for `DatePicker`).

## E. Minor

- `Truncation` has extra `NONE=3` (spec: Head/Middle/Tail only).
- Missing control enums (`TOGGLE_STYLE`, `PICKER_STYLE`, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `SHAPE_KIND`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`).

---

## Proposed plan

**Phase 1 — wire sync (A1–A5)**: renumber `Components.java` to spec ranges, fix `Color`/`Rectangle`/`ZStack` mappings, correct `ValueTypes` + `FontWeight`, delete stale constants, update `HtmlRenderer` + `EmitterTest` golden expectations. This makes Java frames spec-valid and cross-language-correct today.

**Phase 2 — modifiers**: add the missing `Properties` constants + `View` modifier methods + `ValueTypes` coverage + enum types.

**Phase 3 — controls/events**: add control views (Toggle, Slider, Picker, etc.) with `BINDING_ID`/value-input wiring, complete listener bits + `FrameCodec` decode, add `SET_DATE`.

# pathland-view (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 25+ DSL (`com.pathland.view`):
SwiftUI-style views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
codec, lazy FFM ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Views**: `View` (open interface), `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Text`,
  `Image`, `Color` (dual identity: a `COLOR` view *and* a value passed into
  style modifiers), `Rectangle` (a `SHAPE` node), `Button`, `TextField`,
  `Spacer`; `body()` composition; `ButtonStyle`/`ViewModifier`/`Environment`
  (ScopedValue).
- **Component IDs**: synced to the spec's grouped ranges (`Components.java`:
  `TEXT 0x01`, `IMAGE 0x02`, `COLOR 0x03`, `SHAPE 0x04`, `SPACER 0x06`,
  `VSTACK 0x10`, `HSTACK 0x11`, `ZSTACK 0x12`, `BUTTON 0x20`, `TEXT_FIELD 0x21`,
  `TOGGLE 0x24`, `SLIDER 0x25`, `COMMENT 0x7F`, …) — frames are spec-valid and
  cross-language correct.
- **Modifiers**: `foregroundStyle(Color)` (no `.color()`), `background(Color)`,
  `tint(Color)`, padding/opacity/font/etc. — `Color` is never a modifier.
- **Value types**: `ValueTypes.forProperty` mirrors `value_type_for`
  (`VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` are `U8`); `FontWeight` uses the spec's
  numeric 100–900 scale.
- **Signals** (`com.pathland.view.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked` — glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression,
  circular-dependency detection.
- **Emitter** (`emit`): mounts once, stable ids, node-level binding effects
  (a signal change re-emits only that node), `FrameOpcodeSink` /
  `RingOpcodeSink`.
- **Wire codec** (`transport`): `FrameCodec` — self-contained `PLPL` frames
  both directions, `encodeEvents`/`decodeEvents` (host→guest events with
  `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section offsets).
- **FFM ring interop** (`ffm`): lazy `libpathland_core` binding, zero JNI.
- **State** (`state`): `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`, auto-wired by
  `pathland-view-processor`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Missing **modifiers/properties** (text-format, effects, transform, layout
  bounds, semantic extras) — see `spec/MODIFIERS.md`; the `View` chain surface
  covers only a subset.
- Missing **control views**: `Toggle`/`Slider`/`TextEditor`/`Picker`/
  `DatePicker`/`Menu`/`ColorPicker`/`Stepper`/`ProgressView`/`Gauge`/
  `Divider`/`Grid`/`ScrollView`/lazy stacks, and the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`
  helpers that route their events.
- Missing **events**: `FrameCodec.decodeEvents` decodes pointer +
  `VALUE_CHANGED` + `TEXT_CHANGED` only — no `KEY_*`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`,
  `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`; no
  `STYLE::SET_DATE` command; no arbitrary `EVENT_LISTENERS` modifier (only
  `TapGestureView`).
- `Truncation` has an extra `NONE` value not in the spec.

## Verified by

`mvn test` (needs JDK 25) — emitter, codec round-trips, signals, state.

All three phases complete, each committed separately:

**`da21e74` — Phase 1: wire sync** — `Components.java` renumbered to the spec's grouped ranges (`TEXT 0x01`…`TOGGLE 0x24`, `SLIDER 0x25`, `COMMENT 0x7F`); stale `SWITCH`/`CHECKBOX`/`LIST` removed; `Color` now a real `COLOR` node, `Rectangle` → `SHAPE`+`SHAPE_KIND`, `ZStack` → `ZSTACK`; `ValueTypes` fixed (`VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` were emitting f32 bits for a U8 property — `visible(true)` decoded as false); `FontWeight` → 100–900 scale; `PADDING_STYLE` removed.

**`23f363d` — Phase 2: modifiers** — full `MODIFIERS.md` property catalog (~45 IDs) + ~35 chainable `View` methods (offset/position/fixedSize/shadow/blur/filters/clipShape/rotation/accessibility/imageSource/fontFamily…), complete spec value-type table, new enums (`FontStyle`, `FontDesign`, `TextCase`, `ContentMode`, `ControlSize`), `Truncation.NONE` removed.

**`488fcf0` — Phase 3: controls/events** — 19 new views (`Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `TextEditor`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Divider`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyV/HStack/VGrid/HGrid`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker`, `DatePicker`), value controls wired to writable signals via the emitter's value-input registry; `STYLE::SET_DATE` + node-level date binding; full event catalog round-trips (`KEY_*`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`) with listener bits 0–9; `pointerEvents(mask)` modifier; HTML renderer covers all new components.

**Verification**: 36 Java tests pass (compiled+run via JDK 22 preview as a stand-in for the unavailable JDK 25) and 190 Rust tests remain green. 22: /**
23:  * One Pathland application instance per WebSocket connection (1:1). Identical to the
24:  * Quarkus {@code SessionApp} except for the WebSocket transport type ({@link WebSocketSession}
25:  * instead of {@code WebSocketConnection}) — the view, state, and emitter code is shared.
26:  */
27: final class SessionApp {
28: 
29:     private final PersistentState state;
30:     private final CounterView root;
31: 
32:     private final HtmlRenderer html = new HtmlRenderer();
33:     private final FrameOpcodeSink sink;
34:     private final Emitter emitter;
35:     private final Map<Integer, Runnable> tapActions;
36:     private final Map<Integer, Consumer<String>> textInputs;
37:     private final Map<Integer, Consumer<Float>> valueInputs;
38:     private final int rootId;
39: 
40:     /** Frames emitted before the connection attaches, replayed to it on connect. */
41:     private final List<Frame> pending = new ArrayList<>();
42: 
43:     private volatile WebSocketSession session;
44: 
45:     SessionApp(String sessionId, StateStore store) {
46:         this.state = new PersistentState(store, sessionId);
47:         this.root = new CounterView();
48: 
49:         this.sink = new FrameOpcodeSink() {
50:             @Override
51:             public void endFrame() {
52:                 super.endFrame();
53:                 Frame frame = frame();
54:                 if (!frame.opcodes().isEmpty()) {
55:                     html.applyFrame(frame);
56:                     WebSocketSession s = session;
57:                     if (s == null || !s.isOpen()) {
58:                         pending.add(frame);
59:                     } else {
60:                         send(frame);
61:                     }
62:                 }
63:             }
64:         };
65:         this.emitter = new Emitter(sink);
66: 
67:         // Mount wires State fields, then renders and emits the structural frame.
68:         RenderResult result = emitter.mount(root, new Environment(state));
69:         this.tapActions = result.tapActions();
70:         this.textInputs = result.textInputs();
71:         this.valueInputs = result.valueInputs();
72:         this.rootId = result.rootId();
73:     }
74: 
75:     void connect(WebSocketSession session) {
76:         this.session = session;
77:         for (Frame frame : pending) {
78:             send(frame);
79:         }
80:         pending.clear();
81:     }
82: 
83:     private void send(Frame frame) {
84:         WebSocketSession s = session;
85:         if (s == null || !s.isOpen()) {
86:             session = null;
87:             return;
88:         }
89:         byte[] bytes = FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame);
90:         try {
91:             s.sendMessage(new BinaryMessage(bytes));
92:         } catch (Exception e) {
93:             session = null;
94:         }
95:     }
96: 
97:     void dispatch(byte[] message) {
98:         try {
99:             for (Event event : FrameCodec.decodeEvents(message)) {
100:                 if (event.isPointerUp()) {
101:                     Runnable action = tapActions.get(event.target());
102:                     if (action != null) {
103:                         action.run();
104:                     }
105:                 } else if (event.isTextChanged()) {
106:                     Consumer<String> sink = textInputs.get(event.target());
107:                     if (sink != null) {
108:                         sink.accept(event.text());
109:                     }
110:                 } else if (event.isValueChanged()) {
111:                     Consumer<Float> sink = valueInputs.get(event.target());
112:                     if (sink != null) {
113:                         sink.accept(event.value());
114:                     }
115:                 }
116:             }
117:         } catch (RuntimeException e) {
118:             log("dropping event batch: " + e.getMessage());
119:         }
120:     }
121: 
122:     String renderHtml() {
123:         return html.render(rootId)
124:                 .replace("</body>", "<script src=\"/app.js\" defer></script></body>");
125:     }
126: 
127:     void close() {
128:         state.close();
129:         emitter.destroy();
130:         session = null;
131:     }
132: 
133:     private static void log(String message) {
134:         System.out.println("[pathland] " + message);
135:     }
136: }

43:     case COMPONENT.LIST: return 'list';
44:     case COMPONENT.GRID: return 'grid';
45:     case COMPONENT.COMMENT: return 'comment';
46:     case COMPONENT.CHECKBOX: return 'checkbox';

48:     default: return 'unknown';

52: /** ngui modifier inputs decoded from a node's properties (see `@apaq/ngui-elements/core`). */
53: export interface NguiMods {
54:   padding?: PaddingOptions;
55:   color?: string;
56:   background?: BackgroundOptions;
57:   border?: BorderOptions;
58:   rounding?: RoundingOptions;
59:   opacity?: number;
60:   font?: FontOptions;
61:   frame?: FrameOptions;
62:   flex?: FlexOptions;
63:   lineLimit?: number;
64: }
