1: # Pathland Core Modifiers
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core modifiers** the Pathland protocol must
12: support. In the protocol these are the **`STYLE` properties**: the constraint
13: properties and visual decorations carried by `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY`. The set
14: mirrors SwiftUI's core modifiers so that any SwiftUI-shaped UI can be expressed.
15: 
16: Like SwiftUI, modifiers in Pathland are **decoupled from views**: any modifier
17: applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a `VStack` alike). A
18: modifier that a particular renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** —
19: the property is still emitted; the renderer skips it. Application code composes
20: custom modifiers from these core ones.
21: 
22: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
23: - Wire format and value types: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
24: - Events: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)
25: 
26: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
27: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
28: > defines the protocol contract only.
29: 
30: ### Emission rules
31: 
32: Each modifier emits **one or more** `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY` opcodes — one per
33: underlying property. There is no compound-modifier opcode. Compound SwiftUI
34: modifiers (`.frame(width:height:alignment:)`, `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)`,
35: `.border(_:width:)`) are expanded into several `SET_PROPERTY` opcodes, exactly
36: as the existing `.frame` modifier already does (`WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` +
37: `ALIGNMENT`).
38: 
39: `SET_PROPERTY` packing (see OPCODE.md):
40: 
41: ```
42: A = nodeId
43: B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
44: C = value (f32 bit pattern / u32 / u8 / color / arenaRef)
45: ```
46: 
47: Only **changed** properties emit: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes
48: (diff-based reactive emission). `STRING`-valued properties carry their text in
49: the frame's string section; `C` holds the arena offset.
50: 
51: ### Value types (from `value_type`, u8)
52: 
53: | Value Type | Value | `C` encoding |
54: |------------|-------|--------------|
55: | `U8` | 0x01 | low byte of C |
56: | `U32` | 0x02 | u32 |
57: | `I32` | 0x03 | i32 |
58: | `F32` | 0x04 | f32 bit pattern |
59: | `STRING` | 0x05 | arenaRef (utf8) |
60: | `ENUM` | 0x06 | low byte of C |
61: | `COLOR` | 0x07 | packed `0xAARRGGBB` (sRGB) |
62: | `DESIGN_TOKEN` | 0x08 | arenaRef (token path) |
63: 
64: Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1.0` = `FILL` (expand to available), `-2.0` =
65: `HUG_CONTENT` (native intrinsic size).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 1. Layout
70: 
71: Arrangement and sizing. These map to the native renderer's layout knobs.
72: 
73: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
74: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
75: | `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` | `WIDTH` 0x100B, `HEIGHT` 0x100C, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002 | F32, F32, ENUM | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided axis/alignment |
76: | `.frame(minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:minHeight:idealHeight:maxHeight:)` | `MIN_WIDTH` 0x0012, `IDEAL_WIDTH` 0x0013, `MAX_WIDTH` 0x0014, `MIN_HEIGHT` 0x0015, `IDEAL_HEIGHT` 0x0016, `MAX_HEIGHT` 0x0017 | F32 | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided bound |
77: | `.padding(_:)`, `.padding(edges:)`, `.padding(_:edges:)` | `PADDING` 0x1011, `PADDING_TOP` 0x1012, `PADDING_RIGHT` 0x1013, `PADDING_BOTTOM` 0x1014, `PADDING_LEFT` 0x1015 | F32 | uniform → one; per-edge → per-edge |
78: | `.offset(x:y:)` | `OFFSET_X` 0x000E, `OFFSET_Y` 0x000F | F32 | two |
79: | `.position(x:y:)` | `POSITION_X` 0x0010, `POSITION_Y` 0x0011 | F32 | two |
80: | `.fixedSize()` / `.fixedSize(horizontal:vertical:)` | `FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL` 0x0018, `FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL` 0x0019 | U8 (0/1) | two (or one when axis-limited) |
81: | `.layoutPriority(_:)` | `LAYOUT_PRIORITY` 0x001A | F32 | one |
82: | `.zIndex(_:)` | `Z_INDEX` 0x100F | F32 | one |
83: | `.aspectRatio(_:contentMode:)` | `ASPECT_RATIO` 0x001B, `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | F32, ENUM | two |
84: | `.scaledToFit()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fit`=0) | one |
85: | `.scaledToFill()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fill`=1) | one |
86: | `.minimumScaleFactor(_:)` | `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR` 0x001D | F32 | one |
87: | `.spacing(_:)` (stacks) | `SPACING` 0x0001 | F32 | one |
88: | `Spacer` | — (implied by component) | — | none |
89: 
90: ### Semantics
91: 
92: - **`WIDTH` / `HEIGHT`**: size hints; the renderer maps them to its size
93:   request / `width`/`height` style. `FILL` (-1.0) expands to available space;
94:   `HUG_CONTENT` (-2.0) sizes to intrinsic content. Absence of a property leaves
95:   that axis to the native default.
96: - **`frame(min/ideal/max)`**: each provided bound emits its own property.
97:   Renderers map them to min/max/ideal size (GTK `set_size_request`, CSS
98:   `min-width`/`max-width`/`width`).
99: - **`PADDING` vs per-edge**: `PADDING` is uniform and shorthand; a per-edge
100:   modifier overwrites the edge only. Per-edge wins over uniform when both are
101:   present.
102: - **`ALIGNMENT` enum**: `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3.
103: - **`CONTENT_MODE` enum**: `Fit`=0 (aspect-fit within the bounds),
104:   `Fill`=1 (aspect-fill, cropped).
105: - **`OFFSET`** moves the element **after** layout without affecting layout
106:   (post-layout translation; GTK margins/translation, CSS `transform:
107:   translate`).
108: - **`POSITION`** is absolute placement within the parent (CSS `position:
109:   absolute; left/top`); the renderer resolves the anchor.
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## 2. Text Formatting
114: 
115: Apply to `Text`, `Label`, `Button` labels, and text-bearing controls. Renderers
116: map them to their native text attributes.
117: 
118: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
119: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
120: | `.font(.system(size:))` | `FONT_SIZE` 0x1007 | F32 | one |
121: | `.fontWeight(_:)` | `FONT_WEIGHT` 0x1008 | F32 (100–900) | one |
122: | `.font(.custom(name:size:))` | `FONT_FAMILY` 0x1009 | STRING | one (arenaRef) |
123: | `.italic()` / `.fontStyle(_:)` | `FONT_STYLE` 0x1017 | ENUM (`Normal`=0, `Italic`=1) | one |
124: | `.fontDesign(_:)` | `FONT_DESIGN` 0x1018 | ENUM (`Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3) | one |
125: | `.fontWidth(_:)` | `FONT_WIDTH` 0x1019 | F32 (0.5–1.5, 1.0 default) | one |
126: | `.kerning(_:)` | `KERNING` 0x101A | F32 | one |
127: | `.tracking(_:)` | `TRACKING` 0x101B | F32 | one |
128: | `.baselineOffset(_:)` | `BASELINE_OFFSET` 0x101C | F32 | one |
129: | `.lineSpacing(_:)` | `LINE_SPACING` 0x101D | F32 | one |
130: | `.lineLimit(_:)` | `LINE_LIMIT` 0x000B | U32 | one |
131: | `.multilineTextAlignment(_:)` | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` 0x000C | ENUM (`Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2) | one |
132: | `.truncationMode(_:)` | `TRUNCATION_MODE` 0x000D | ENUM (`Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2) | one |
133: | `.textCase(_:)` | `TEXT_CASE` 0x101E | ENUM (`None`=0, `Uppercase`=1, `Lowercase`=2) | one |
134: | `.underline()` | `UNDERLINE` 0x101F | U8 (0/1) | one |
135: | `.strikethrough()` | `STRIKETHROUGH` 0x1020 | U8 (0/1) | one |
136: | `.foregroundStyle(_:)` | `COLOR` 0x100A | COLOR | one |
137: | `.tint(_:)` | `TINT` 0x1030 | COLOR | one |
138: 
139: > **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` exists only as a **View** (a
140: > layout-greedy solid-color fill) and as a **Data Type** passed into
141: > style-taking modifiers (`.foregroundStyle(_:)`, `.background(_:)`,
142: > `.border(_:)`, `.tint(_:)`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier and
143: > `.foregroundColor(_:)` is deprecated — all foreground styling uses
144: > `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
145: 
146: \* `FONT_FAMILY` is a `STRING` property (arenaRef), matching SwiftUI, which
147: passes font families as string names (`.font(.custom("Georgia", size:))`).
148: 
149: ### Semantics
150: 
151: - **`FONT_WEIGHT`** is a numeric F32 on the 100–900 scale (`regular`≈400,
152:   `bold`≈700). Renderers map it to the nearest native weight.
153: - **`KERNING` vs `TRACKING`**: kerning adjusts per-glyph spacing at a
154:   point/em scale; tracking adds uniform letter spacing. Both are F32 points.
155: - **`LINE_LIMIT`** of 0 means unlimited.
156: - **`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`** differs from stack `ALIGNMENT`: it aligns the text block
157:   inside its own bounds (CSS `text-align`), not children of a stack.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 3. Appearance & Effects
162: 
163: Visual decoration. These never change layout; they decorate the element.
164: 
165: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
166: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
167: | `.background(_:)` | `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001 | COLOR | one |
168: | `.border(_:width:)` | `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `BORDER_WIDTH` 0x1003 | COLOR, F32 | two |
169: | `.border(_:width:edges:)` | `BORDER_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`, `BORDER_EDGES` 0x1016 | COLOR, F32, U32 (bitmask) | three |
170: | `.cornerRadius(_:)` | `BORDER_RADIUS` 0x1005 | F32 | one |
171: | `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)` | `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `SHADOW_RADIUS` 0x1022, `SHADOW_X` 0x1023, `SHADOW_Y` 0x1024 | COLOR, F32, F32, F32 | four |
172: | `.opacity(_:)` | `OPACITY` 0x100D | F32 (0–1) | one |
173: | `.blur(radius:)` | `BLUR_RADIUS` 0x1025 | F32 | one |
174: | `.saturation(_:)` | `SATURATION` 0x1026 | F32 (0–1) | one |
175: | `.contrast(_:)` | `CONTRAST` 0x1027 | F32 (0–1) | one |
176: | `.brightness(_:)` | `BRIGHTNESS` 0x1028 | F32 (−1–1) | one |
177: | `.grayscale(_:)` | `GRAYSCALE` 0x1029 | F32 (0–1) | one |
178: | `.hueRotation(_:)` | `HUE_ROTATION` 0x102A | F32 (degrees) | one |
179: | `.colorMultiply(_:)` | `COLOR_MULTIPLY` 0x102B | COLOR | one |
180: | `.colorInvert()` | `COLOR_INVERT` 0x102C | U8 (0/1) | one |
181: | `.clipped()` / `.clipsToBounds` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 | U8 (0/1) | one |
182: | `.clipShape(_:)` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 + `SHAPE_KIND` 0x0006 | U8 + ENUM | two (see note) |
183: 
184: ### Semantics
185: 
186: - **`BORDER_EDGES`** is a u32 bitmask: `TOP`=1, `LEADING`=2, `BOTTOM`=4,
187:   `TRAILING`=8 (direction-aware; see OPCODE.md). When `.border` has no `edges:`
188:   argument the renderer treats the mask as `ALL` (0xF).
189: - **`BORDER_RADIUS`** rounds all corners; a future per-corner variant would add
190:   `TOP_LEFT_*`/… properties.
191: - **`SHADOW`** is a compound: exactly four `SET_PROPERTY` opcodes. Missing
192:   fields default: color = token `color.shadow`, radius = 0, x = 0, y = 0.
193: - **`clipShape`**: `SHAPE_KIND` (0x0006, defined in
194:   [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md#5-shapes--paints)) selects the clip geometry;
195:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` (1) turns clipping on. A bare `.clipped()` is
196:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` with no shape.
197: - **Color effects** (`SATURATION`, `CONTRAST`, …) are renderer-owned filters;
198:   the renderer maps them to native filter APIs (CSS `filter`, GTK
199:   `GtkSnapshot` effects). They compose in the order applied.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 4. Transform
204: 
205: Geometric transforms applied after layout.
206: 
207: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
208: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
209: | `.rotationEffect(_:anchor:)` | `ROTATION_DEGREES` 0x102D | F32 (degrees, counter-clockwise) | one (anchor is renderer-token-owned) |
210: | `.scaleEffect(_:anchor:)` | `SCALE` 0x102E | F32 (uniform scale) | one (anchor is renderer-token-owned) |
211: 
212: ### Semantics
213: 
214: - Transforms do **not** affect layout; the renderer applies them as a
215:   post-layout visual transform (CSS `transform`, GTK `gtk_widget_allocate`
216:   transform).
217: - **Anchor** is renderer-token-owned (`.center` default); the protocol does not
218:   transmit anchors — the renderer owns presentation (see OPCODE.md design
219:   tokens). Non-uniform scale / 3D rotation are future extensions.
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## 5. Interaction & State
224: 
225: Semantic properties controlling whether and how an element responds to input,
226: plus accessibility. These are the "semantic" (`0x2000`) properties.
227: 
228: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property | Type | Emission |
229: | ------------------ | ------------------- | ------ | ---------- |
230: | `.hidden()` | `VISIBLE` 0x100E | U8 (0 = hidden) | one |
231: | `.disabled(_:)` | `ENABLED` 0x2003 | U8 (1 = enabled) | one |
232: | `.allowsHitTesting(_:)` | `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING` 0x102F | U8 (0/1) | one |
233: | `.controlSize(_:)` | `CONTROL_SIZE` 0x200C | ENUM (`Small`=0, `Regular`=1, `Large`=2) | one |
234: | `.focusable(_:)` | — (via `FOCUS` listener) | — | none (declares `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit 5) |
235: | `.accessibilityLabel(_:)` | `LABEL` 0x200A | STRING | one (arenaRef) |
236: | `.accessibilityRole(_:)` | `ROLE` 0x2001 | ENUM | one |
237: | `.accessibilityState(_:)` | `STATE` 0x2002 | ENUM | one |
238: 
239: ### Semantics
240: 
241: - **`VISIBLE`**: 0 hides the element entirely (removed from layout and hit
242:   testing by the renderer); 1 shows it. Diff-based emission means toggling
243:   visibility emits a single `SET_PROPERTY`.
244: - **`ENABLED`** is the inverse of SwiftUI `.disabled()`: 1 = interactive, 0 =
245:   disabled. Disabled controls do not emit events.
246: - **`.focusable`** has no property: the app requests focus events via the
247:   `FOCUS` listener bit (`EVENT_LISTENERS`, bit 5) and observes
248:   `EVENT::FOCUS_CHANGED` — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md).
249: - **`ROLE`/`STATE`** are accessibility enums; their enumerated values are
250:   defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#semantic-properties), not here. `STATE` is
251:   a semantic accessibility property — it never describes visual styling.
252: - **`LABEL`** is a `STRING` property (the accessibility label), distinct from a
253:   `TEXT_FIELD`'s caption label.
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## Property ID Catalog
258: 
259: ### Allocated property IDs
260: 
261: | Range | Group |
262: | ------- | ------- |
263: | `0x0001`–`0x0005` | Stack constraint (SPACING, ALIGNMENT, …, CONTENT_MARGINS) |
264: | `0x0006` | `SHAPE_KIND` (ENUM; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
265: | `0x000A`–`0x000D` | Text (TEXT, LINE_LIMIT, TEXT_ALIGNMENT, TRUNCATION_MODE) |
266: | `0x000E`–`0x001D` | Layout properties (allocated: OFFSET, POSITION, frame bounds, FIXED_SIZE, LAYOUT_PRIORITY, ASPECT_RATIO/CONTENT_MODE, MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR) |
267: | `0x001E`–`0x00FF` | Future layout/format properties (unallocated) |
268: | `0x1001`–`0x1016` | Styling (BACKGROUND_COLOR, BORDER_*, FONT_SIZE/WEIGHT/FAMILY, COLOR, WIDTH, HEIGHT, OPACITY, VISIBLE, Z_INDEX, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS, PADDING_*, BORDER_EDGES) |
269: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (STRING; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
270: | `0x1017`–`0x102F` | Text-format properties (allocated: FONT_STYLE/DESIGN/WIDTH, KERNING, TRACKING, BASELINE_OFFSET, LINE_SPACING, TEXT_CASE, UNDERLINE, STRIKETHROUGH), effect properties (SHADOW_*, BLUR, SATURATION, CONTRAST, BRIGHTNESS, GRAYSCALE, HUE_ROTATION, COLOR_MULTIPLY, COLOR_INVERT), ROTATION_DEGREES, SCALE, ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING |
271: | `0x1030` | `TINT` (COLOR) | — |
272: | `0x1030`–`0x10FF` | Future styling properties (unallocated) |
273: | `0x2001`–`0x200B` | Semantic (ROLE, STATE, ENABLED, SELECTED, EVENT_LISTENERS, VALUE, MIN_VALUE, MAX_VALUE, LABEL, PROMPT) |
274: | `0x2009`, `0x200C`–`0x2014` | Control properties (allocated: STEP_VALUE, CONTROL_SIZE, IS_SECURE, PROGRESS, IS_INDETERMINATE, SELECTION, COLOR_VALUE, DATE_PICKER_MODE, PICKER_STYLE) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md controls. Note: a `DATE_PICKER`'s date is set via the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (0x04), not a property; **`0x2011` is unallocated/reserved** (its former `DATE_VALUE` draft was dropped) |
275: | `0x2016`–`0x2018` | Binding/action properties (allocated: `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md semantic controls |
276: | `0x2015`, `0x2019`–`0x20FF` | Future semantic properties (unallocated) |
277: 
278: ### Reserved ranges
279: 
280: | Range | Use |
281: |-------|-----|
282: | `0x0003`, `0x0004` | Reserved (formerly JUSTIFICATION, PADDING) — MUST NOT be reused |
283: | `0x0007`–`0x0009`, `0x000E`+ high | Draft/future layout |
284: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (allocated) |
285: 
286: A renderer MUST ignore unknown property ids and continue decoding.
287: 
288: ### Default value type resolution
289: 
290: The canonical value type per property (the protocol's authoritative mapping):
291: 
292: - `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_COLOR`, `COLOR_MULTIPLY`,
293:   `SHADOW_COLOR`, `COLOR_VALUE`, `TINT` → `COLOR`
294: - `EVENT_LISTENERS`, `BORDER_EDGES` → `U32`
295: - `SELECTED`, `VISIBLE`, `ENABLED`, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`,
296:   `COLOR_INVERT`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `IS_SECURE`,
297:   `IS_INDETERMINATE`, `FIXED_SIZE_*` → `U8`
298: - `LABEL`, `PROMPT`, `FONT_FAMILY`, `IMAGE_SOURCE` → `STRING`
299: - `LINE_LIMIT`, `SELECTION`, `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID` → `U32`
300: - `ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`,
301:   `FONT_DESIGN`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `SHAPE_KIND`,
302:   `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `PICKER_STYLE`, `TOGGLE_STYLE` → `F32` (numeric enum code;
303:   see the appendix and [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#value-types))
304: - everything else → `F32`
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## Appendix: Enumerated values
309: 
310: Single authoritative source for every enum-valued property in the protocol.
311: A renderer or emitter MUST use these exact numeric codes. The code is carried
312: in the property value as an **f32 bit pattern** (`value_type::F32`) — see the
313: [value-type
314: conventions](./OPCODE.md#value-types) and the [default value type
315: resolution](#default-value-type-resolution).
316: 
317: | Property | ID | Values |
318: |----------|----|--------|
319: | `ALIGNMENT` | 0x0002 | `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3 |
320: | `SHAPE_KIND` | 0x0006 | `Circle`=0, `Rectangle`=1, `RoundedRectangle`=2, `Capsule`=3, `Ellipse`=4, `Path`=5 |
321: | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` | 0x000C | `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2 |
322: | `TRUNCATION_MODE` | 0x000D | `Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2 |
323: | `CONTENT_MODE` | 0x001C | `Fit`=0, `Fill`=1 |
324: | `FONT_STYLE` | 0x1017 | `Normal`=0, `Italic`=1 |
325: | `FONT_DESIGN` | 0x1018 | `Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3 |
326: | `TEXT_CASE` | 0x101E | `None`=0, `Uppercase`=1, `Lowercase`=2 |
327: | `CONTROL_SIZE` | 0x200C | `Small`=0, `Regular`=1, `Large`=2 |
328: | `DATE_PICKER_MODE` | 0x2013 | `Date`=0, `Time`=1, `DateAndTime`=2 |
329: | `PICKER_STYLE` | 0x2014 | `Menu`=0, `Segmented`=1, `Wheel`=2, `RadioGroup`=3 |
330: | `TOGGLE_STYLE` | 0x2018 | `Switch`=0 (default), `Checkbox`=1, `Button`=2 |
331: 
332: Non-`ENUM` scales:
333: 
334: - `FONT_WEIGHT` (0x1008) is a numeric F32 on the 100–900 scale
335:   (`regular`≈400, `bold`≈700), not an enum.
336: - `ROLE` (0x2001) and `STATE` (0x2002) are accessibility enums; their value
337:   sets are defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#semantic-properties) and are not
338:   reproduced here.
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## Conformance
343: 
344: New properties added here MUST be reflected in `pathland-core`'s diff emitter
345: and the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) before renderers
346: depend on them.

(End of file - total 346 lines)

content.text: I want to emphasize that we want to stay as close to Swiftui as possible while keepin state variables as signals. we want to learn from the Java DSL. It has pretty much all the right things, except the syntax is not quite as close to swiftui as it could be.
I'll research the existing DSLs to ground the spec, focusing on the Java DSL surface and its divergences from SwiftUI syntax.

1: //! # pathland-view
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,
4: //! `Text`) and chainable modifiers (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`,
5: //! `background`) build a retained **view tree** (`pathland_engine::Node`) that the
6: //! diff emitter in `pathland-core` turns into declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes.
7: //!
8: //! ## Building a tree
9: //!
10: //! Use the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros (which box children for you) with the
11: //! free `text`/`spacer` functions, then chain modifiers and `build()`:
12: //!
13: //! ```
14: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, hstack, text, View, ViewExt};
15: //!
16: //! let node = vstack![
17: //!     text("a"),
18: //!     hstack![text("b")],
19: //! ]
20: //! .padding(16.0)
21: //! .build();
22: //! # let _ = node;
23: //! ```
24: //!
25: //! ## Decoupled modifiers
26: //!
27: //! Modifiers are **decoupled from views** (SwiftUI-style): any modifier applies
28: //! to any view via the blanket `View::modifier`, and application code composes
29: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:
30: //!
31: //! ```
32: //! use pathland_view::{View, ViewExt, ViewModifier, Node, Padding, Background, Color};
33: //!
34: //! struct Card;
35: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
36: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
37: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
38: //!         Background(Color(0xFF_EEEEEE)).apply(node);
39: //!     }
40: //! }
41: //!
42: //! // Works on any view:
43: //! let a = pathland_view::text("A").modifier(Card);
44: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].modifier(Card);
45: //! # let _ = (a, b);
46: //! ```
47: //!
48: //! Unsupported combinations are **allowed and ignored**: the modifier emits its
49: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.
50: //!
51: //! ## No layout math
52: //!
53: //! The DSL describes structure + constraint properties only. It never computes
54: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.
55: //!
56: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`.
57:

59: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]

92: /// Build a vertical stack from a comma-separated list of views.
93: ///
94: /// Each child is boxed automatically, so children can mix `Text`, `HStack`,
95: /// modified views, or custom `View` implementations. Nested stacks work:
96: ///
97: /// ```
98: /// use pathland_view::{vstack, text, View};
99: /// let node = vstack![text("a"), text("b")].build();
100: /// # let _ = node;
101: /// ```
102: #[macro_export]
103: macro_rules! vstack {
104:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
105:         $crate::VStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
106:     };
107: }
108: 
109: /// Build a horizontal stack from a comma-separated list of views.
110: ///
111: /// See [`vstack!`] for details.
112: #[macro_export]
113: macro_rules! hstack {
114:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
115:         $crate::HStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
116:     };
117: }

126:     Spacer

129: /// Cross-axis alignment values for stacks and the `Frame` compound modifier.
130: ///
131: /// These are emitted as the `ALIGNMENT` (0x0002) property with an `ENUM` value
132: /// type (low byte of the property value).
133: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
134: pub enum Align {
135:     /// Align to the leading (start) edge.
136:     Leading,
137:     /// Center along the cross axis.
138:     Center,
139:     /// Align to the trailing (end) edge.
140:     Trailing,
141:     /// Fill the available cross-axis space.
142:     Fill,
143: }
144: 
145: impl Align {
146:     /// The protocol enum value for this alignment.
147:     pub fn value(self) -> u8 {
148:         match self {
149:             Align::Leading => 0,
150:             Align::Center => 1,
151:             Align::Trailing => 2,
152:             Align::Fill => 3,
153:         }
154:     }
155: }

157: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
158: // View protocol
159: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
160: 
161: /// A composable view. Implement for custom views; the core components and
162: /// `Modified` wrappers implement it already.
163: pub trait View {
164:     /// Build the retained node for this view.
165:     fn build(&self) -> Node;
166: }
167: 
168: /// A view decorator (SwiftUI `ViewModifier`): transforms a node's properties.
169: ///
170: /// Core modifiers (`Spacing`, `Padding`, `FontSize`, `Color`, `Background`)
171: /// implement this; application code implements it to compose custom modifiers.
172: pub trait ViewModifier {
173:     /// Apply the modifier to `node` (mutating constraint properties).
174:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node);
175: }
176: 
177: /// A view wrapped by a modifier (SwiftUI `some View` nesting).
178: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
179: pub struct Modified<V, M> {
180:     view: V,
181:     modifier: M,
182: }
183: 
184: impl<V: View, M: ViewModifier> View for Modified<V, M> {
185:     fn build(&self) -> Node {
186:         let mut node = self.view.build();
187:         self.modifier.apply(&mut node);
188:         node
189:     }
190: }
191: 
192: /// Blanket modifier methods on any `View`.
193: ///
194: /// `.modifier(...)` applies a custom (or core) modifier; the sugar methods
195: /// (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`, `background`) are conveniences
196: /// that construct the corresponding core modifier. Modifiers apply
197: /// innermost-first, matching SwiftUI ordering.
198: pub trait ViewExt: View + Sized {
199:     /// Apply a modifier to this view.
200:     fn modifier<M: ViewModifier>(self, modifier: M) -> Modified<Self, M> {
201:         Modified { view: self, modifier }
202:     }
203: 
204:     /// Chain `.spacing(value)`.
205:     fn spacing(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Spacing> {
206:         self.modifier(Spacing(value))
207:     }
208: 
209:     /// Chain `.padding(value)`.
210:     fn padding(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Padding> {
211:         self.modifier(Padding(value))
212:     }
213: 
214:     /// Chain `.font_size(value)`.
215:     fn font_size(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, FontSize> {
216:         self.modifier(FontSize(value))
217:     }
218: 
219:     /// Chain `.foreground_style(color)` — the foreground color
220:     /// (a `COLOR` property). There is deliberately **no** `.color()` /
221:     /// `.foregroundColor()` modifier; foreground styling is
222:     /// `.foreground_style(_:)` (SwiftUI `.foregroundStyle`).
223:     fn foreground_style(self, color: Color) -> Modified<Self, ForegroundStyle> {
224:         self.modifier(ForegroundStyle(color))
225:     }
226: 
227:     /// Chain `.background(color)` — the background color.
228:     fn background(self, color: Color) -> Modified<Self, Background> {
229:         self.modifier(Background(color))
230:     }
231: 
232:     /// Chain `.border(color, width)`.
233:     fn border(self, color: Color, width: f32) -> Modified<Self, Border> {
234:         self.modifier(Border { color, width })
235:     }
236: 
237:     /// Chain `.tint(color)` — the accent/tint color (a `TINT` property).
238:     fn tint(self, color: Color) -> Modified<Self, Tint> {
239:         self.modifier(Tint(color))
240:     }
241: 
242:     /// Chain `.frame(width, height, alignment)` — a compound sizing modifier.
243:     ///
244:     /// `width`/`height` use the `size::FILL` (-1.0) and `size::HUG_CONTENT`
245:     /// (-2.0) sentinels, or `None` to leave that axis to the native renderer.
246:     /// When an alignment is provided it is emitted as the `ALIGNMENT` property.
247:     fn frame(
248:         self,
249:         width: Option<f32>,
250:         height: Option<f32>,
251:         alignment: Option<Align>,
252:     ) -> Modified<Self, Frame> {
253:         self.modifier(Frame {
254:             width,
255:             height,
256:             alignment,
257:         })
258:     }
259: 
260:     /// Chain `.pointer_events(mask)` — declare which raw pointer events this
261:     /// view wants the renderer to report (`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask). This is
262:     /// what makes any element (not just a button) emit raw events; combine
263:     /// `pathland_core::listener::*` bits, e.g.
264:     /// `POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_UP`.
265:     fn pointer_events(self, mask: u32) -> Modified<Self, PointerEvents> {
266:         self.modifier(PointerEvents(mask))
267:     }
268: 
269:     /// Chain `.on_tap_gesture(f)` — attach a tap gesture (SwiftUI
270:     /// `onTapGesture`) to any view. The callback `f` runs when a tap is
271:     /// recognized from the view's raw pointer events (down then up on the same
272:     /// target).
273:     fn on_tap_gesture<F: FnMut() + 'static>(self, f: F) -> Modified<Self, TapGesture> {
274:         self.modifier(TapGesture(Rc::new(RefCell::new(f))))
275:     }
276: 
277:     /// Chain `.opacity(value)` (0..1).
278:     fn opacity(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Opacity> {
279:         self.modifier(Opacity(value))
280:     }
281: 
282:     /// Chain `.hidden()` — hide the view (`VISIBLE` = 0).
283:     fn hidden(self) -> Modified<Self, Hidden> {
284:         self.modifier(Hidden)
285:     }
286: 
287:     /// Chain `.corner_radius(value)`.
288:     fn corner_radius(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, CornerRadius> {
289:         self.modifier(CornerRadius(value))
290:     }
291: 
292:     /// Chain `.font_weight(value)` (100–900).
293:     fn font_weight(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, FontWeight> {
294:         self.modifier(FontWeight(value))
295:     }
296: 
297:     /// Chain `.line_limit(n)` (0 = unlimited).
298:     fn line_limit(self, n: u32) -> Modified<Self, LineLimit> {
299:         self.modifier(LineLimit(n))
300:     }
301: 
302:     /// Chain `.text_alignment(a)` (0=Leading, 1=Center, 2=Trailing).
303:     fn text_alignment(self, a: u8) -> Modified<Self, TextAlignment> {
304:         self.modifier(TextAlignment(a))
305:     }
306: 
307:     /// Chain `.truncation_mode(m)` (0=Head, 1=Middle, 2=Tail).
308:     fn truncation_mode(self, m: u8) -> Modified<Self, TruncationMode> {
309:         self.modifier(TruncationMode(m))
310:     }
311: 
312:     /// Chain `.offset(x, y)` — post-layout translation.
313:     fn offset(self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Modified<Self, Offset> {
314:         self.modifier(Offset { x, y })
315:     }
316: 
317:     /// Chain `.position(x, y)` — absolute placement within the parent.
318:     fn position(self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Modified<Self, Position> {
319:         self.modifier(Position { x, y })
320:     }
321: 
322:     /// Chain `.z_index(value)`.
323:     fn z_index(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, ZIndex> {
324:         self.modifier(ZIndex(value))
325:     }
326: }

328: impl<T: View> ViewExt for T {}

346: /// An sRGB color (`0xAARRGGBB`), with **dual identity** mirroring SwiftUI:
347: ///
348: /// - **View** — placing a `Color` in a layout tree draws a solid-color fill
349: ///   that is **layout-greedy** (expands to the available space unless a
350: ///   `.frame`/size modifier constrains it).
351: /// - **Data type** — a `Color` value is passed into style-taking modifiers
352: ///   (`.foreground_style`, `.background`, `.border`, `.tint`).
353: ///
354: /// There is deliberately **no** `.color()` / `.foregroundColor()` modifier.
355: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
356: pub struct Color(pub u32);

358: impl View for Color {
359:     fn build(&self) -> Node {
360:         let mut p = BTreeMap::new();
361:         p.insert(property_id::COLOR, self.0);
362:         plain_node(Component::Color, Vec::new(), p)
363:     }
364: }

366: /// Foreground color modifier (SwiftUI `.foregroundStyle`). There is no
367: /// `.color()` / `.foregroundColor()` modifier.
368: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
369: pub struct ForegroundStyle(pub Color);

371: /// Background color (a `Color` value).

373: pub struct Background(pub Color);
374: 
375: /// Accent/tint color (a `TINT` property).

377: pub struct Tint(pub Color);

379: /// The compound `frame` sizing modifier (SwiftUI `frame`).
380: ///
381: /// Emits `WIDTH`, `HEIGHT`, and optionally `ALIGNMENT` as ordinary
382: /// `SET_PROPERTY` values. `width`/`height` use the `size::FILL` (-1.0) and
383: /// `size::HUG_CONTENT` (-2.0) sentinels; `None` leaves that axis to the native
384: /// renderer.
385: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
386: pub struct Frame {
387:     pub width: Option<f32>,
388:     pub height: Option<f32>,
389:     pub alignment: Option<Align>,

392: /// Declares which raw pointer events a view wants reported (the `EVENT_LISTENERS`
393: /// u32 bitmask, e.g. `listener::POINTER_DOWN | listener::POINTER_UP`). Applies to
394: /// any view; the renderer attaches native input recognition for the requested
395: /// events.

399: /// A tap-gesture modifier (SwiftUI `onTapGesture`). Declares the pointer
400: /// down/up listeners and stores the app-side callback in the node's gesture

403: pub struct TapGesture(Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>);

405: impl PartialEq for TapGesture {

433:     }
434: }

436: impl ViewModifier for ForegroundStyle {
437:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
438:         node.properties.insert(property_id::COLOR, self.0 .0);
439:     }
440: }
441: 
442: impl ViewModifier for Background {
443:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
444:         node.properties.insert(property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR, self.0 .0);
445:     }
446: }

448: impl ViewModifier for Tint {
449:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {

452: }

454: impl ViewModifier for Frame {
455:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
456:         if let Some(w) = self.width {
457:             node.properties
458:                 .insert(property_id::WIDTH, w.to_bits());
459:         }
460:         if let Some(h) = self.height {
461:             node.properties
462:                 .insert(property_id::HEIGHT, h.to_bits());
463:         }
464:         if let Some(a) = self.alignment {
465:             node.properties
466:                 .insert(property_id::ALIGNMENT, (a.value() as f32).to_bits());
467:         }
468:     }
469: }
470: 
471: impl ViewModifier for PointerEvents {
472:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
473:         // OR into any existing mask so multiple modifiers compose.
474:         let existing = node
475:             .properties
476:             .get(&property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS)
477:             .copied()
478:             .unwrap_or(0);
479:         node.properties
480:             .insert(property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS, existing | self.0);
481:     }
482: }
483: 
484: impl ViewModifier for TapGesture {
485:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
486:         // Declare the raw pointer listeners the renderer must attach, then store
487:         // the callback in the app-side gesture list.
488:         let existing = node
489:             .properties
490:             .get(&property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS)
491:             .copied()
492:             .unwrap_or(0);
493:         node.properties.insert(
494:             property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS,
495:             existing
496:                 | pathland_core::listener::POINTER_DOWN
497:                 | pathland_core::listener::POINTER_UP,
498:         );
499:         node.gestures.push(Gesture::Tap(self.0.clone()));
500:     }
501: }

I've studied the Java DSL (`View.java` factories + modifiers), the Rust DSL (`pathland-view`), the signal model (`Signals`/`WritableSignal`/`State`), and both companion specs. Here's my proposed plan for `spec/DSL.md`.

## Plan: `spec/DSL.md` — the DSL authoring contract

A companion spec that defines the **authoring surface** (what an app developer writes) on top of the protocol surface (`PRIMITIVES.md` = components, `MODIFIERS.md` = properties, `EVENTS.md` = events). Its job: an AI can read it and emit a conformant Pathland DSL in any language.

**Guiding stance** (from your emphasis):
- **SwiftUI-shaped canonical syntax** — signatures mirror SwiftUI (`.foregroundStyle`, `.background(_:)`, `.border(_:width:)`, `.frame(width:height:alignment:)`, `Button { }`, `Toggle(_:isOn:)`, `Slider(value:in:)`, `TextField(_:text:)`).
- **Signals are the state model** — Angular-style `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`untracked`, `get()/set()/update()`, two-way binding = passing a `WritableSignal` into a control. Deliberate divergence from SwiftUI's `@State`/`@Binding`; the *view syntax* is SwiftUI, the *reactivity* is signals.
- **Java DSL is the reference implementation** — the spec captures its full surface but flags where its *syntax* diverges from SwiftUI (e.g. `View.text("x")` vs `Text("x")`, `View.hstack(...)` vs `HStack { }`, `View.button(label, action)` vs `Button(label) { }`, `View.slider(v,min,max,binding)` vs `Slider(value:in:)`, `.fontSize(28)` vs `.font(.system(size:))`).

**Proposed outline:**

1. **Purpose & relationship** — DSL.md vs the protocol specs; what "conformant DSL" means (same surface → same opcodes); per-language adaptation is allowed, protocol IDs are not.
2. **Design principles** (DSL-flavored recap) — declarative structure only; body evaluated **once** at mount; modifiers decoupled + "allowed and ignored"; constructor props = structural (spacing/alignment), modifiers = chainable; `Color` never a modifier; only changes emitted.
3. **State model (signals)** — the full signal contract + how binding drives fine-grained `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` and how host event routing (tap/text/value/date registries) writes back into signals; persisted `State<T>` keyed fields.
4. **The view surface** — canonical SwiftUI-shaped signature per view/control (the 3 protocol categories), each with protocol mapping links, plus the Java DSL's actual signature as the reference.
5. **The modifier surface** — grouped from `MODIFIERS.md`, each with canonical signature, emitted property(ies), value type.
6. **Authoring conventions** — naming/case rules, signature-order preservation, typed enums, `Spacer`/`Color` as views, environment scoping (`ButtonStyle` via `ScopedValue`, `PersistentState`).
7. **Generation contract for a new language** — required-surface checklist, signature→opcode mapping rules, language adaptation rules (trailing closures / macros / static factories), conformance = byte-identical emission vs `CONFORMANCE.md` vectors.
8. **Appendix A: SwiftUI ↔ DSL signature map** — `SwiftUI` snippet → canonical DSL → current Java DSL → current Rust DSL (the "what Java could move closer to" delta table).

1: # Pathland Core Events
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core events** the Pathland protocol supports.
12: Events are the **raw inputs** a renderer reports about the user's interaction —
13: pointer motion, keys, value changes, text edits, scroll. Only the **core
14: events** are specified here; **gestures** (tap, long-press, drag, magnify,
15: rotate) are explicitly **out of scope** and are composed application-side from
16: the raw pointer events (see [Deferred: gestures](#deferred-gestures)).
17: 
18: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
19: - Modifiers (properties): [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
20: - Wire format: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
21: 
22: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
23: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
24: > defines the protocol contract only.
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Event model
29: 
30: Events flow **host → guest**. The renderer is the producer; the app/engine is
31: the consumer. Both directions of the protocol are binary and share the same
32: 16-byte opcode format; events are `EVENT`-category (0x03) opcodes.
33: 
34: ### Who emits what
35: 
36: - The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
37:   writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
38: - The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its
39:   bound `State` signals (which in turn re-emit `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`
40:   deltas).
41: - The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
42:   wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
43:   bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
44:   (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.
45: 
46: ### Transport-aware event guards (MUST)
47: 
48: Renderers **MUST** implement event guards to prevent network noise. A user
49: interaction — tap, text change, drag, value edit — **MUST NEVER** produce an
50: outbound event opcode unless the target node explicitly declared intent in **at
51: least one** of these ways:
52: 
53: 1. it set the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) bits, **or**
54: 2. it is a **value-bearing control** reporting by component type (`SLIDER`,
55:    `TOGGLE`, `PICKER`, `MENU`, `DATE_PICKER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, …), **or**
56: 3. it carries a bound callback property — `ACTION_ID` (0x2016) or `BINDING_ID`
57:    (0x2017) — that identifies where the interaction must be routed.
58: 
59: Interactions that match none of these are **dropped at the renderer**; they are
60: never serialized to the event ring or a network batch. This is the wire-level
61: guard: a `Button` tap with no `ACTION_ID`, no `BINDING_ID`, and no
62: `EVENT_LISTENERS` produces no events.
63: 
64: ### Target resolution
65: 
66: The renderer resolves `targetId` from its own rendered-output tree (its
67: `id → native element` map): the event's position is hit-tested against that
68: tree to find the deepest node with the matching listener bit. If no listener is
69: declared, the event is not reported.
70: 
71: ### Transport paths
72: 
73: | Path | Mechanism |
74: |------|-----------|
75: | Shared memory (desktop/native) | The host writes `EVENT` opcodes into the event ring (host → guest) at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains at `eventReadCursor`. Events are consumed as written (no frame batching). |
76: | Network batch (SSR → browser) | Host → guest batches use the `0x0001` direction flag of the `PLPL` batch format (see OPCODE.md Transport) |
77: 
78: ### Encoding
79: 
80: Every event is a 16-byte opcode:
81: 
82: ```
83: [Category=0x03][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
84: ```
85: 
86: `TEXT_CHANGED` is the exception: its payload is an offset into the host → guest
87: event arena (shared memory) or the batch's string section (network), so it is
88: only fully decodable with that string source (the same convention as
89: `STYLE::SET_TEXT`).
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## Core event catalog
94: 
95: ### Pointer
96: 
97: Pointer events carry a viewport-relative point in **logical points** (`B`=x,
98: `C`=y, f32).
99: 
100: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
101: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
102: | `POINTER_DOWN` | 0x01 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | press (basis of `onTapGesture`, `Button` action) |
103: | `POINTER_MOVE` | 0x02 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` (0x0001) / `HOVER_LEAVE` (0x0002) | hover/enter/leave, drag basis |
104: | `POINTER_UP` | 0x03 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | release (basis of `onTapGesture`) |
105: 
106: - **Flags**:
107:   - `POINTER_SECONDARY`: the secondary button (right mouse, long-press) rather
108:     than the primary.
109:   - `HOVER_ENTER` (bit 0 of `POINTER_MOVE`): the pointer just entered the
110:     node's bounds (is now hovering). `HOVER_LEAVE` (bit 1): the pointer just
111:     left. A plain move has neither bit set.
112: - **Listener bits**: `POINTER_DOWN` (bit 0), `POINTER_MOVE` (bit 1),
113:   `POINTER_UP` (bit 2).
114: - **Renderer**: attaches native press/hover recognition to the matching native
115:   element when the listener bit is set. Multiple pointer events may be reported
116:   for one physical gesture (down → several moves → up), all for the same
117:   `targetId` while the pointer stays over the node.
118: 
119: ### Keyboard
120: 
121: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
122: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
123: | `KEY_DOWN` | 0x04 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` (0x0002) | `onKeyPress(.down)` |
124: | `KEY_UP` | 0x05 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | `onKeyPress(.up)` |
125: 
126: - **`keyCode`**: a **canonical, platform-independent logical key code** (a
127:   renderer maps native scancodes/key-codes onto this canonical set). The
128:   canonical set (letters/digits/arrows/Enter/Tab/…) is renderer-shared and
129:   documented in the conformance vectors.
130: - **`modifiers`**: u8 bitmask — `Shift`=0x01, `Control`=0x02, `Alt`=0x04,
131:   `Meta/Super`=0x08.
132: - **`KEY_REPEAT`**: bit 1 of flags; set when the key is an OS auto-repeat.
133: - **Listener bits**: `KEY_DOWN` (bit 3), `KEY_UP` (bit 4).
134: - **Focus**: keyboard events are reported to the focused node (the node that
135:   most recently gained focus), or to the node that declared the listener and
136:   has keyboard focus. See `FOCUS_CHANGED` below.
137: 
138: ### Value
139: 
140: Value events carry a control's semantic value, resolved by the renderer from
141: its own native control geometry.
142: 
143: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
144: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
145: | `VALUE_CHANGED` | 0x06 | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`Toggle`/`Picker`/`Menu` binding changes |
146: 
147: - **Semantics per control** (see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) controls):
148:   - `SLIDER`/`STEPPER`/`GAUGE` — the numeric value in the control's range.
149:   - `TOGGLE` — 0/1 (checked state; the same value the app writes to
150:     `SELECTED`).
151:   - `PICKER`/`MENU` — the selected option/action-item index.
152:   - `COLOR_PICKER` — the packed `0xAARRGGBB` color reinterpreted as an f32 bit
153:     pattern.
154:   - `DATE_PICKER` uses the dedicated `DATE_CHANGED` event below (its value is
155:     two fields and does not fit `VALUE_CHANGED`).
156: - The app writes the received value into its bound `State`; the engine's
157:   signal flush re-emits the `SET_PROPERTY` delta back to the renderer (the
158:   renderer reflects its own native control).
159: - **No listener bit**: value-bearing controls are reported by the renderer by
160:   virtue of their component type, but still gated by the transport-aware event
161:   guards (a control without `BINDING_ID` reports nothing). The renderer owns
162:   the gesture (e.g. slider drag) that produces them.
163: 
164: ### Date
165: 
166: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
167: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
168: | `DATE_CHANGED` | 0x0D | targetId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | `DatePicker` value binding |
169: 
170: - The date is encoded as two 32-bit fields — `B` = **days since epoch**
171:   (signed I32; pre-1970 is negative) and `C` = **millis of day** (U32,
172:   0..86,400,000) — matching the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (OPCODE.md). No
173:   string/arena indirection: the event is fully inline. It works over the
174:   shared-memory ring today and will use the same inline encoding for host →
175:   guest network batches once that direction lands (see OPCODE.md Transport).
176: - **No listener bit**: like `VALUE_CHANGED`, reported by virtue of the
177:   component type.
178: 
179: ### Text
180: 
181: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
182: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
183: | `TEXT_CHANGED` | 0x07 | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | `TextField` value binding |
184: | `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 0x08 | targetId | focused (0/1) | 0 | — | `@FocusState` |
185: | `EDITING_CHANGED` | 0x09 | targetId | editing (0/1) | 0 | — | `TextField`/`Slider` `onEditingChanged` |
186: | `SUBMIT` | 0x0A | targetId | 0 | 0 | — | `TextField` `onSubmit` / `onCommit` |
187: 
188: - **`TEXT_CHANGED`**: the new text is a length-prefixed entry
189:   (`[u32 byteLength][bytes…]`). Over the **shared-memory ring** the renderer
190:   bump-allocates it into the host-owned **event arena** and `B` is its absolute
191:   offset (see OPCODE.md); over the **network** it lives in the batch's string
192:   section referenced by a *relative* `B` offset — exactly the `STYLE::SET_TEXT`
193:   dual convention. A bare opcode cannot resolve the text; batch-aware decoders
194:   (`pathland-core-transport`, Java `FrameCodec`, TS `decoder.ts`) resolve it.
195:   The event is reported on **every** edit, including intermediate edits, not
196:   only on commit.
197: - **`FOCUS_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 gained focus, 0 lost focus. The renderer reports
198:   it for nodes that declared the `FOCUS` listener bit (bit 5). Focus is what
199:   routes subsequent `KEY_*` events.
200: - **`EDITING_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 editing session began, 0 ended. Reported for
201:   nodes that declared the `EDITING` listener bit (bit 6).
202: - **`SUBMIT`**: the user committed the field (Enter). Reported for nodes that
203:   declared the `SUBMIT` listener bit (bit 7). `B` MAY carry the current text as
204:   a string-section offset (reserved for future use; 0 today).
205: 
206: ### Scroll
207: 
208: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
209: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
210: | `SCROLL` | 0x0B | targetId | offsetX (f32) | offsetY (f32) | — | `ScrollView` offset, `onScrollPhaseChange` |
211: | `WHEEL` | 0x0C | targetId | deltaX (f32) | deltaY (f32) | — | `onScrollWheelEvent` / trackpad |
212: 
213: - **`SCROLL`**: the content offset of a `SCROLLVIEW` (logical points), reported
214:   for nodes that declared the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8). The renderer
215:   reports the absolute offset after each scroll delta.
216: - **`WHEEL`**: raw wheel/trackpad deltas (logical points), reported for nodes
217:   that declared the `WHEEL` listener bit (bit 9). Renderers map native scroll
218:   deltas (GTK `GtkEventControllerScroll`, DOM `wheel`) onto x/y deltas.
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: ## Event listeners (`EVENT_LISTENERS`)
223: 
224: `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) is a u32 bitmask set via `SET_PROPERTY` (U32). Each
225: bit requests one raw-input event kind for the node:
226: 
227: | Bit | Mask | Event |
228: | ----- | ------ | ------- |
229: | 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` |
230: | 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` (incl. hover enter/leave) |
231: | 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` |
232: | 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` |
233: | 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` |
234: | 5 | `0x00000020` | `FOCUS_CHANGED` |
235: | 6 | `0x00000040` | `EDITING_CHANGED` |
236: | 7 | `0x00000080` | `SUBMIT` |
237: | 8 | `0x00000100` | `SCROLL` |
238: | 9 | `0x00000200` | `WHEEL` |
239: | 10–31 | — | reserved |
240: 
241: Convenience aliases (DSL-side): `POINTER = bits 0|1|2`.
242: 
243: DSL surfaces:
244: 
245: - Rust: `pathland_view::pointer_events(mask)` modifier + `listener::*` bits;
246:   `on_tap_gesture` sets `POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_UP`.
247: - Java: `TapGestureView` / `EVENT_LISTENERS` via the emitter; host forwards raw
248:   `EVENT` batches into bound `State` signals.
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## Deferred: gestures
253: 
254: SwiftUI gestures — `onTapGesture`, `onLongPressGesture`, `DragGesture`,
255: `MagnifyGesture`, `RotateGesture` — are **not protocol events**. Per the
256: protocol's raw-inputs-only rule, they are **composed application-side** from
257: the raw `POINTER_*` / `KEY_*` events above:
258: 
259: - **Tap** = `POINTER_DOWN` then `POINTER_UP` on the same `targetId` within the
260:   platform's tap window.
261: - **Long-press** = `POINTER_DOWN` held past a threshold.
262: - **Drag** = `POINTER_DOWN` + `POINTER_MOVE` sequence.
263: - **Magnify / rotate** = multi-pointer deltas; the underlying raw events are
264:   `POINTER_*` (multi-touch reported per pointer).
265: 
266: A future "gesture recognition" layer MAY define app-side recognizers, but the
267: wire protocol will never carry interpreted gestures — only raw inputs.
268: 
269: ---
270: 
271: ## Reserved event command IDs
272: 
273: | Range | Use |
274: |-------|-----|
275: | `0x01`–`0x0D` | Core events (allocated, this file) |
276: | `0x0E`–`0x3F` | Future core events (unallocated) |
277: | `0x40`–`0xFF` | Custom/application events |
278: 
279: A renderer/decoder MUST skip unknown event commands and continue.
280: 
281: ---
282: 
283: ## Conformance
284: 
285: Event encode/decode round-trips and golden byte vectors (incl. raw-input
286: `EVENT` and network-batch bytes) live in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).
287: New events added here MUST add vectors before implementation.

# Pathland DSL Authoring Contract

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** August 30, 2026

---

## Purpose

This document defines the **authoring surface** — the SwiftUI-shaped DSL an
application developer writes — for every Pathland implementation. Where
[PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md), [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md), and
[EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) describe the **wire surface** (component types,
property ids, events, opcodes), this file describes the **surface in source
code**: how views, controls, modifiers, and state are *named*, *ordered*, and
*composed* so that any language can expose a conformant, idiomatic DSL.

A DSL in a new language is **conformant** when it:

1. exposes the full surface catalogued here (views, controls, modifiers,
   signals, state);
2. maps every DSL element to the exact protocol component/property/event
   documented in the companion specs (no re-interpretation, no reallocation);
3. produces **byte-identical opcode output** for the same source tree as the
   reference implementations (see the [Generation
   contract](#8-generation-contract-for-a-new-language)).

### Relationship to the other specs

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format: categories, commands, 16-byte opcode layout, ring/arena, value types |
| [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | Which **views/nodes** exist and their component ids |
| [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | Which **modifiers** (properties) exist and how they encode |
| [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | Which **core events** (raw inputs) exist and how they encode |
| [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden byte vectors |
| **DSL.md** (this file) | How an application **author** composes those into source code |

> **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
> in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. The Java DSL
> (`com.pathland.view`) and the Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) are the two reference
> realizations and are cited here by their **current signatures**; where they
> diverge from the canonical form below, that divergence is noted as a *delta*,
> and [§7](#7-java-convergence-proposal) proposes how the Java DSL converges.
> This document defines the contract only.

### Two guiding rules

1. **Stay as close to SwiftUI as possible.** View names, modifier names, and
   signature shapes mirror SwiftUI. Adapt only where the host language forces
   it (Rust snake_case + macros; Java camelCase + static factories), and never
   in a way that reorders or renames the canonical parameters.
2. **State variables are signals.** Pathland does **not** use SwiftUI's
   `@State`/`@Binding` property wrappers. The view syntax is SwiftUI; the
   reactivity model is Angular-style signals (writable signals, computeds,
   effects, two-way bindings). A generated DSL MUST expose the signal surface
   of [§3](#3-state-model-signals).

---

## 1. Design principles (DSL-flavored)

These recap the protocol's non-negotiables in author-facing terms. A conformant
DSL must be *shaped* by them:

- **Declarative structure, never positions.** The DSL expresses `WHAT` — a
  `VStack`, a `HStack`, a `Text` — and constraint properties (spacing, padding,
  alignment, size hints). It never computes bounds and never emits rects.
- **`body()` is evaluated once at mount.** A composite view declares its
  subtree once; reactivity comes from **signals**, never from re-evaluating the
  body. This is what lets the emitter produce fine-grained
  `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` deltas instead of rebuilding the tree.
- **Modifiers are decoupled from views.** Any modifier applies to any view
  (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a `VStack` alike). A modifier a given
  renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** — the property is still
  emitted.
- **Constructor properties vs modifiers.** Structural/layout parameters
  (`alignment`, `spacing`) are **constructor arguments**, never chainable.
  Everything decorative (padding, color, font, frame, border, …) is a
  **chainable modifier**. There is no standalone width/height — use the
  compound `frame` modifier.
- **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` has SwiftUI's dual identity: it is a
  **View** (a layout-greedy solid-color fill) and a **Data Type** (passed into
  style-taking modifiers: `.foregroundStyle`, `.background`, `.border`,
  `.tint`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier, and `.foregroundColor(_:)` is
  deprecated — foreground styling is always `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
- **Only changes are transmitted.** Emission is diff-based; an unchanged tree
  emits **zero** opcodes. The DSL describes values; the emitter diffs them.
- **Typed enums, never raw ints.** Every enumerated value is a typed constant
  (`Alignment.leading`, `FontWeight.bold`, `ToggleStyle.checkbox`), not a bare
  integer. The numeric code is the DSL's job to resolve (see the value-type and
  enum tables in MODIFIERS.md).

---

## 2. Canonical signature notation

The canonical signatures below are written SwiftUI-shaped and language
agnostic. Conventions used:

- `T("…")` / `View("…")` — a view/control constructor.
- `{ ... }` — the child subtree (a trailing closure in SwiftUI; a vararg,
  macro, builder, or lambda in other languages).
- `Signal<T>` — a read-only derived or writable signal; `WritableSignal<T>` —
  a two-way binding target. A control takes a `WritableSignal<T>` for its
  value (see [§3](#3-state-model-signals)).
- `()` — the action a `Button` fires.
- Modifiers chain as `.name(args)` on any view and are applied
  **innermost-first** (the last chained modifier's property wins).

Per-language adaptation rules:

| Language | Case | Composition mechanism | Example |
|----------|------|-----------------------|---------|
| SwiftUI | `camelCase` | trailing closures + result builder | `VStack { Text("x").padding() }` |
| Java (`com.pathland.view`) | `camelCase` | static factories + varargs + chainable default methods | `View.vstack(View.text("x").padding(16))` |
| Rust (`pathland-view`) | `snake_case` | macros + free functions + chainable trait methods | `vstack![text("x").padding(16.0)]` |

---

## 3. State model (signals)

Pathland state is **Angular-style signals**. This is the non-negotiable
reactive core every DSL exposes.

### 3.1 Signal surface

| Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view.signal`) | Semantics |
|-----------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
| `signal(initial)` | `Signals.signal(T)` | a writable signal |
| `signal(name, initial)` | `Signals.signal(String, T)` | named (names surface in dependency errors) |
| `signal(initial, equal)` | `Signals.signal(T, BiPredicate<T,T>)` | custom equality |
| `computed(fn)` | `Signals.computed(Supplier<T>)` | lazy, memoized derived signal |
| `effect(fn)` | `Signals.effect(Runnable)` | runs immediately, then on dependency change |
| `untracked(fn)` | `Signals.untracked(Supplier<T>)` | reads without recording dependencies |
| `read()` | `get()` | current value |
| `write(v)` | `set(T)` | replace (no-op when equal) |
| `update(fn)` | `update(UnaryOperator<T>)` | derive from current and write |
| `asReadonly()` | `asReadonly()` | read-only view of a writable signal |

**Guarantees** (must be preserved by any implementation): equality suppression,
synchronous flush at the end of the outermost write, glitch-free propagation
(each computed recomputes at most once per flush), error caching, write
discipline, and circular-dependency detection.

### 3.2 Two-way binding

A control's value is **a `WritableSignal<T>` passed to its constructor**:
`TextField(placeholder, writable)`, `Toggle(label, isOn: writable)`,
`Slider(value: writable, in: min...max)`. The flow:

1. At **mount**, the DSL control records a **value input** (a sink on the
   retained node) for the signal, and the emitter exposes routing registries to
   the host: tap actions, text inputs, value inputs, date inputs.
2. The host receives the control's raw event (`TEXT_CHANGED`,
   `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED`, or a composed tap) and calls the sink,
   which **writes into the signal**.
3. The signal flush re-emits **only that node's** delta (`SET_TEXT`,
   `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_DATE`) back through the emitter.

Reading is equally fine-grained: a node's text or a property can be **bound to
a signal** (`Text(signal)`, `.foregroundStyle(signal)`, `.fontSize(signal)`),
so a change re-emits only the bound node.

### 3.3 Persisted state (`State<T>`)

A `State<T>` field is the SwiftUI-`@State`-shaped form of a persisted signal,
**auto-wired by key**:

```java
State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);            // key = field name "count"
State<Integer> total = new State<>(0, "total");   // explicit store key
count.get(); count.set(0); count.update(v -> v + 1);
count.signal();                                   // the WritableSignal (for TextField, …)
```

The store (`StateStore`) is untyped and platform-neutral (in-memory, Redis,
file, SQLite, LocalStorage, NVS flash). The Java realization wires `State`
fields via an annotation processor that generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per
view class; connection happens when the view renders. A generated DSL in a
language without reflection/annotation processing MUST offer the equivalent
explicit wiring.

---

## 4. View surface

Component ids and wire behavior come from
[PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md); the tables here give the **DSL signature**.
`Java DSL (current)` is the reference realization today.

### 4.1 Primitive drawing & visual nodes

| View | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
|------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
| `Text` | `Text("…")` / `Text(Signal<String>)` | `View.text(String)` / `View.text(Signal<String>)` | `TEXT` 0x01; content `SET_TEXT` |
| `Image` | `Image("name")` / `Image(systemName:)` | `View.image()` / `View.image(String source)` | `IMAGE` 0x02; `IMAGE_SOURCE` 0x1002 |
| `Color` | `Color(.sRGB, red:green:blue:)` (a View) | `Color.rgb(int,int,int)` (implements `View`) | `COLOR` 0x03; `COLOR` 0x100A |
| `Shape` | `Rectangle()`, `Circle()`, `Capsule()`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:)` | `View.rectangle()` | `SHAPE` 0x04; `SHAPE_KIND` 0x0006 |
| `Divider` | `Divider()` | `View.divider()` | `DIVIDER` 0x05 |
| `Spacer` | `Spacer()` | `View.spacer()` | `SPACER` 0x06 |
| `ProgressView` | `ProgressView(value:)` / `ProgressView()` | `View.progressView(float)` / `View.progressView()` | `PROGRESS_VIEW` 0x07; `PROGRESS` 0x200E / `IS_INDETERMINATE` 0x200F |
| `Gauge` | `Gauge(value:in:)` | `View.gauge(float value, float min, float max)` | `GAUGE` 0x08; `VALUE`/`MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE` |

**Deltas (Java)**: primitives are constructed via the `View.` static factory
(`View.text("…")`) rather than direct construction (`Text("…")`). Shape kinds
other than `Rectangle` are not exposed as named constructors in the Java DSL
today (only `View.rectangle()`); the canonical form exposes the full
`ShapeKind` set.

### 4.2 Layout & container nodes

| View | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
|------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
| `VStack` | `VStack(alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `View.vstack(View...)` / `View.vstack(Alignment, float, View...)` | `VSTACK` 0x10; `SPACING` 0x0001, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002, `CONTENT_MARGINS` 0x0005 |
| `HStack` | `HStack(alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `View.hstack(View...)` / `View.hstack(Alignment, float, View...)` | `HSTACK` 0x11 |
| `ZStack` | `ZStack(alignment:) { … }` | `View.zstack(View...)` | `ZSTACK` 0x12; `ALIGNMENT` |
| `Grid` | `Grid(alignment:horizontalSpacing:verticalSpacing:) { … }` | `View.grid(View...)` | `GRID` 0x13 |
| `ScrollView` | `ScrollView { … }` | `View.scrollView(View...)` | `SCROLLVIEW` 0x14 |
| `LazyVGrid` | `LazyVGrid(columns:alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `View.lazyVGrid(View...)` | `LAZY_VGRID` 0x15 |
| `LazyHGrid` | `LazyHGrid(rows:alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `View.lazyHGrid(View...)` | `LAZY_HGRID` 0x16 |
| `LazyVStack` | `LazyVStack(alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `View.lazyVStack(View...)` | `LAZY_VSTACK` 0x1B |
| `LazyHStack` | `LazyHStack(alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `View.lazyHStack(View...)` | `LAZY_HSTACK` 0x1C |

**Deltas (Java)**: stacks are constructed with the `View.vstack(...)` factory
using varargs (`View.vstack(children...)`), not a builder/trailing-closure
block. Constructor layout properties come as a separate overload
(`View.vstack(Alignment, float, View...)`). The canonical SwiftUI form passes
`alignment`/`spacing` as labeled constructor arguments inside the braces' call.

### 4.3 Semantic controls

Two-way value controls bind a `WritableSignal`. Actions bind a callback.

| Control | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
|---------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
| `Button` | `Button("title", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `View.button(String, Runnable)` / `View.button(View, Runnable)` | `BUTTON` 0x20; tap = composed `POINTER_DOWN`+`POINTER_UP` |
| `TextField` | `TextField("placeholder", text: writable)` | `View.textField(String, WritableSignal<String>)` | `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21; `TEXT_CHANGED` → text input |
| `SecureField` | `SecureField("…", text: writable)` | (secure via `IS_SECURE` token) | `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21 + `IS_SECURE` 0x200D |
| `TextEditor` | `TextEditor(text: writable)` | `View.textEditor(WritableSignal<String>)` | `TEXT_EDITOR` 0x22 |
| `Toggle` | `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `View.toggle(boolean, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` / `View.toggle(ToggleStyle, boolean, WritableSignal<Boolean>, String)` | `TOGGLE` 0x24; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input; `TOGGLE_STYLE` 0x2018 |
| `Slider` | `Slider(value: writable, in: min...max)` | `View.slider(float value, float min, float max, WritableSignal<Float>)` | `SLIDER` 0x25; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input |
| `Stepper` | `Stepper("label", value: writable, in: min...max, step:)` | `View.stepper(float, float, float, float, WritableSignal<Float>)` | `STEPPER` 0x26; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input |
| `DatePicker` | `DatePicker("label", selection: writable, displayedComponents:)` | `View.datePicker(DatePickerMode, WritableSignal<Integer>)` | `DATE_PICKER` 0x27; `DATE_CHANGED` → date input; value via `STYLE::SET_DATE` |
| `Picker` | `Picker("label", selection: writable) { options }` | `View.picker(PickerStyle, WritableSignal<Integer>, View... options)` | `PICKER` 0x28; `VALUE_CHANGED` (index) → value input |
| `Menu` | `Menu { actions } label: { trigger }` | `View.menu(View trigger, View... actions)` / `View.menu(View, WritableSignal<Integer>, View...)` | `MENU` 0x29; `VALUE_CHANGED` (item index) → value input |
| `ColorPicker` | `ColorPicker("label", selection: writable)` | `View.colorPicker(WritableSignal<Color>)` | `COLOR_PICKER` 0x2A; `VALUE_CHANGED` (packed `0xAARRGGBB` as f32) → value input |

**Deltas (Java)**: the value binding is a positional constructor argument
(`View.slider(value, min, max, binding)`) instead of SwiftUI's labeled
`value:in:` range binding. `Button` takes a `(label, action)` pair rather than
SwiftUI's `Button("title") { action }` trailing-action form. `Toggle` takes
`(style, selected, binding, label)` positionally; `DatePicker` binds
**days-since-epoch** (`WritableSignal<Integer>`) rather than a date object —
the protocol's `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` two-field encoding is
days + millis-of-day (see [§7](#7-java-convergence-proposal)).

**Control guarantees** (from PRIMITIVES.md): a control without children renders
in **Native Token Mode** (native OS control); a control with a child subtree
renders in **Composite Override Mode** (custom chrome wrapped with native
gesture semantics). Renderers MUST gate value/text/date events by
`BINDING_ID`, `ACTION_ID`, or the `EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask (transport-aware
event guards) — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md).

### 4.4 Gestures

| Gesture | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Rust DSL (current) |
|---------|---------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| tap | `.onTapGesture { action }` | `.onTapGesture(Runnable)` | `.on_tap_gesture(f)` |
| raw pointer | `.gesture` composition from raw inputs | `.pointerEvents(int mask)` | `.pointer_events(u32 mask)` |

Tap is **not** a protocol event: it is composed app-side from `POINTER_DOWN`
then `POINTER_UP` on the same target (`EVENT_LISTENERS` bits 0|2). The DSL's
`.onTapGesture` declares those listeners and records the action; the host
routes the recognized tap via the emitter's tap-action registry.

## 5. Modifier surface

Properties, value types, and emission rules come from
[MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md); the tables here give the **DSL signature**. A
compound SwiftUI modifier expands to **one `SET_PROPERTY` per underlying
property** (`.frame` → `WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` + `ALIGNMENT`; `.border` →
`BORDER_COLOR` + `BORDER_WIDTH`; `.shadow` → `SHADOW_COLOR` + `SHADOW_RADIUS` +
`SHADOW_X` + `SHADOW_Y`). `Java DSL (current)` is the reference realization.

## 6. Authoring conventions

A conformant DSL follows these conventions:

1. **Names**: SwiftUI view/modifier names; per-language case (camelCase,
   snake_case). `foregroundStyle` not `foregroundColor`; `fontWeight`,
   `multilineTextAlignment`, `scaledToFit`, `allowsHitTesting` keep their
   SwiftUI spellings.
2. **Signature order**: canonical parameter order is preserved —
   `.border(color, width)`, `.frame(width, height, alignment)`,
   `.shadow(color, radius, x, y)`. Compound modifiers expand to one property
   per argument.
3. **Constructor vs modifier**: structural (alignment, spacing) in the
   constructor; everything else chainable.
4. **Typed enums**: `Alignment` (leading/center/trailing/fill),
   `TextAlignment`, `FontWeight` (100–900), `Truncation` (head/middle/tail),
   `TextCase` (none/uppercase/lowercase), `FontStyle` (normal/italic),
   `FontDesign` (default/serif/rounded/monospaced), `ContentMode` (fit/fill),
   `ControlSize` (small/regular/large), `ToggleStyle`
   (switch/checkbox/button), `PickerStyle` (menu/segmented/wheel/radiogroup),
   `DatePickerMode` (date/time/dateAndTime), `ShapeKind`
   (circle/rectangle/roundedRectangle/capsule/ellipse/path). Numeric codes
   come from MODIFIERS.md's appendix; the DSL resolves them.
5. **`Spacer`/`Color` as views**: `Spacer()` is a flexible expanding filler;
   `Color(...)` in a tree is a layout-greedy fill.
6. **Environment scoping**: styles and state that must reach a whole subtree
   (`ButtonStyle`, the session's persisted state) are injected via the
   environment (Java: `ScopedValue`), never threaded through constructors.
7. **Reactivity discipline**: `body()` is evaluated once; a signal read during
   mount records a dependency; a later write re-emits only the bound node.
   Never mutate signals during mount.
8. **Emission contract**: each DSL call emits exactly the documented
   properties with the documented value types; the emitter diffs. The DSL never
   computes layout, never positions, never serializes full trees.

## 7. Java convergence proposal

The Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) has the complete surface; its *syntax*
drifts from the canonical SwiftUI shape. This section proposes convergence as a
future workstream (out of scope for this document's landing). It is a
**proposal** — the canonical contract is defined in [§4](#4-view-surface) and
[§5](#5-modifier-surface), not here.

| Canonical | Java today | Proposed Java (SwiftUI-closer) |
|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------|
| `Text("…")` | `View.text("…")` | `new Text("…")` (direct construction; keep `View.text` as a factory alias) |
| `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `View.button(String, Runnable)` | `Button.of("…", () -> …)`; a `Button(String)` + `Button(View, Runnable)` mirroring `Button(title, action)` |
| `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `View.toggle(boolean, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` | labeled params or an overload `Toggle.of(String label, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` |
| `Slider(value: in:)` | `View.slider(value, min, max, binding)` | `Slider.of(binding, min, max)` keeping positional order: binding first |
| `.border(color, width)` | `.border(width, color, radius)` | add `.border(Color, float)`; keep `(width, color, radius)` as the corner-radius convenience |
| `DatePicker(selection:)` | `View.datePicker(DatePickerMode, WritableSignal<Integer>)` | keep days-since-epoch binding; optionally add a `Date`-shaped wrapper that encodes days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` |

Guidance for the proposal:

- Prefer **additive overloads/aliases** over breaking changes; keep the
  existing factory names working so application code (the demos) migrates
  incrementally.
- Add a `SwiftUIShape`-style named constructor for each `ShapeKind`
  (`Circle.of()`, `Capsule.of()`, `RoundedRectangle.of(cornerRadius:)`) to
  match the canonical view set.
- Consider a `ButtonStyle`/`environment` path that lets the trailing-action
  form (`Button(label) { action }`) read the action from the environment, if a
  Java-idiomatic trailing lambda is desirable.
- Land the convergence only after the DSL.md surface is stable, and update
  `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` in the same change.

## 8. Generation contract for a new language

An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
are the companion specs.

### 8.1 Required surface

- [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
  `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
  `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
  `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
- [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), chainable on
  any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument.
- [ ] **Signals** — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `get`/`set`/`update`/`asReadonly`, with equality suppression, synchronous
  flush, glitch-free propagation, error caching, write discipline, circular
  detection ([§3.1](#31-signal-surface)).
- [ ] **Two-way bindings** — every value control takes a writable signal and
  exposes a sink the host routes its event into ([§3.2](#32-two-way-binding)).
- [ ] **Persisted state** — `State<T>` keyed fields (or the language's
  equivalent wiring) against a platform-neutral store ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)).
- [ ] **Gestures** — `.onTapGesture` (composed from raw pointer down/up) and
  raw `pointerEvents`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask ([§4.4](#44-gestures)).

### 8.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)

1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
   Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
   never reuse allocated ids.
2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
   with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
   DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
   appendix.
3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`.
4. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` sentinels: `FILL` = −1.0, `HUG_CONTENT` = −2.0.
5. `DatePicker` value/event use the two-field encoding **days since epoch
   (I32) + millis of day (U32)**; there is no `DATE_VALUE` property.
6. Value/text/date events are gated by the transport-aware event guards; the
   DSL's controls emit the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` that
   declare intent.
7. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**: the DSL describes values, the
   emitter diffs. A generated DSL must keep the retained tree + emitter
   separation; it must not hand-serialize full trees.

### 8.3 Language adaptation rules

| SwiftUI mechanism | Adapt as |
|-------------------|----------|
| trailing closure / result builder for children | varargs (Java), macros (Rust), builders/block (C#/Kotlin), element list (any) |
| `Binding<T>` (Swift) | `WritableSignal<T>` (always — signals are the model, never property wrappers) |
| `some View` opaque return | the language's `View` interface/trait (Java `View`, Rust `View` trait) |
| `@State`/`@Binding` property wrappers | signals + persisted `State<T>` ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)) |
| labeled parameters | named params where the language has them; otherwise preserve **parameter order** and document labels |
| method chaining for modifiers | default methods (Java), extension traits (Rust), extension methods (C#/Kotlin) |

### 8.4 Conformance recipe

A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
reference implementations:

1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new
   DSL's test harness; assert byte-identical `TREE`/`STYLE`/`EVENT`/`META`
   opcodes for each canonical element.
2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
   deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,
   `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` write into the bound signal).
3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
   language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
   steady-state emission).
4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md
   (the specs are the source of truth, never the reference code).

**Reference implementations to read**: Java — `lib/java/pathland-view`
(`com.pathland.view`, `com.pathland.view.signal`, `com.pathland.view.state`,
`com.pathland.view.emit`); Rust — `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view` +
`pathland-engine` + `pathland-core::signal`.
