1: # Pathland DSL Authoring Contract
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 30, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document defines the **authoring surface** — the SwiftUI-shaped DSL an
12: application developer writes — for every Pathland implementation. Where
13: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md), [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md), and
14: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) describe the **wire surface** (component types,
15: property ids, events, opcodes), this file describes the **surface in source
16: code**: how views, controls, modifiers, and state are *named*, *ordered*, and
17: *composed* so that any language can expose a conformant, idiomatic DSL.
18: 
19: A DSL in a new language is **conformant** when it:
20: 
21: 1. exposes the full surface catalogued here (views, controls, modifiers,
22:    signals, state);
23: 2. maps every DSL element to the exact protocol component/property/event
24:    documented in the companion specs (no re-interpretation, no reallocation);
25: 3. produces **byte-identical opcode output** for the same source tree as the
26:    reference implementations (see the [Generation
27:    contract](#8-generation-contract-for-a-new-language)).
28: 
29: ### Relationship to the other specs
30: 
31: | File | Role |
32: |------|------|
33: | [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format: categories, commands, 16-byte opcode layout, ring/arena, value types |
34: | [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | Which **views/nodes** exist and their component ids |
35: | [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | Which **modifiers** (properties) exist and how they encode |
36: | [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | Which **core events** (raw inputs) exist and how they encode |
37: | [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden byte vectors |
38: | **DSL.md** (this file) | How an application **author** composes those into source code |
39: 
40: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
41: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. The Java DSL
42: > (`com.pathland.view`) and the Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) are the two reference
43: > realizations and are cited here by their **current signatures**; where they
44: > diverge from the canonical form below, that divergence is noted as a *delta*,
45: > and [§7](#7-java-convergence-proposal) proposes how the Java DSL converges.
46: > This document defines the contract only.
47: 
48: ### Two guiding rules
49: 
50: 1. **Stay as close to SwiftUI as possible.** View names, modifier names, and
51:    signature shapes mirror SwiftUI. Adapt only where the host language forces
52:    it (Rust snake_case + macros; Java camelCase + static factories), and never
53:    in a way that reorders or renames the canonical parameters.
54: 2. **State variables are signals.** Pathland does **not** use SwiftUI's
55:    `@State`/`@Binding` property wrappers. The view syntax is SwiftUI; the
56:    reactivity model is Angular-style signals (writable signals, computeds,
57:    effects, two-way bindings). A generated DSL MUST expose the signal surface
58:    of [§3](#3-state-model-signals).
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 1. Design principles (DSL-flavored)
63: 
64: These recap the protocol's non-negotiables in author-facing terms. A conformant
65: DSL must be *shaped* by them:
66: 
67: - **Declarative structure, never positions.** The DSL expresses `WHAT` — a
68:   `VStack`, a `HStack`, a `Text` — and constraint properties (spacing, padding,
69:   alignment, size hints). It never computes bounds and never emits rects.
70: - **`body()` is evaluated once at mount.** A composite view declares its
71:   subtree once; reactivity comes from **signals**, never from re-evaluating the
72:   body. This is what lets the emitter produce fine-grained
73:   `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` deltas instead of rebuilding the tree.
74: - **Modifiers are decoupled from views.** Any modifier applies to any view
75:   (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a `VStack` alike). A modifier a given
76:   renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** — the property is still
77:   emitted.
78: - **Constructor properties vs modifiers.** Structural/layout parameters
79:   (`alignment`, `spacing`) are **constructor arguments**, never chainable.
80:   Everything decorative (padding, color, font, frame, border, …) is a
81:   **chainable modifier**. There is no standalone width/height — use the
82:   compound `frame` modifier.
83: - **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` has SwiftUI's dual identity: it is a
84:   **View** (a layout-greedy solid-color fill) and a **Data Type** (passed into
85:   style-taking modifiers: `.foregroundStyle`, `.background`, `.border`,
86:   `.tint`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier, and `.foregroundColor(_:)` is
87:   deprecated — foreground styling is always `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
88: - **Only changes are transmitted.** Emission is diff-based; an unchanged tree
89:   emits **zero** opcodes. The DSL describes values; the emitter diffs them.
90: - **Typed enums, never raw ints.** Every enumerated value is a typed constant
91:   (`Alignment.leading`, `FontWeight.bold`, `ToggleStyle.checkbox`), not a bare
92:   integer. The numeric code is the DSL's job to resolve (see the value-type and
93:   enum tables in MODIFIERS.md).
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 2. Canonical signature notation
98: 
99: The canonical signatures below are written SwiftUI-shaped and language
100: agnostic. Conventions used:
101: 
102: - `T("…")` / `View("…")` — a view/control constructor.
103: - `{ ... }` — the child subtree (a trailing closure in SwiftUI; a vararg,
104:   macro, builder, or lambda in other languages).
105: - `Signal<T>` — a read-only derived or writable signal; `WritableSignal<T>` —
106:   a two-way binding target. A control takes a `WritableSignal<T>` for its
107:   value (see [§3](#3-state-model-signals)).
108: - `()` — the action a `Button` fires.
109: - Modifiers chain as `.name(args)` on any view and are applied
110:   **innermost-first** (the last chained modifier's property wins).
111: 
112: Per-language adaptation rules:
113: 
114: | Language | Case | Composition mechanism | Example |
115: |----------|------|-----------------------|---------|
116: | SwiftUI | `camelCase` | trailing closures + result builder | `VStack { Text("x").padding() }` |
117: | Java (`com.pathland.view`) | `camelCase` | static factories + varargs + chainable default methods | `View.vstack(View.text("x").padding(16))` |
118: | Rust (`pathland-view`) | `snake_case` | macros + free functions + chainable trait methods | `vstack![text("x").padding(16.0)]` |
119: 
120: ---
121: 
122: ## 3. State model (signals)
123: 
124: Pathland state is **Angular-style signals**. This is the non-negotiable
125: reactive core every DSL exposes.
126: 
127: ### 3.1 Signal surface
128: 
129: | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view.signal`) | Semantics |
130: |-----------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
131: | `signal(initial)` | `Signals.signal(T)` | a writable signal |
132: | `signal(name, initial)` | `Signals.signal(String, T)` | named (names surface in dependency errors) |
133: | `signal(initial, equal)` | `Signals.signal(T, BiPredicate<T,T>)` | custom equality |
134: | `computed(fn)` | `Signals.computed(Supplier<T>)` | lazy, memoized derived signal |
135: | `effect(fn)` | `Signals.effect(Runnable)` | runs immediately, then on dependency change |
136: | `untracked(fn)` | `Signals.untracked(Supplier<T>)` | reads without recording dependencies |
137: | `read()` | `get()` | current value |
138: | `write(v)` | `set(T)` | replace (no-op when equal) |
139: | `update(fn)` | `update(UnaryOperator<T>)` | derive from current and write |
140: | `asReadonly()` | `asReadonly()` | read-only view of a writable signal |
141: 
142: **Guarantees** (must be preserved by any implementation): equality suppression,
143: synchronous flush at the end of the outermost write, glitch-free propagation
144: (each computed recomputes at most once per flush), error caching, write
145: discipline, and circular-dependency detection.
146: 
147: ### 3.2 Two-way binding
148: 
149: A control's value is **a `WritableSignal<T>` passed to its constructor**:
150: `TextField(placeholder, writable)`, `Toggle(label, isOn: writable)`,
151: `Slider(value: writable, in: min...max)`. The flow:
152: 
153: 1. At **mount**, the DSL control records a **value input** (a sink on the
154:    retained node) for the signal, and the emitter exposes routing registries to
155:    the host: tap actions, text inputs, value inputs, date inputs.
156: 2. The host receives the control's raw event (`TEXT_CHANGED`,
157:    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED`, or a composed tap) and calls the sink,
158:    which **writes into the signal**.
159: 3. The signal flush re-emits **only that node's** delta (`SET_TEXT`,
160:    `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_DATE`) back through the emitter.
161: 
162: Reading is equally fine-grained: a node's text or a property can be **bound to
163: a signal** (`Text(signal)`, `.foregroundStyle(signal)`, `.fontSize(signal)`),
164: so a change re-emits only the bound node.
165: 
166: ### 3.3 Persisted state (`State<T>`)
167: 
168: A `State<T>` field is the SwiftUI-`@State`-shaped form of a persisted signal,
169: **auto-wired by key**:
170: 
171: ```java
172: State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);            // key = field name "count"
173: State<Integer> total = new State<>(0, "total");   // explicit store key
174: count.get(); count.set(0); count.update(v -> v + 1);
175: count.signal();                                   // the WritableSignal (for TextField, …)
176: ```
177: 
178: The store (`StateStore`) is untyped and platform-neutral (in-memory, Redis,
179: file, SQLite, LocalStorage, NVS flash). The Java realization wires `State`
180: fields via an annotation processor that generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per
181: view class; connection happens when the view renders. A generated DSL in a
182: language without reflection/annotation processing MUST offer the equivalent
183: explicit wiring.
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. View surface
188: 
189: Component ids and wire behavior come from
190: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md); the tables here give the **DSL signature**.
191: `Java DSL (current)` is the reference realization today.
192: 
193: ### 4.1 Primitive drawing & visual nodes
194: 
195: | View | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
196: |------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|

198: | `Image` | `Image("name")` / `Image(systemName:)` | `View.image()` / `View.image(String source)` | `IMAGE` 0x02; `IMAGE_SOURCE` 0x1002 |
199: | `Color` | `Color(.sRGB, red:green:blue:)` (a View) | `Color.rgb(int,int,int)` (implements `View`) | `COLOR` 0x03; `COLOR` 0x100A |
200: | `Shape` | `Rectangle()`, `Circle()`, `Capsule()`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:)` | `View.rectangle()` | `SHAPE` 0x04; `SHAPE_KIND` 0x0006 |
201: | `Divider` | `Divider()` | `View.divider()` | `DIVIDER` 0x05 |
202: | `Spacer` | `Spacer()` | `View.spacer()` | `SPACER` 0x06 |
203: | `ProgressView` | `ProgressView(value:)` / `ProgressView()` | `View.progressView(float)` / `View.progressView()` | `PROGRESS_VIEW` 0x07; `PROGRESS` 0x200E / `IS_INDETERMINATE` 0x200F |

207: (`View.text("…")`) rather than direct construction (`Text("…")`). Shape kinds
208: other than `Rectangle` are not exposed as named constructors in the Java DSL
209: today (only `View.rectangle()`); the canonical form exposes the full
210: `ShapeKind` set.
211: 
212: ### 4.2 Layout & container nodes

214: | View | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
215: |------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|

231: 
232: ### 4.3 Semantic controls
233: 
234: Two-way value controls bind a `WritableSignal`. Actions bind a callback.
235: 
236: | Control | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
237: |---------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
238: | `Button` | `Button("title", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `View.button(String, Runnable)` / `View.button(View, Runnable)` | `BUTTON` 0x20; tap = composed `POINTER_DOWN`+`POINTER_UP` |
239: | `TextField` | `TextField("placeholder", text: writable)` | `View.textField(String, WritableSignal<String>)` | `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21; `TEXT_CHANGED` → text input |
240: | `SecureField` | `SecureField("…", text: writable)` | (secure via `IS_SECURE` token) | `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21 + `IS_SECURE` 0x200D |
241: | `TextEditor` | `TextEditor(text: writable)` | `View.textEditor(WritableSignal<String>)` | `TEXT_EDITOR` 0x22 |

243: | `Slider` | `Slider(value: writable, in: min...max)` | `View.slider(float value, float min, float max, WritableSignal<Float>)` | `SLIDER` 0x25; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input |
244: | `Stepper` | `Stepper("label", value: writable, in: min...max, step:)` | `View.stepper(float, float, float, float, WritableSignal<Float>)` | `STEPPER` 0x26; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input |
245: | `DatePicker` | `DatePicker("label", selection: writable, displayedComponents:)` | `View.datePicker(DatePickerMode, WritableSignal<Integer>)` | `DATE_PICKER` 0x27; `DATE_CHANGED` → date input; value via `STYLE::SET_DATE` |
246: | `Picker` | `Picker("label", selection: writable) { options }` | `View.picker(PickerStyle, WritableSignal<Integer>, View... options)` | `PICKER` 0x28; `VALUE_CHANGED` (index) → value input |
247: | `Menu` | `Menu { actions } label: { trigger }` | `View.menu(View trigger, View... actions)` / `View.menu(View, WritableSignal<Integer>, View...)` | `MENU` 0x29; `VALUE_CHANGED` (item index) → value input |

251: (`View.slider(value, min, max, binding)`) instead of SwiftUI's labeled
252: `value:in:` range binding. `Button` takes a `(label, action)` pair rather than

254: `(style, selected, binding, label)` positionally; `DatePicker` binds
255: **days-since-epoch** (`WritableSignal<Integer>`) rather than a date object —
256: the protocol's `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` two-field encoding is
257: days + millis-of-day (see [§7](#7-java-convergence-proposal)).
258: 
259: **Control guarantees** (from PRIMITIVES.md): a control without children renders
260: in **Native Token Mode** (native OS control); a control with a child subtree
261: renders in **Composite Override Mode** (custom chrome wrapped with native
262: gesture semantics). Renderers MUST gate value/text/date events by
263: `BINDING_ID`, `ACTION_ID`, or the `EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask (transport-aware
264: event guards) — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md).

266: ### 4.4 Gestures
267: 
268: | Gesture | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Rust DSL (current) |
269: |---------|---------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|

271: | raw pointer | `.gesture` composition from raw inputs | `.pointerEvents(int mask)` | `.pointer_events(u32 mask)` |
272: 
273: Tap is **not** a protocol event: it is composed app-side from `POINTER_DOWN`
274: then `POINTER_UP` on the same target (`EVENT_LISTENERS` bits 0|2). The DSL's
275: `.onTapGesture` declares those listeners and records the action; the host
276: routes the recognized tap via the emitter's tap-action registry.

279: 
280: ## 5. Modifier surface

283: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md); the tables here give the **DSL signature**. A
284: compound SwiftUI modifier expands to **one `SET_PROPERTY` per underlying
285: property** (`.frame` → `WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` + `ALIGNMENT`; `.border` →
286: `BORDER_COLOR` + `BORDER_WIDTH`; `.shadow` → `SHADOW_COLOR` + `SHADOW_RADIUS` +

302: | `scaledToFit` | `.scaledToFit()` | `.scaledToFit()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C (Fit) |
303: | `scaledToFill` | `.scaledToFill()` | `.scaledToFill()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C (Fill) |

306: **Semantics**: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use the sentinels `FILL` (−1.0 = expand) and
307: `HUG_CONTENT` (−2.0 = intrinsic); omitting an axis leaves it to the native
308: renderer. `OFFSET` is a post-layout translation; `POSITION` is absolute
309: placement within the parent.

311: ### 5.2 Text formatting
312:

314: |----------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|

337: ### 5.3 Appearance & effects
338: 
339: | Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Property(ies) |
340: |----------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
341: | `background` | `.background(_:)` | `.background(Color)` / `.background(Signal<Color>)` | `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001 |
342: | `border` | `.border(_:width:)` | `.border(float width, Color color, float radius)` | `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `BORDER_WIDTH` 0x1003, `BORDER_RADIUS` 0x1005 |
343: | `border` (edges) | `.border(_:width:edges:)` | (not exposed) | + `BORDER_EDGES` 0x1016 (u32 bitmask: `TOP`=1, `LEADING`=2, `BOTTOM`=4, `TRAILING`=8) |
344: | `cornerRadius` | `.cornerRadius(_:)` | `.cornerRadius(float)` | `BORDER_RADIUS` 0x1005 |
345: | `shadow` | `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)` | `.shadow(Color, float, float, float)` / `.shadow(float)` | `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `SHADOW_RADIUS` 0x1022, `SHADOW_X` 0x1023, `SHADOW_Y` 0x1024 |
346: | `opacity` | `.opacity(_:)` | `.opacity(float)` | `OPACITY` 0x100D |
347: | `blur` | `.blur(radius:)` | `.blur(float)` | `BLUR_RADIUS` 0x1025 |
348: | `saturation` | `.saturation(_:)` | `.saturation(float)` | `SATURATION` 0x1026 |
349: | `contrast` | `.contrast(_:)` | `.contrast(float)` | `CONTRAST` 0x1027 |
350: | `brightness` | `.brightness(_:)` | `.brightness(float)` | `BRIGHTNESS` 0x1028 |
351: | `grayscale` | `.grayscale(_:)` | `.grayscale(float)` | `GRAYSCALE` 0x1029 |
352: | `hueRotation` | `.hueRotation(_:)` | `.hueRotation(float)` | `HUE_ROTATION` 0x102A |
353: | `colorMultiply` | `.colorMultiply(_:)` | `.colorMultiply(Color)` | `COLOR_MULTIPLY` 0x102B |
354: | `colorInvert` | `.colorInvert()` | `.colorInvert()` | `COLOR_INVERT` 0x102C |
355: | `clipped` | `.clipped()` | `.clipped()` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 |
356: | `clipShape` | `.clipShape(_:)` | `.clipShape(ShapeKind)` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 + `SHAPE_KIND` 0x0006 |

358: **Delta (Java)**: `.border` takes `(width, color, radius)` — SwiftUI's
359: parameter order is `.border(color, width)` and corner radius is a separate
360: `.cornerRadius`. The canonical order MUST be color-then-width.

363: 
364: | Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Property(ies) |
365: |----------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
366: | `rotationEffect` | `.rotationEffect(_:anchor:)` | `.rotation(float)` | `ROTATION_DEGREES` 0x102D |

370: anchors. Transforms do not affect layout.
371: 
372: ### 5.5 Interaction & state
373: 
374: | Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Property(ies) |
375: |----------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
376: | `hidden` | `.hidden()` | `.hidden()` / `.visible(boolean)` | `VISIBLE` 0x100E |
377: | `disabled` | `.disabled(_:)` | `.disabled(boolean)` | `ENABLED` 0x2003 (inverse: 1 = interactive) |
378: | `allowsHitTesting` | `.allowsHitTesting(_:)` | `.allowsHitTesting(boolean)` | `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING` 0x102F |
379: | `controlSize` | `.controlSize(_:)` | `.controlSize(ControlSize)` | `CONTROL_SIZE` 0x200C |
380: | `accessibilityLabel` | `.accessibilityLabel(_:)` | `.accessibilityLabel(String)` | `LABEL` 0x200A |
381: | `accessibilityRole` | `.accessibilityRole(_:)` | `.accessibilityRole(int)` | `ROLE` 0x2001 |
382: | `accessibilityState` | `.accessibilityState(_:)` | `.accessibilityState(int)` | `STATE` 0x2002 |
383: | `modifier` (custom) | `.modifier(_:)` | `.modifier(ViewModifier)` | composes core modifiers |
384: | `buttonStyle` | `.buttonStyle(_:)` | `.buttonStyle(ButtonStyle)` | environment-scoped (ScopedValue) |
385: | `focusable` | `.focusable(_:)` | (via `.pointerEvents`) | **no property** — declares `FOCUS` listener bit 5; observe `FOCUS_CHANGED` |
386: | raw listeners | `.pointerEvents(mask)` / `.pointer_events(mask)` | `.pointerEvents(int)` | `EVENT_LISTENERS` 0x2005 (u32 bitmask, bits per EVENTS.md) |
387: 
388: **Delta (Java)**: `.visible(boolean)` is a Pathland extra (SwiftUI only has
389: `.hidden()`). `.accessibilityRole`/`.accessibilityState` take raw `int` codes
390: today rather than a typed enum. Raw input listeners are exposed only through
391: `.pointerEvents(mask)` — there is no per-event sugar (e.g. a `.focusable` or
392: `.onSubmit` that sets the matching bit).
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: ## 6. Authoring conventions
397: 
398: A conformant DSL follows these conventions:
399: 
400: 1. **Names**: SwiftUI view/modifier names; per-language case (camelCase,
401:    snake_case). `foregroundStyle` not `foregroundColor`; `fontWeight`,
402:    `multilineTextAlignment`, `scaledToFit`, `allowsHitTesting` keep their
403:    SwiftUI spellings.
404: 2. **Signature order**: canonical parameter order is preserved —
405:    `.border(color, width)`, `.frame(width, height, alignment)`,
406:    `.shadow(color, radius, x, y)`. Compound modifiers expand to one property
407:    per argument.
408: 3. **Constructor vs modifier**: structural (alignment, spacing) in the
409:    constructor; everything else chainable.
410: 4. **Typed enums**: `Alignment` (leading/center/trailing/fill),
411:    `TextAlignment`, `FontWeight` (100–900), `Truncation` (head/middle/tail),
412:    `TextCase` (none/uppercase/lowercase), `FontStyle` (normal/italic),
413:    `FontDesign` (default/serif/rounded/monospaced), `ContentMode` (fit/fill),
414:    `ControlSize` (small/regular/large), `ToggleStyle`
415:    (switch/checkbox/button), `PickerStyle` (menu/segmented/wheel/radiogroup),
416:    `DatePickerMode` (date/time/dateAndTime), `ShapeKind`
417:    (circle/rectangle/roundedRectangle/capsule/ellipse/path). Numeric codes
418:    come from MODIFIERS.md's appendix; the DSL resolves them.
419: 5. **`Spacer`/`Color` as views**: `Spacer()` is a flexible expanding filler;
420:    `Color(...)` in a tree is a layout-greedy fill.
421: 6. **Environment scoping**: styles and state that must reach a whole subtree
422:    (`ButtonStyle`, the session's persisted state) are injected via the
423:    environment (Java: `ScopedValue`), never threaded through constructors.
424: 7. **Reactivity discipline**: `body()` is evaluated once; a signal read during
425:    mount records a dependency; a later write re-emits only the bound node.
426:    Never mutate signals during mount.
427: 8. **Emission contract**: each DSL call emits exactly the documented
428:    properties with the documented value types; the emitter diffs. The DSL never
429:    computes layout, never positions, never serializes full trees.
430: 
431: ---
432: 
433: ## 7. Java convergence proposal
434: 
435: The Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) has the complete surface; its *syntax*
436: drifts from the canonical SwiftUI shape. This section proposes convergence as a
437: future workstream (out of scope for this document's landing). It is a
438: **proposal** — the canonical contract is defined in [§4](#4-view-surface) and
439: [§5](#5-modifier-surface), not here.
440: 
441: | Canonical | Java today | Proposed Java (SwiftUI-closer) |
442: |-----------|-----------|--------------------------------|
443: | `Text("…")` | `View.text("…")` | `new Text("…")` (direct construction; keep `View.text` as a factory alias) |
444: | `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `View.button(String, Runnable)` | `Button.of("…", () -> …)`; a `Button(String)` + `Button(View, Runnable)` mirroring `Button(title, action)` |
445: | `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `View.toggle(boolean, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` | labeled params or an overload `Toggle.of(String label, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` |
446: | `Slider(value: in:)` | `View.slider(value, min, max, binding)` | `Slider.of(binding, min, max)` keeping positional order: binding first |
447: | `.border(color, width)` | `.border(width, color, radius)` | add `.border(Color, float)`; keep `(width, color, radius)` as the corner-radius convenience |
448: | `DatePicker(selection:)` | `View.datePicker(DatePickerMode, WritableSignal<Integer>)` | keep days-since-epoch binding; optionally add a `Date`-shaped wrapper that encodes days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` |
449: 
450: Guidance for the proposal:
451: 
452: - Prefer **additive overloads/aliases** over breaking changes; keep the
453:   existing factory names working so application code (the demos) migrates
454:   incrementally.
455: - Add a `SwiftUIShape`-style named constructor for each `ShapeKind`
456:   (`Circle.of()`, `Capsule.of()`, `RoundedRectangle.of(cornerRadius:)`) to
457:   match the canonical view set.
458: - Consider a `ButtonStyle`/`environment` path that lets the trailing-action
459:   form (`Button(label) { action }`) read the action from the environment, if a
460:   Java-idiomatic trailing lambda is desirable.
461: - Land the convergence only after the DSL.md surface is stable, and update
462:   `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` in the same change.
463: 
464: ---
465: 
466: ## 8. Generation contract for a new language
467: 
468: An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
469: following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
470: are the companion specs.
471: 
472: ### 8.1 Required surface
473: 
474: - [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
475:   `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
476:   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`,
477:   `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
478:   `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
479:   `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
480: - [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), chainable on
481:   any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument.
482: - [ ] **Signals** — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `untracked`,
483:   `get`/`set`/`update`/`asReadonly`, with equality suppression, synchronous
484:   flush, glitch-free propagation, error caching, write discipline, circular
485:   detection ([§3.1](#31-signal-surface)).
486: - [ ] **Two-way bindings** — every value control takes a writable signal and
487:   exposes a sink the host routes its event into ([§3.2](#32-two-way-binding)).
488: - [ ] **Persisted state** — `State<T>` keyed fields (or the language's
489:   equivalent wiring) against a platform-neutral store ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)).
490: - [ ] **Gestures** — `.onTapGesture` (composed from raw pointer down/up) and
491:   raw `pointerEvents`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask ([§4.4](#44-gestures)).
492: 
493: ### 8.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)
494: 
495: 1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
496:    Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
497:    never reuse allocated ids.
498: 2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
499:    with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
500:    DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
501:    appendix.
502: 3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`.
503: 4. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` sentinels: `FILL` = −1.0, `HUG_CONTENT` = −2.0.
504: 5. `DatePicker` value/event use the two-field encoding **days since epoch
505:    (I32) + millis of day (U32)**; there is no `DATE_VALUE` property.
506: 6. Value/text/date events are gated by the transport-aware event guards; the
507:    DSL's controls emit the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` that
508:    declare intent.
509: 7. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**: the DSL describes values, the
510:    emitter diffs. A generated DSL must keep the retained tree + emitter
511:    separation; it must not hand-serialize full trees.
512: 
513: ### 8.3 Language adaptation rules
514: 
515: | SwiftUI mechanism | Adapt as |
516: |-------------------|----------|
517: | trailing closure / result builder for children | varargs (Java), macros (Rust), builders/block (C#/Kotlin), element list (any) |
518: | `Binding<T>` (Swift) | `WritableSignal<T>` (always — signals are the model, never property wrappers) |
519: | `some View` opaque return | the language's `View` interface/trait (Java `View`, Rust `View` trait) |
520: | `@State`/`@Binding` property wrappers | signals + persisted `State<T>` ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)) |
521: | labeled parameters | named params where the language has them; otherwise preserve **parameter order** and document labels |
522: | method chaining for modifiers | default methods (Java), extension traits (Rust), extension methods (C#/Kotlin) |
523: 
524: ### 8.4 Conformance recipe
525: 
526: A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
527: reference implementations:
528: 
529: 1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new
530:    DSL's test harness; assert byte-identical `TREE`/`STYLE`/`EVENT`/`META`
531:    opcodes for each canonical element.
532: 2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
533:    deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,
534:    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` write into the bound signal).
535: 3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
536:    language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
537:    steady-state emission).
538: 4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md
539:    (the specs are the source of truth, never the reference code).
540: 
541: **Reference implementations to read**: Java — `lib/java/pathland-view`
542: (`com.pathland.view`, `com.pathland.view.signal`, `com.pathland.view.state`,
543: `com.pathland.view.emit`); Rust — `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view` +
544: `pathland-engine` + `pathland-core::signal`.
545: 
546: ---
547: 
548: ## 9. Appendix A: SwiftUI ↔ DSL signature map
549: 
550: Representative rows; the full surface is in [§4](#4-view-surface) and
551: [§5](#5-modifier-surface).
552: 
553: | SwiftUI | Canonical DSL | Java DSL (current) | Rust DSL (current) |
554: |---------|---------------|--------------------|--------------------|
555: | `Text("Hi")` | `Text("Hi")` | `View.text("Hi")` | `text("Hi")` |
556: | `VStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 8) { … }` | `VStack(alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `View.vstack(Alignment.CENTER, 8, children...)` | `vstack![…].spacing(8.0)` |
557: | `Button("+") { inc() }` | `Button("+", action)` | `View.button("+", () -> inc())` | `button("+")` (no action yet) |
558: | `TextField("Name", text: $name)` | `TextField("Name", text: writable)` | `View.textField("Name", name)` | `TextField { placeholder }` (no binding yet) |
559: | `Toggle("On", isOn: $on)` | `Toggle("On", isOn: writable)` | `View.toggle(selected, on)` | `Toggle(style)` (no binding yet) |
560: | `Slider(value: $v, in: 0...100)` | `Slider(value: writable, in: min...max)` | `View.slider(v, 0, 100, vSig)` | `Slider { value, min, max }` (no binding yet) |
561: | `DatePicker("D", selection: $d)` | `DatePicker("D", selection: writable)` | `View.datePicker(DatePickerMode.DATE, days)` | `DatePicker` (bare) |
562: | `.foregroundStyle(.red)` | `.foregroundStyle(Color)` | `.foregroundStyle(Color)` | `.foreground_style(Color(0xFF0000FF))` |
563: | `.background(.gray)` | `.background(Color)` | `.background(Color)` | `.background(Color(0xFFEEEEEE))` |
564: | `.border(.blue, width: 2)` | `.border(Color, width: 2)` | `.border(2, Color, 8)` | `.border(Color, 2.0)` |
565: | `.frame(width: 100, height: 24)` | `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` | `.frame(100, 24, Alignment)` | `.frame(Some(100.0), Some(24.0), None)` |
566: | `.padding(16)` | `.padding(16)` | `.padding(16)` | `.padding(16.0)` |
567: | `.font(.system(size: 28))` | `.font(size: 28)` | `.fontSize(28)` | `.font_size(28.0)` |
568: | `.fontWeight(.bold)` | `.fontWeight(FontWeight)` | `.fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)` | `.font_weight(700.0)` |
569: | `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)` | `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)` | `.shadow(Color, float, float, float)` | (not yet) |
570: | `.onTapGesture { go() }` | `.onTapGesture(action)` | `.onTapGesture(() -> go())` | `.on_tap_gesture(|| go())` |
571: 
572: **Status deltas captured by this table**: the Java DSL is surface-complete but
573: uses static-factory syntax and a few non-SwiftUI parameter orders (see
574: [§7](#7-java-convergence-proposal)); the Rust DSL is structural today —
575: `pathland-view` exposes the view/modifier surface without signals, two-way
576: bindings, or actions (signals live in `pathland-core::signal` for engine-side
577: binding). Neither difference affects the protocol; both are per-project
578: implementation status tracked in each project's `status.md`.
579: 
580: ---
581: 
582: ## Conformance
583: 
584: - The wire footprint of every DSL element above is defined by the golden
585:   vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md). A new DSL element MUST add
586:   vectors before any implementation depends on it.
587: - Component ids: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md); property ids and value
588:   types: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md); event ids and listener bits:
589:   [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md). These specs are the single source of truth.

(End of file - total 589 lines)
</content>

I've reviewed how custom modifiers work today in both realizations:

- **Java**: `ViewModifier` is a `@FunctionalInterface` with `View body(View content)` — SwiftUI-shaped; usage is `content.modifier(new CardStyle())`; the returned view can wrap structure, not just set properties.
- **Rust**: `trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&mut Node) }` mutates the built node's properties only — it cannot wrap content with new structure.

The spec currently mentions modifier decoupling only as one §1 bullet and a single `.modifier(_:)` row in §5.5 — not as the first-class, developer-authored capability you're describing. Here's my plan.

## Plan: elevate developer-authored custom modifiers to a first-class DSL contract

**1. §1 Design principles** — upgrade the "Modifiers are decoupled" bullet:
> Any developer can **author a custom modifier in application code**, and it applies to **any existing view** — library primitive, container, control, custom view, or an already-modified view. Modifiers are **never hard-bound to a view type**; the same modifier works on a `Text`, a `VStack`, or a `Button` (SwiftUI `.modifier(_:)`). Cross-link to new §5.6.

**2. New §5.6 "Custom modifiers (developer-authored)"** — the full contract:
- **MUST guarantee**: application-authored modifiers are a supported, first-class surface in every conformant DSL; they apply to any view.
- **Canonical contract**: SwiftUI-shaped `ViewModifier` with `body(content) -> View` (`func body(content: Content) -> some View`). The modifier composes core modifiers *or* wraps `content` with additional structure (backgrounds, overlays).
- **Authoring + usage**, three columns (canonical / Java `body(View)` / Rust `apply(&mut Node)`).
- **Emission contract**: a custom modifier composed from core modifiers emits the same one-`SET_PROPERTY`-per-property deltas; diff-based; a renderer that can't apply it "allows and ignores" it.
- **Delta noted**: Rust's `apply(&mut Node)` currently mutates properties only and cannot restructure content — documented as a partial realization; a conformant DSL's custom-modifier mechanism should be able to wrap content (SwiftUI-shaped).

**3. §5.5** — keep the `.modifier(_:)` row, cross-link to §5.6.

**4. §7 Java convergence** — add a note/row: Java's `ViewModifier.body(View)` is already the canonical shape; propose `.of(...)` construction for parameterized modifier values (e.g. `CardStyle.of(padding, color)`) consistent with the one-construction-path convention; `.modifier(...)` stays.

**5. §8.1 required surface** — add a checkbox: "Custom modifiers — a `ViewModifier` authoring surface (`body(content) -> View`) plus `.modifier(...)` chainable on any view."

**6. §9 appendix** — add a row: SwiftUI `content.modifier(Card())` → canonical → Java `content.modifier(new CardStyle())` → Rust `.modifier(Card)`.

**1. §1 Design principles** — strengthen the "Modifiers are decoupled from views" bullet:
> Any developer can **author a custom modifier in application code** (a `ViewModifier`), and it applies to **any existing view** — library primitive, container, control, custom view, or an already-modified view. Modifiers are **never hard-bound to a view type**: the same modifier works on a `Text`, a `VStack`, or a `Button` (SwiftUI `.modifier(_:)`). A modifier a renderer cannot apply is allowed and ignored.

**2. New §5.6 "Custom modifiers (developer-authored)"** — the full contract:
- **MUST guarantee**: application-authored modifiers are a first-class surface in every conformant DSL and apply to any view.
- **Canonical contract**: SwiftUI-shaped `ViewModifier` with `body(content) -> View`; the modifier composes core modifiers *or* wraps `content` with structure (backgrounds, overlays).
- Authoring + usage in canonical / Java (`@FunctionalInterface ViewModifier { View body(View content) }`, `content.modifier(...)`) / Rust (`trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&mut Node) }`, `.modifier(...)`) — with Rust documented as a **partial realization** (mutates properties only; cannot restructure content) and the generation requirement that a conformant DSL's mechanism can wrap content.

content.text: Now the new §5.6 section:

input.newString:
**Delta (Java)**: `.visible(boolean)` is a Pathland extra (SwiftUI only has
`.hidden()`). `.accessibilityRole`/`.accessibilityState` take raw `int` codes
today rather than a typed enum. Raw input listeners are exposed only through
`.pointerEvents(mask)` — there is no per-event sugar (e.g. a `.focusable` or
`.onSubmit` that sets the matching bit).

### 5.6 Custom modifiers (developer-authored)

In SwiftUI any developer can define a modifier that applies to **any** existing
view — and Pathland is the same. This is a **first-class, MUST** property of
every conformant DSL: modifiers are never hard-bound to a view type.

- **Applicable to any view.** A modifier works on a library primitive
  (`Text`), a container (`VStack`), a control (`Button`), a custom view, or an
  already-modified view. The same modifier value applies everywhere.
- **One mechanism.** Core and application-authored modifiers are the **same
  surface**: a `ViewModifier` value applied via `.modifier(...)`. The library's
  sugar names (`.padding`, `.foregroundStyle`, …) are conveniences that
  construct the built-in `ViewModifier` values; there is exactly one modifier
  mechanism ([§5](#5-modifier-surface)).

| | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) |
|-|-----------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
| authoring | `struct Card: ViewModifier { func body(content: Content) -> some View }` | `@FunctionalInterface ViewModifier { View body(View content) }` | `trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&mut Node) }` |
| applying | `content.modifier(Card())` | `content.modifier(new CardStyle())` | `content.modifier(Card)` |
| sugar | `.padding(16)` ≡ `.modifier(Padding(16))` | `.padding(16)` → separate property-map path today (see §7) | `.padding(16.0)` ≡ `.modifier(Padding(16.0))` |

**Composition**: a custom modifier composes core modifiers **or** wraps
`content` with additional structure (a background, an overlay, a frame) and
returns the decorated view — exactly SwiftUI's `body(content: Content)`.

**Emission contract**: a custom modifier composed from core modifiers emits the
same one-`SET_PROPERTY`-per-property deltas as writing the modifiers inline;
emission stays diff-based, and a renderer that cannot apply a modifier
**allows and ignores** it.

**Realization deltas**:
- **Rust** — already conformant: every core modifier (`Padding`, `FontSize`,
  `ForegroundStyle`, `Frame`, …) implements `ViewModifier`, and the sugar
  methods delegate to `.modifier(...)`. Caveat: `apply(&mut Node)` mutates the
  built node's properties only — it cannot wrap `content` with new structure
  (the Java/SwiftUI `body(content)` form can). A conformant DSL's
  custom-modifier mechanism should support wrapping.
- **Java** — the custom `ViewModifier.body(View)` is SwiftUI-shaped, but the
  **core** modifiers currently go through a separate property-map path
  (`Modified.props`), not `ViewModifier`. Converging them to one mechanism is
  proposed in [§7](#7-java-convergence-proposal).

16: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

18: /**
19:  * Proves the desktop/embedded path: the Java DSL pushes raw 16-byte opcodes into the
20:  * Rust SPSC ring via FFM (zero JNI, zero-copy). Skipped when {@code libpathland_core}
21:  * is not on {@code java.library.path}.
22:  */
23: class RingOpcodeSinkTest {
24: 
25:     private static final int OFF_RING_OFFSET = 0x06;
26:     private static final int OFF_SLOT_COUNT = 0x0E;
27:     private static final int OFF_WRITE_CURSOR = 0x22;
28: 
29:     @Test
30:     void pushesOpcodesIntoTheSharedRing() {
31:         PathlandCore core;
32:         try {
33:             core = PathlandCore.instance();
34:         } catch (Throwable t) {
35:             Assumptions.assumeTrue(false,
36:                     "libpathland_core unavailable on java.library.path; FFM ring test skipped: " + t);
37:             return;
38:         }
39: 
40:         try (RingOpcodeSink sink = new RingOpcodeSink(core)) {
41:             Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
42:             emitter.mount(
43:                     View.vstack(View.text("Hi"), View.button("Go", () -> { })),
44:                     Environment.DEFAULT);
45: 
46:             long len = core.ringLen(sink.handle());
47:             MemorySegment ring = core.ringPtr(sink.handle()).reinterpret(len);
48:             byte[] buf = ring.toArray(ValueLayout.JAVA_BYTE);
49:             assertTrue(buf.length >= 64, "full linear memory buffer (header + rings + arena)");
50: 
51:             int ringOff = readIntLE(buf, OFF_RING_OFFSET);
52:             int slotCount = readIntLE(buf, OFF_SLOT_COUNT);
53:             int writeCursor = readIntLE(buf, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
54: 
55:             boolean sawCreate = false;
56:             boolean sawSetText = false;
57:             for (int i = 0; i < writeCursor; i++) {
58:                 int slot = i % slotCount;
59:                 int base = ringOff + slot * 16;
60:                 Opcode op = Opcode.fromBytes(java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(buf, base, base + 16));
61:                 if (op.category() == Categories.TREE && op.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE) {
62:                     sawCreate = true;
63:                 }
64:                 if (op.category() == Categories.STYLE && op.command() == Commands.Style.SET_TEXT) {
65:                     sawSetText = true;
66:                 }
67:             }
68:             assertTrue(sawCreate, "CREATE_NODE written into the ring");
69:             assertTrue(sawSetText, "SET_TEXT written into the ring");
70: 
71:             // The SET_TEXT string ("Hi") lives in the shared arena (absolute offset).
72:             int arenaOff = readIntLE(buf, 0x12);
73:             String text = new String(buf, arenaOff + 4, 2);
74:             assertEquals("Hi", text);
75:         }
76:     }
77: 
78:     private static int readIntLE(byte[] buf, int offset) {
79:         return (buf[offset] & 0xFF)
80:                 | ((buf[offset + 1] & 0xFF) << 8)
81:                 | ((buf[offset + 2] & 0xFF) << 16)
82:                 | ((buf[offset + 3] & 0xFF) << 24);
83:     }
84: }

## Commit 1 — `.of()` construction path (+ Group, shapes, `border(Color, width)`)

**New classes (`com.pathland.view`):**

~55 new public final classes, each `implements ViewModifier` with `.of(...)` and `body(View content)` returning `Modified.props(content, …)` (same properties/values the current sugar emits — byte-identical output). content.text:
All three commits landed on `spec/dsl-generation` (working tree clean), **41 Java tests green** via the JDK-22 harness:

- **`915c33a`** — `.of()` is the one construction path: every view/control has `<ViewName>.of(...)` (constructors private), the entire `View.*` static-factory block is deleted, `Group.of(...)` first-class view, full `ShapeKind` coverage (`Circle`/`Capsule`/`Ellipse`/`RoundedRectangle`/`Shape.of`), `Slider`/`Stepper` binding-first, `Toggle.of(label, isOn)`, `.border(Color, float)` canonical order, `Color.of(int)`. All 15 demo-views + tests migrated.
- **`2a19e6c`** — one modifier mechanism: 60 named `ViewModifier` classes (`Padding.of(16)`, `ForegroundStyle.of(color)`, `Border.of(color, width)`, `FrameMod.of(w,h,align)`, …), every sugar method delegates to `.modifier(...)`, reactive overloads included. Built-in and app-authored modifiers now share the identical surface (spec DSL.md §5.6). `FrameMod`/`*Mod` names avoid collisions.
- **`6bd6bad`** — `status.md` synced.

Emission is byte-identical (the modifier bodies apply the exact same properties as the old sugar), so the wire output is unchanged. The demo modules were untouched (they mount `KitchenSinkView`, which migrated) — they can't be compile-verified locally (JDK 25), as noted.

One follow-up worth flagging: `Group` maps to a `VSTACK` node today (no `GROUP` protocol component yet), and `DatePicker.of(mode, days)` stays days-based — both noted in the spec as "for now".
There should not be factory methods for modifiers on View class.

The directive: the `View` interface should have **no modifier factory methods** — modifiers are applied only as values via `view.modifier(X.of(...))`, exactly like application-authored ones. That means removing the entire sugar surface (`.padding(...)`, `.foregroundStyle(...)`, `.frame(...)`, …, `.onTapGesture(...)`) from `View.java`.

## Plan: remove modifier sugar from `View`

**1. `View.java`** — delete every modifier sugar default method (padding, foregroundStyle, background, tint, opacity, fontSize, fontWeight, border, visible/hidden, frame, offset, position, fixedSize, layoutPriority, zIndex, aspectRatio, scaledToFit/Fill, minimumScaleFactor, fontStyle, italic, fontDesign, fontWidth, kerning, tracking, baselineOffset, lineSpacing, lineLimit, multilineTextAlignment, truncationMode, textCase, underline, strikethrough, fontFamily, cornerRadius, shadow, blur, saturation, contrast, brightness, grayscale, hueRotation, colorMultiply, colorInvert, clipped, clipShape, rotation, scaleEffect, disabled, allowsHitTesting, controlSize, accessibilityLabel/Role/State, imageSource, pointerEvents, actionId, bindingId, onTapGesture). `View` keeps only `body()`, `render()`, `modifier(ViewModifier)`, and `buttonStyle(ButtonStyle)`. Modifiers become pure values: `content.modifier(Padding.of(16))`, `content.modifier(ForegroundStyle.of(color))`, `content.modifier(FrameMod.of(w,h,align))`, etc.

**2. Internal styles** — `PlainButtonStyle.makeBody` (`onTapGesture` → `.modifier(TapGesture.of(action))`) and `BorderedButtonStyle.makeBody` (foregroundStyle/padding/background/border/onTapGesture → `.modifier(...)`, border reordered to `Border.of(color, width, radius)`).

**3. Migrate call sites** (~150–200 modifier usages): the 15 `pathland-demo-views` files + `EmitterTest` + `HtmlRendererTest` (`RingOpcodeSinkTest` has none). `.name(args)` → `.modifier(Name.of(args))`, with the two order-sensitive ones fixed: `.border(width, color, radius)` → `.modifier(Border.of(color, width, radius))` (only `SectionCard`, `AppearanceSection`); `.frame(w,h,Alignment)` → `FrameMod.of(w,h,Alignment)` (order already matches); reactive `.background(signal)`/`.foregroundStyle(signal)` → `Background.of(signal)`/`ForegroundStyle.of(signal)`.

**4. Spec + status** — update `spec/DSL.md` (§5 intro & §5.6 "sugar" row, §7 convergence bullet "keep the `.padding(16)` sugar" → "remove the sugar", §9 appendix Java columns) to record that Java applies modifiers only via `.modifier(...)`, and `status.md`.

**5. Verify** — JDK-22 harness compile + 41 tests (with migrated test code); demo modules untouched.

Two decisions before I finalize:

Both confirmed. Final plan:

## Final plan: `View` has zero modifier factory methods

**1. `View.java`** — delete every modifier sugar method (`padding`, `foregroundStyle`, `background`, `tint`, `opacity`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `border`, `visible`/`hidden`, `frame`, `offset`, `position`, `fixedSize`, `layoutPriority`, `zIndex`, `aspectRatio`, `scaledToFit`/`scaledToFill`, `minimumScaleFactor`, `fontStyle`, `italic`, `fontDesign`, `fontWidth`, `kerning`, `tracking`, `baselineOffset`, `lineSpacing`, `lineLimit`, `multilineTextAlignment`, `truncationMode`, `textCase`, `underline`, `strikethrough`, `fontFamily`, `cornerRadius`, `shadow`, `blur`, `saturation`, `contrast`, `brightness`, `grayscale`, `hueRotation`, `colorMultiply`, `colorInvert`, `clipped`, `clipShape`, `rotation`, `scaleEffect`, `disabled`, `allowsHitTesting`, `controlSize`, `accessibilityLabel`/`Role`/`State`, `imageSource`, `pointerEvents`, `actionId`, `bindingId`, `onTapGesture`, `buttonStyle`). `View` keeps **only** `body()`, `render()`, and `modifier(ViewModifier)` — the single application entry point.

**2. New `ButtonStyleMod`** — a `ViewModifier` value: `ButtonStyleMod.of(ButtonStyle)` whose `body(content)` returns `new ButtonStyleView(content, style)` (the existing ScopedValue scoping). `buttonStyle(...)` sugar is replaced by `.modifier(ButtonStyleMod.of(...))`.

**3. Internal styles** — `PlainButtonStyle.makeBody` → `config.label().modifier(TapGesture.of(config.action()))`; `BorderedButtonStyle.makeBody` → chained `.modifier(ForegroundStyle.of(...)).modifier(Padding.of(...)).modifier(Background.of(...)).modifier(Border.of(borderColor, 1f, radius)).modifier(TapGesture.of(...))`.

**4. Migrate call sites** (~17 files, ~200 sites) via a method→modifier transform: `.name(args)` → `.modifier(Name.of(args))`. Special cases: `.border(width, color, radius)` → `Border.of(color, width, radius)` (reorder); reactive `.background(signal)`/`.foregroundStyle(signal)` → `Background.of(signal)`/`ForegroundStyle.of(signal)`; `.buttonStyle(...)` → `ButtonStyleMod.of(...)`; `.onTapGesture(...)` → `TapGesture.of(...)`. Files: 15 `pathland-demo-views`, `EmitterTest`, `HtmlRendererTest`.

**5. Spec + status** — `spec/DSL.md`: §5 intro note ("Java applies every modifier as `.modifier(X.of(...))`; no sugar"), §5.6 sugar-row Java cell, §7 unification bullet (change "keep the `.padding` sugar" → "remove the sugar"), §9 appendix Java columns, plus `status.md`.

**6. Verify** — JDK-22 harness compile + 41 tests (migrated); demo modules untouched.

Note: this makes the Java DSL deliberately more explicit (`.modifier(Padding.of(16))` rather than `.padding(16)`) — the built-in modifiers are now byte-for-byte the same surface as app-authored ones, per your directive.

Good addition — a `modifiers(ViewModifier...)` varargs entry point for applying several modifiers to the same node in one call. Here's the revised plan.

## Revised final plan

**`View.java`** — after removing all sugar, `View` exposes exactly three modifier entry points:
- `modifier(ViewModifier)` — single (unchanged)
- **`modifiers(ViewModifier... mods)`** — NEW: applies each in order, innermost-first (SwiftUI semantics): `modifiers(A, B, C)` ≡ `modifier(A).modifier(B).modifier(C)`; empty → `this`. Implemented as a fold over `modifier(...)` in a default method.

def balanced(s, open_idx):
    depth = 0
    i = open_idx
    while i < len(s):
        c = s[i]
        if c == '(':
            depth += 1
        elif c == ')':
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return i
        i += 1
    raise ValueError("unbalanced")

def pass_a(s):
    names = "|".join(sorted(SUGAR, key=len, reverse=True))
    out = []
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        m = re.match(r"\.(%s)\(" % names, s[i:])
        if m:
            name = m.group(1)
            cls = SUGAR[name]
            open_idx = i + m.start() + m.end() - 1
            close_idx = balanced(s, open_idx)
            inner = s[open_idx+1:close_idx]
            if name == "border":
                args = split_args(inner)
                if len(args) == 2:
                    inner = f"{args[1]}, {args[0]}"
                elif len(args) == 3:
                    inner = f"{args[1]}, {args[0]}, {args[2]}"
            out.append(f".modifier({cls}.of({inner}))")
            i = close_idx + 1
        else:
            out.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return "".join(out)

def split_args(inner):
    args = []
    depth = 0
    cur = []
    for ch in inner:
        if ch == '(':
            depth += 1
        elif ch == ')':
            depth -= 1
        if ch == ',' and depth == 0:
            args.append("".join(cur).strip())
            cur = []
        else:
            cur.append(ch)
    if cur:
        args.append("".join(cur).strip())
    return args

def pass_b(s):
    out = []
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        if s.startswith(".modifier(", i):
            segs = []
            j = i
            while s.startswith(".modifier(", j):
                open_idx = j + len(".modifier(") - 1
                close_idx = balanced(s, open_idx)
                segs.append(s[open_idx+1:close_idx])
                j = close_idx + 1
            if len(segs) == 1:
                out.append(f".modifier({segs[0]})")
            else:
                out.append(f".modifiers(" + ", ".join(segs) + ")")
            i = j
        else:
            out.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return "".join(out)

    b = pass_b(a)
    if b != s:

        print("migrated", p.relative_to(ROOT))
    else:

421: ### 5.6 Custom modifiers (developer-authored)
422: 
423: In SwiftUI any developer can define a modifier that applies to **any** existing
424: view — and Pathland is the same. This is a **first-class, MUST** property of
425: every conformant DSL: modifiers are never hard-bound to a view type.
426: 
427: - **Applicable to any view.** A modifier works on a library primitive
428:   (`Text`), a container (`VStack`), a control (`Button`), a custom view, or an
429:   already-modified view. The same modifier value applies everywhere.
430: - **One mechanism.** Core and application-authored modifiers are the **same
431:   surface**: a `ViewModifier` value applied via `.modifier(...)`. The library's
432:   sugar names (`.padding`, `.foregroundStyle`, …) are conveniences that
433:   construct the built-in `ViewModifier` values; there is exactly one modifier
434:   mechanism ([§5](#5-modifier-surface)).
435: 
436: | | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) |
437: |-|-----------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
438: | authoring | `struct Card: ViewModifier { func body(content: Content) -> some View }` | `@FunctionalInterface ViewModifier { View body(View content) }` | `trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&mut Node) }` |
439: | applying | `content.modifier(Card())` | `content.modifier(new CardStyle())` | `content.modifier(Card)` |
440: | sugar | `.padding(16)` ≡ `.modifier(Padding(16))` | `.modifier(Padding.of(16))` → separate property-map path today (see §7) | `.padding(16.0)` ≡ `.modifier(Padding(16.0))` |
441: 
442: **Composition**: a custom modifier composes core modifiers **or** wraps
443: `content` with additional structure (a background, an overlay, a frame) and
444: returns the decorated view — exactly SwiftUI's `body(content: Content)`.
445: 
446: **Emission contract**: a custom modifier composed from core modifiers emits the
447: same one-`SET_PROPERTY`-per-property deltas as writing the modifiers inline;
448: emission stays diff-based, and a renderer that cannot apply a modifier
449: **allows and ignores** it.

451: **Realization deltas**:
452: - **Rust** — already conformant: every core modifier (`Padding`, `FontSize`,
453:   `ForegroundStyle`, `Frame`, …) implements `ViewModifier`, and the sugar
454:   methods delegate to `.modifier(...)`. Caveat: `apply(&mut Node)` mutates the
455:   built node's properties only — it cannot wrap `content` with new structure
456:   (the Java/SwiftUI `body(content)` form can). A conformant DSL's
457:   custom-modifier mechanism should support wrapping.

## 7. Java DSL convergence (adopted)

The Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) has the complete surface. The convergence
below has been **adopted** (`.of()` construction, the removal of the `View.*`
factories, and modifiers as `ViewModifier` values); the remaining items are
marked *optional*. The canonical contract is [§4](#4-view-surface) and
[§5](#5-modifier-surface).

| Canonical | Java (adopted) | Optional / remaining |
|-----------|----------------|----------------------|
| `Text("…")` | `Text.of(String)` / `Text.of(Signal<String>)` | — |
| `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `Button.of(String, Runnable)` / `Button.of(View, Runnable)` | — |
| `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `Toggle.of(String label, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` (+ `ToggleStyle` overload) | — |
| `Slider(value: in:)` | `Slider.of(binding, min, max)` (binding first) | — |
| `.border(color, width)` | `Border.of(Color, float)` via `.modifier(...)` | `Border.of(Color, float, float)` radius convenience |
| `DatePicker(selection:)` | `DatePicker.of(mode, days)` | *optional* `Date`-shaped overload encoding days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` |

Adopted conventions:

- **`.of()` is the one construction path.** Every concrete view/control exposes
  a static `<ViewName>.of(...)` factory on its own class. Construction is never
  `new <ViewName>()` and never `View.<name>(...)`.
- **The `View.*` static-factory surface is removed.** The entire factory block
  (`text`, `image`, `rectangle`, `spacer`, `vstack`, `hstack`, `zstack`,
  `button`, `textField`, `textEditor`, `toggle`, `slider`, `stepper`,
  `progressView`, `gauge`, `divider`, `grid`, `scrollView`, `lazyVStack`,
  `lazyHStack`, `lazyVGrid`, `lazyHGrid`, `picker`, `menu`, `colorPicker`,
  `datePicker`, `group`) is deleted from `View.java`.
- **`Group` is a first-class view.** `Group.of(View...)` is a transparent
  container view (SwiftUI `Group`).
- **Core and custom modifiers share one mechanism.** Core modifiers are
  `ViewModifier` values (`Padding.of(16)`, `ForegroundStyle.of(color)`) applied
  via `.modifier(...)` — there is **no sugar on `View`**; several modifiers at
  once use `.modifiers(...)`, innermost-first. Parameterized modifier values use
  `.of(...)`; `buttonStyle` is the `ButtonStyleMod` value.
- **Full `ShapeKind` coverage.** `Circle.of()`, `Capsule.of()`, `Ellipse.of()`,
  `RoundedRectangle.of(cornerRadius:)`, generic `Shape.of(ShapeKind)` (for
  `Path`).
- *Optional*: a `ButtonStyle`/`environment` path letting the trailing-action
  form (`Button(label) { action }`) read the action from the environment, if a
  Java-idiomatic trailing lambda is desirable.
- *Optional*: a `Date`-shaped `DatePicker` binding (see table).

## 7. Java convergence proposal

The Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) has the complete surface; its *syntax*
drifts from the canonical SwiftUI shape. This section proposes convergence as a
future workstream (out of scope for this document's landing). It is a
**proposal** — the canonical contract is defined in [§4](#4-view-surface) and
[§5](#5-modifier-surface), not here.

| Canonical | Java today | Proposed Java (SwiftUI-closer) |
|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------|
| `Text("…")` | `View.text(String)` / `View.text(Signal<String>)` | `Text.of(String)` / `Text.of(Signal<String>)` |
| `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `View.button(String, Runnable)` / `View.button(View, Runnable)` | `Button.of(String, Runnable)` / `Button.of(View, Runnable)` |
| `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `View.toggle(boolean, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` (+ `ToggleStyle` overload) | `Toggle.of(String label, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` (+ `ToggleStyle` overload) |
| `Slider(value: in:)` | `View.slider(value, min, max, binding)` | `Slider.of(binding, min, max)` keeping positional order: binding first |
| `.border(color, width)` | `.border(width, color, radius)` | add `.border(Color, float)`; keep `(width, color, radius)` as the corner-radius convenience |
| `DatePicker(selection:)` | `View.datePicker(DatePickerMode, WritableSignal<Integer>)` | `DatePicker.of(mode, days)` (optionally a `Date`-shaped overload encoding days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED`) |

Guidance for the proposal:

- **`.of()` is the one construction path.** Every concrete view/control
  exposes a static `<ViewName>.of(...)` factory on its own class. Construction
  is never `new <ViewName>()` and never `View.<name>(...)`.
- **Remove the `View.*` static-factory surface.** Once the `.of()` factories
  land and `pathland-demo-views` + both demos migrate, delete the entire
  static-factory block in `View.java` — `text`, `image`, `rectangle`,
  `spacer`, `vstack`, `hstack`, `zstack`, `button`, `textField`,
  `textEditor`, `toggle`, `slider`, `stepper`, `progressView`, `gauge`,
  `divider`, `grid`, `scrollView`, `lazyVStack`, `lazyHStack`, `lazyVGrid`,
  `lazyHGrid`, `picker`, `menu`, `colorPicker`, `datePicker`, `group`. The
  chainable default modifiers on `View` stay. This is a deliberate, single
  breaking change — additive first (`.of()` factories), then removal.
- **`Group` becomes a first-class view.** `View.group(List<View>)` (which
  returned a `VStack`) is replaced by `Group.of(View...)`, a transparent
  container view (SwiftUI `Group`) that composites its children;
  `View.group(...)` is removed with the rest of the factories.
- **Core and custom modifiers share one mechanism.** Core modifiers are
  `ViewModifier` values (`Padding.of(16)`, `ForegroundStyle.of(color)`) applied
  via `.modifier(...)` — the `.padding(16)` sugar is **removed** (there is no
  per-modifier factory method on `View`; several modifiers at once use
  `.modifiers(...)`, innermost-first). Parameterized modifier values use
  `.of(...)` (e.g. `CardStyle.of(padding, color)`); `buttonStyle` is the
  `ButtonStyleMod` value (Rust is already conformant).
- Add a static `.of()` factory for each `ShapeKind` (`Circle.of()`,
  `Capsule.of()`, `RoundedRectangle.of(cornerRadius:)`) to match the
  canonical view set.
- Consider a `ButtonStyle`/`environment` path that lets the trailing-action
  form (`Button(label) { action }`) read the action from the environment, if a
  Java-idiomatic trailing lambda is desirable.
- Land the convergence only after the DSL.md surface is stable, and update
  `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` in the same change.

- **`d5cdade`** (code) — `View` has **zero modifier factory methods**. It keeps only `body()`, `render()`, `modifier(ViewModifier)`, and the new **`modifiers(ViewModifier...)`** (varargs, innermost-first, empty → `this`). - L46–47 `Rectangle.of().modifier(FrameMod.of(180, 80, CENTER)).modifiers(Background.of(...), CornerRadius.of(8))` → one `.modifiers(...)`

- L49–50 `...modifiers(LineLimit.of(1), TruncationMod.of(TAIL)).modifier(FrameMod.of(280, NaN, CENTER))` → one `.modifiers(...)`

### Category 1: Hardening, Memory Safety & Fuzzing

3: > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol for declarative, retained-mode UI

7: ## Overview
8: 
9: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
10: multiple renderer backends. It offers a declarative, retained-mode view API
11: (SwiftUI-shaped in ergonomics) designed to be **language-agnostic** and
12: **platform-agnostic**.
13: 
14: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
15: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
16: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
17: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
18: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
19: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
20: 
21: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
22: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
23: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`).
24: 
25: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
26: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
27: change detection is fine-grained and signal-based — a signal bound to a node's
28: text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas, so only the things that
29: actually changed emit opcodes and an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.

39: ## The Three Elements
40: 
41: Pathland is composed of three elements. They are the vocabulary the whole
42: project speaks, so they are settled and used consistently:
43: 
44: ```
45: ┌────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
46: │ 1. Retained UI     │        │ 3. Renderer         │
47: │ the app's UI tree  │────┐   │ maps opcodes onto   │
48: │ (any language,     │    │   │ native elements +   │
49: │  any platform)     │    │   │ event reporting     │
50: └────────────────────┘    │   └───────────▲─────────┘
51:                          │                │
52: ┌────────────────────┐    │                │
53: │ 2. Opcode engine   │◄───┘                │
54: │ reconciles + emits │─────────────────────┘
55: └────────────────────┘
56: ```
57: 
58: 1. **Retained UI** — the application's canonical retained UI tree. It is the
59:    single source of truth, owned by the application. It can be authored in
60:    **any language on any platform**: Rust, Java, Swift, C#, C, TypeScript —
61:    desktop, mobile, or embedded — through a generated DSL or the flat native C
62:    ABI.
63: 2. **Opcode engine** — the producer: reconciles the retained tree and emits it as
64:    fixed **16-byte opcodes** using fine-grained, signal-based change detection: a
65:    signal bound to a node's text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas,
66:    so only the things that actually changed emit and an unchanged tree emits zero
67:    opcodes. The engine is language-independent — the same opcode stream serves
68:    every renderer. It spans a pure protocol core (`pathland-core`) and a
69:    retained-tree emitter (`pathland-engine`).
70: 3. **Renderer** — consumes the opcode stream and maps it onto that platform's
71:    **native elements**, and reports raw inputs back as events. It is a pure
72:    function of the opcode stream (stateless) and never retains application
73:    state. *"Host" and "driver" are roles a renderer plays: it runs inside a
74:    host and is pumped by a driver — they are not separate elements.* The same
75:    opcode stream targets **different UI systems**: a GTK4 renderer on desktop,
76:    an AppKit/SwiftUI renderer on macOS, a WinUI renderer on Windows, an LVGL
77:    renderer on embedded, a DOM renderer in the browser.
78: 
79: The opcodes are carried from the engine to the renderer by a transport (a
80: zero-copy shared-memory ring on desktop/native, a serialized network batch for
81: remote/browser); transport is an implementation detail, not a fourth element.

83: ## Core Principles
84: 
85: - **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
86: - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
87: - **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
88: - **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
89: - **Reactive emission**: fine-grained, signal-based change detection — only the nodes that actually changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
90: - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
91: - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
92: - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
93: - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
94: - **Hand-written Java DSL**: the declarative view DSL lives as a reusable Java library (`com.pathland.view`), not generated code — one ergonomic surface for desktop, server (Spring/Quarkus), and embedded hosts

1: //! # pathland-core-capi
2: //!
3: //! The minimal C ABI for the Pathland SPSC ring buffer + 16-byte opcode engine,
4: //! built as `libpathland_core` (a `cdylib`). Foreign hosts (Java FFM, Swift,
5: //! C#, …) construct the 16-byte opcodes themselves, allocate variable-length
6: //! strings into the bump arena, and push them into the shared ring **in
7: //! place** — the engine stays in Rust, the retained tree / diff stays in the
8: //! host language.
9: //!
10: //! ```c
11: //! void* h = pathland_core_create();
12: //! pathland_core_begin_frame(h);
13: //! uint8_t op[16] = { 0x01, 0x01, 0, 0, 1,0,0,0, 2,0,0,0, 0,0,0,0 };
14: //! pathland_ring_buffer_push(h, op);   // TREE::CREATE_NODE, id 1, vstack
15: //! pathland_core_end_frame(h);
16: //! // read opcodes zero-copy from pathland_core_ring_ptr(h)
17: //! pathland_core_destroy(h);
18: //! ```
19: //!
20: //! Opcode layout (little-endian): `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32]
21: //! [B u32][C u32]` — see `spec/OPCODE.md`.
22: 
23: use plcore::{Opcode, OPCODE_SIZE};
24: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
25: 
26: /// Opaque handle to a ring host.
27: pub type CoreHandle = *mut std::ffi::c_void;
28: 
29: /// The native host: owns the shared-memory ring + arena.
30: struct CoreHost {
31:     ring: RingTransport,
32: }
33: 
34: fn as_host<'a>(handle: CoreHandle) -> &'a mut CoreHost {
35:     assert!(!handle.is_null(), "pathland_core: null handle");
36:     // SAFETY: handles come only from `pathland_core_create`.
37:     unsafe { &mut *(handle as *mut CoreHost) }
38: }
39: 
40: /// Read a 16-byte opcode from a foreign pointer.
41: fn opcode_from_ptr(opcode: *const u8) -> Option<Opcode> {
42:     if opcode.is_null() {
43:         return None;
44:     }
45:     // SAFETY: the caller guarantees `opcode` points to ≥ 16 readable bytes.
46:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(opcode, OPCODE_SIZE) };
47:     let arr: [u8; OPCODE_SIZE] = slice.try_into().ok()?;
48:     Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&arr))
49: }
50: 
51: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
52: // Lifetime
53: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
54: 
55: /// Create a ring host over a fresh zero-copy shared ring. Returns an opaque
56: /// handle (non-null on success).
57: #[no_mangle]
58: pub extern "C" fn pathland_core_create() -> CoreHandle {
59:     let host = Box::new(CoreHost {
60:         ring: RingTransport::new(),
61:     });
62:     Box::into_raw(host) as CoreHandle
63: }
64: 
65: /// Destroy a ring host previously created by [`pathland_core_create`].
66: #[no_mangle]
67: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_destroy(handle: CoreHandle) {
68:     if !handle.is_null() {
69:         // SAFETY: `handle` is the pointer returned by `pathland_core_create`.
70:         drop(Box::from_raw(handle as *mut CoreHost));
71:     }
72: }
73: 
74: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
75: // Ring (guest → host)
76: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77: 
78: /// Push one raw 16-byte opcode into the shared ring at `writeCursor`, advancing
79: /// it. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the ring is full or `opcode` is null.
80: #[no_mangle]
81: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle: CoreHandle, opcode: *const u8) -> u8 {
82:     let Some(op) = opcode_from_ptr(opcode) else {
83:         return 0;
84:     };
85:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
86:     u8::from(guest.push_opcode(op).is_ok())
87: }
88: 
89: /// Allocate `len` bytes into the bump arena, returning the absolute arena
90: /// offset (a `u32` reference for `STYLE::SET_TEXT` / `STRING` property values).
91: /// Returns `u32::MAX` when the arena is full or `bytes` is null.
92: #[no_mangle]
93: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_arena_alloc(
94:     handle: CoreHandle,
95:     bytes: *const u8,
96:     len: u32,
97: ) -> u32 {
98:     if bytes.is_null() {
99:         return u32::MAX;
100:     }
101:     // SAFETY: the caller guarantees `bytes` points to ≥ `len` readable bytes.
102:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(bytes, len as usize) };
103:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
104:     guest.alloc(slice).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
105: }
106: 
107: /// Record the start of a frame (frame boundaries delimit a batch of opcodes).
108: #[no_mangle]
109: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_begin_frame(handle: CoreHandle) {
110:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
111:     guest.begin_frame();
112: }
113: 
114: /// End the current frame, publishing `frameCount`.
115: #[no_mangle]
116: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_end_frame(handle: CoreHandle) {
117:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
118:     guest.end_frame();
119: }
120: 
121: /// The monotonic frame counter published so far.
122: #[no_mangle]
123: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_frame_count(handle: CoreHandle) -> u32 {
124:     let guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
125:     guest.frame_count()
126: }
127: 
128: /// Pointer to the shared linear memory (header | ring | arena) for zero-copy
129: /// reads. Never null.
130: #[no_mangle]
131: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle: CoreHandle) -> *const u8 {
132:     as_host(handle).ring.buffer().as_ptr()
133: }
134: 
135: /// Total byte length of the shared linear memory buffer.
136: #[no_mangle]
137: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_len(handle: CoreHandle) -> u64 {
138:     as_host(handle).ring.buffer().len() as u64
139: }
140: 
141: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
142: // Events (host → guest)
143: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144: 
145: /// Drain pending raw `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring,
146: /// copying each 16-byte opcode into `out`. Returns the number of events
147: /// written (≤ `max`). `out` must point to ≥ `max * 16` writable bytes.
148: #[no_mangle]
149: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_drain_events(
150:     handle: CoreHandle,
151:     out: *mut u8,
152:     max: u32,
153: ) -> u32 {
154:     if out.is_null() || max == 0 {
155:         return 0;
156:     }
157:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
158:     let events = guest.drain_event_opcodes();
159:     let n = events.len().min(max as usize);
160:     for (i, op) in events.into_iter().take(n).enumerate() {
161:         let bytes = op.to_bytes();
162:         // SAFETY: `out` points to ≥ max*16 writable bytes; we write ≤ max slots.
163:         std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), out.add(i * 16), 16);
164:     }
165:     n as u32
166: }
167: 
168: /// Push one raw 16-byte `EVENT`-category opcode into the host → guest event
169: /// ring (the renderer reporting an input). Returns 1 on success.
170: #[no_mangle]
171: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_send_event(handle: CoreHandle, opcode: *const u8) -> u8 {
172:     let Some(op) = opcode_from_ptr(opcode) else {
173:         return 0;
174:     };
175:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
176:     u8::from(guest.push_event_opcode(op).is_ok())
177: }
178:

180: mod tests {
181:     use super::*;
182:     use plcore::{category, component_type, tree};
183: 
184:     #[test]
185:     fn create_destroy_round_trips() {
186:         let handle = pathland_core_create();
187:         assert!(!handle.is_null());
188:         // SAFETY: handle from create.
189:         unsafe { pathland_core_destroy(handle) };
190:     }
191: 
192:     #[test]
193:     fn push_then_read_back_via_ring_ptr() {
194:         // SAFETY: handle from create; all pointers valid.
195:         unsafe {
196:             let handle = pathland_core_create();
197: 
198:             pathland_core_begin_frame(handle);
199:             let op = Opcode::new(
200:                 category::TREE,
201:                 tree::CREATE_NODE,
202:                 0,
203:                 1,
204:                 component_type::VSTACK as u32,
205:                 0,
206:             );
207:             let op_bytes = op.to_bytes();

209:             pathland_core_end_frame(handle);
210:

212: 
213:             // Read the shared memory zero-copy and find the opcode.
214:             let ptr = pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle);

218:             let ring_off = u32::from_le_bytes(buf[0x06..0x0A].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
219:             let slot_count = u32::from_le_bytes(buf[0x0E..0x12].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
220:             let write_cur = u32::from_le_bytes(buf[0x22..0x26].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
221:             let slot = (write_cur - 1) % slot_count;
222:             let base = ring_off + slot * 16;
223:             let read_back = Opcode::from_bytes(buf[base..base + 16].try_into().unwrap());
224:             assert_eq!(read_back, op);

226:             pathland_core_destroy(handle);

246:             let buf = std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, len as usize);
247:             let arena_off = u32::from_le_bytes(buf[0x12..0x16].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
248:             let arena = &buf[arena_off..];

263:             let bytes = ev.to_bytes();
