# Pathland — Grant Proposal (Submittable Draft)

**Fund:** NLnet / NGI "Open Internet Stack" — new fund calls reopen **Sept 3, 2026**; deadline **Nov 3, 2026, 12:00 CET**
**Status:** Ready to adapt into the NLnet propose form
**Prepared:** 2026-08-31

> **Proposal name:**
> **Pathland — an implementable open UI-protocol standard: specification, conformance, validation, hardening, evidence.**

---

## 1. Applicant

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Legal entity | Apaq ApS |
| Country | Denmark (EU) |
| VAT / CVR | DK41717955 |
| Website | https://apaq.dk |
| Contact | Michael Krog · mic@apaq.dk |
| Role | Founder / lead developer (solo) |
| Capacity | Part-time R&D, 10 h/week during the project |

---

## 2. Problem

Server-driven UI (SDUI) and cross-platform UI are fragmented: each platform
re-invents retained-mode UI inside a closed framework (Flutter, React Native,
Compose Multiplatform, per-vendor SDUI like Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify). The result:

- **No open, language- and platform-agnostic *protocol*** exists for describing
  declarative, retained-mode UI — only frameworks that couple the UI model to a
  specific runtime.
- **No single wire format** serves the full spectrum from embedded (LVGL on
  microcontrollers) to in-browser to server-driven enterprise apps, so teams
  build and maintain N different UI transports.
- **Full-tree serialization is wasteful**: typical SDUI re-sends large JSON
  payloads; large, reactive trees cannot sustain high frame rates on the wire or
  on the main thread.

## 3. Innovation — a standard, not another framework

Pathland describes **WHAT** the UI is — structure + constraint properties
(VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment) — as a stream of **fixed
16-byte opcodes** in a ring buffer, and never **WHERE** (no layout, no rects).
Renderers are **pure functions of the stream**, so the same opcode stream maps
onto native widgets on every platform (GTK4, DOM/HTML, LVGL-planned).

The engine is **transport- and process-agnostic**: the producer and consumer
only need to exchange bytes, so it runs identically across embedded dual-core,
pure in-browser (WASM worker → `SharedArrayBuffer`), native desktop (C ABI /
Java FFM over a zero-copy shared ring), and distributed server-driven modes.

**Emission is diff-based and reactive**: a signal bound to a node re-emits only
that node's deltas; an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. That is what makes
the binary format dramatically smaller than JSON SDUI and fast enough for a
120 FPS interaction target.

The open-standard angle: anyone can implement a Pathland renderer or DSL in any
language against the spec and the golden conformance vectors, with no lock-in to
a runtime.

## 4. The specification (exists — split, not monolithic)

The normative spec is **already present** and is the contract this proposal
matures:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `spec/OPCODE.md` | 16-byte opcode format, ring buffer, arena, frame lifecycle, value types, design tokens |
| `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` | Primitive views + component IDs |
| `spec/MODIFIERS.md` | Core modifiers/properties + value types + enum codes |
| `spec/EVENTS.md` | Core events + listener bits |
| `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` | Golden byte vectors |
| `spec/DSL.md` | Authoring surface (SwiftUI-shaped DSL contract) — informative |

Gap this proposal fills: a **spec index + consolidated property-key registry**
and a **cross-language validator** so the split files read as one implementable
whole and cannot drift.

## 5. Scope & work packages (core-first)

The **core is the deliverable** (an implementable open standard); the visual
layer is cheap proof, not the product.

| WP | Deliverable | Issue | Effort (h) | Cost @€45/h |
|----|-------------|-------|-----------|-------------|
| WP1 | `spec/README.md` index + consolidated `0x0000–0xFFFF` property-key registry (derived, cross-checked against all four language surfaces) | #48 | 30 | €1,350 |
| WP2 | Machine-readable ID schema + cross-language validator CLI (Rust/Java drift guard) + expanded golden conformance vectors (validation only — codegen deferred) | #43 | 80 | €3,600 |
| WP3 | Coverage-guided fuzz harnesses (Rust/JS/Java), TS `stringAt` bounds fix, one Miri pass on the C ABI | #37, #38 | 70 | €3,150 |
| WP4 | Benchmark suite: 16-byte vs JSON/Protobuf SDUI (payload size, decode latency, memory) + one CI chart | #40 | 30 | €1,350 |
| WP5 | CI completion (rust + java jobs), hosted SSR HTML demo (URL + screenshots), evidence pack | #49, #50 | 35 | €1,575 |
| PM / reporting (10%) | NLnet reporting, MoU tracking | — | 15 | €675 |
| **Total** | | | **260 h** | **€11,700** |

## 6. Budget & rates

- **Cost-recovery**, rate **€45/h**, **260 h**, total ask **€11,700**.
- NLnet may adjust ineligible costs; the final amount is settled in the MoU.
- No other funding sources at present.

## 7. Evidence layer (the demo is proof, not the product)

The web path already exists (SSR HTML renderer + the demos' vanilla-JS `app.js`
client). WP5 makes it visible cheaply: host the existing Quarkus SSR demo at a
public URL, include 2 screenshots and the WP4 comparison chart. Reviewers can
click a working multi-renderer demo without the core work being a "black box".

## 8. Prior-art comparison

Airbnb, Lyft and Spotify ship proprietary, per-app SDUI JSON schemas — closed,
not an open standard. Flutter, React Native and Compose Multiplatform are
frameworks that couple the UI model to one runtime. Native toolkits (GTK,
SwiftUI, WinUI) are per-platform and closed. Generic serialization (JSON,
Protobuf) is schema-driven data transport, not a UI instruction stream, and
re-sends full trees. Pathland is a **16-byte command stream** (tree mutations +
properties), open-spec, process/transport-agnostic, with native-element renderers
and zero-copy, diff-based emission — an open standard, not another framework.

## 9. European dimension & ecosystem

- **Digital sovereignty**: an open, Apache-2.0 UI protocol reduces dependence on
  US-owned UI stacks — a "made in Europe" alternative for the Open Internet
  Stack's *independent and cross-platform development framework* area.
- **Open standards / interoperability**: spec + conformance vectors let any EU
  vendor implement renderers/DSLs; relevant to W3C/WebUI-type standardization.
- **Efficiency/frugality**: 16-byte opcodes + zero-delta emission cut bandwidth
  and embedded power vs JSON SDUI.
- **Engagement**: reach out to adjacent open projects (LVGL for the embedded
  renderer, W3C WebUI) and present at FOSDEM/IETF/W3C-style venues; publish the
  validator as a reusable tool for any SDUI adopter.

## 10. Timeline

| Milestone | Date |
|-----------|------|
| Submit proposal | Sept 3, 2026 (calls open) |
| Deadline | Nov 3, 2026, 12:00 CET |
| Decision / MoU | ~Dec 2026 |
| Project | Jan–Jun 2027 (6 months, 10 h/week) |
| Deliverables + final report | Jun 2027 |

## 11. Deliverables & acceptance

All software FOSS (Apache-2.0); all open outcomes open access. Deliverables are
WCAG-compliant where they include web surfaces.

- [ ] `spec/README.md` + consolidated property registry (WP1)
- [ ] Schema + validator CLI + expanded conformance vectors, CI-gated (WP2)
- [ ] Fuzz harnesses (Rust/JS/Java) + C ABI Miri pass (WP3)
- [ ] Benchmark suite + comparison chart (WP4)
- [ ] CI green (rust + java), hosted demo URL, screenshots (WP5)
- [ ] NLnet final report + MoU deliverables (PM)

## 12. Two-page narrative (copy-ready for the NLnet form)

**Proposal name:** Pathland — an implementable open UI-protocol standard.

**What it is.** Pathland is an open, Apache-2.0 protocol for declarative,
retained-mode UI that is language- and platform-agnostic. It describes *what* a
UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a stream of fixed
**16-byte opcodes**, never *where*. Emission is diff-based and reactive: only the
nodes that changed emit, an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes, and renderers are
pure functions of the stream that map onto native elements (GTK4, DOM/HTML,
LVGL-planned). The engine is transport- and process-agnostic, running from
embedded dual-core to in-browser WASM to distributed server-driven backends.
The spec already exists (split across `spec/OPCODE`, `PRIMITIVES`, `MODIFIERS`,
`EVENTS`, `CONFORMANCE`, plus the `DSL` authoring surface) and is enforced by
golden byte vectors.

**What we will build.** This project turns the working proof-of-concept into an
**implementable open standard**: (1) a spec index and consolidated
property-key registry; (2) a machine-readable ID schema and cross-language
validator so the four language surfaces cannot drift; (3) coverage-guided fuzzing
and a Miri pass proving the decoders and the C ABI are robust against malformed
input; (4) a benchmark suite quantifying the 16-byte-vs-JSON/Protobuf claim; and
(5) CI plus a hosted SSR HTML demo as live evidence. A solo maintainer delivers
this in six months at 260 hours (cost-recovery, €11,700).

**Why it matters.** An open UI *protocol* — rather than another UI *framework* —
lets any EU vendor build renderers and DSLs against one spec, reducing lock-in to
US-owned stacks and supporting the Open Internet Stack's cross-platform
development goal. The 16-byte, zero-delta wire format is an efficiency answer to
bloated JSON SDUI. Prior art (Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify SDUI, Flutter, React Native)
is closed or runtime-coupled; nothing provides an open, diff-based binary
instruction stream across embedded, browser, desktop, and server.

**European dimension.** Made in Denmark; Apache-2.0; engagement with LVGL, W3C
WebUI, and EU open-source venues; the validator and conformance suite become a
reusable tool for any SDUI adopter.

## 13. Open items (to confirm before submission)

- [ ] Re-verify the specific fund's eligibility page when the Sept 3 call opens
  (post-NGI rules may differ; NLnet's general policy accepts companies of any
  size).
- [ ] Confirm GenAI-disclosure preference (none used in this document's drafting
  beyond tool-assisted editing).
- [ ] Finalize the NLnet form fields: call topic, exact wording, attachments
  (budget table, screenshots, repo link).

Here's the honest comparison.

## Your track record (from git)

| Metric | Value |

| First commit → today | **2026-06-25 → 2026-08-31** |

**Scope delivered in that time:** the entire stack — Rust 16-byte opcode core (`no_std`, zero-alloc), diff-based reactive emitter + signals, view DSL, transport (shared ring + network batches), C ABI, **GTK4 renderer**, **HTML renderer**, the full **Java DSL + signals + annotation processor + state store**, Quarkus & Spring demos, the **six spec files + conformance vectors**, tests green, plus this week's CI + governance + grant prep.

So: **one person (with AI-assisted tooling) built a whole cross-platform protocol + 3 renderers + 2 DSLs in ~2 months.**

## The grant asks for

**260 h over 6 months (10 h/week)** for a *much smaller, well-defined* scope: spec index + registry (30h), validator CLI + conformance (80h), fuzzing/bounds/Miri (70h), benchmarks (30h), CI + hosted demo (35h), PM (15h).

## Verdict

**The proposal is comfortably conservative — by roughly 2–3×.** Based on what you actually delivered in ~2 months, the grant scope is realistically **80–160h** of focused work (2–4 weeks of equivalent effort). At 10h/week that's 8–16 weeks, inside a 6-month window. The buffer is a *feature*, not a problem: it's exactly what maximizes the "deliver on time, on budget, all artifacts public" outcome that unlocks the bigger grants later.

## Honest caveats (so you don't oversell)

What is Miri

**Miri** is a Rust tool that *interprets* your code's MIR (mid-level IR) and **detects Undefined Behavior (UB)** at runtime — `cargo miri test`. It's effectively a dynamic UB checker for Rust, and it's the standard tool for auditing `unsafe` code.

## What it catches
- Out-of-bounds / misaligned reads and writes
- Use-after-free and invalid pointer arithmetic
- Reads of uninitialized memory
- Memory leaks (with `-Zmiri-leak-check`)
- **Stacked Borrows** aliasing violations (the rules that make raw-pointer code sound)
- Data races (with the right flags, for threaded code)

## Why it matters for Pathland
The security-critical surfaces are full of `unsafe`:
- `pathland-core-capi` — `Box::into_raw`/`from_raw`, `std::slice::from_raw_parts` on caller pointers, `ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` in `pathland_core_drain_events`
- `pathland-core` (`memory.rs`) — the `no_std` ring/arena layout
- `pathland-core-transport` — the zero-copy decoders

A "Miri pass" means running `cargo miri test` over those crates' test suites so the interpreter executes the actual code paths and proves the `unsafe` blocks don't exhibit UB. Because the crate is `no_std` + a plain cdylib, it's a clean target for Miri.

## How it fits the toolchain
It **complements** the other WP3 items rather than replacing them:
- **Fuzzing** finds *inputs* that crash/hang the decoders.
- **Miri** finds *UB in the code paths that actually run* — bugs that may not crash today but are memory-unsafety landmines (and, for a binary protocol, security vulnerabilities).
- **ASan/UBSan** are runtime sanitizers for native builds; Miri is more precise on the `unsafe`-heavy Rust core.

Practical notes: Miri needs the **nightly** toolchain and is slow (interpreted), so the "one pass" is scoped to the core/capi test suites — which is exactly the right amount for the grant's "audit handled" evidence.

Here's the reframed plan.

## Strategic reframe

Two artifacts, sequenced:
1. **Product push (Sept–Nov 2026, full speed):** make Pathland a credible HTMX alternative for enterprise SRE — hardened client, resilient transport, observability, security, a11y, forms, docs, benchmarks. Target state at NLnet's **Nov 3 deadline**.
2. **Grant (due Nov 3, decision ~Dec):** fund only the **standardization/validation/trust layer** — things that build on the product and keep improving *after* it. The pitch flips from "help me build the product" to *"the product is live and proven; fund the layer that makes it a dependable standard enterprises can adopt."* That's a stronger pitch than the current draft, and it answers the "you built it in 2 months, why fund you?" question.

The inventory confirms the web path is a **demo-grade skeleton of exactly the right shape**: SSR + PLPL deltas + WS works, but there's no reconnect, no heartbeat, no metrics, no form semantics, no CSRF/origin checks (Spring `setAllowedOrigins("*")`), a duplicated unversioned `app.js` that can't apply TREE deltas and has zero JS tests, and Java/Rust renderers that already diverge (Java lacks IMAGE/ZSTACK/password/ARIA).

## Product push — workstreams (by Nov 3)

**P1 · Client + renderer convergence (days 1–10)**
- Promote `app.js` → single source `pathland.js` (versioned, minified, SRI, served by both demos), version negotiation, JS tests (vitest).
- Java renderer up to Rust parity (IMAGE, ZSTACK, `IS_SECURE`→password, ARIA, event attrs); Rust becomes canonical, Java a faithful port; HTML golden vectors.

**P2 · Transport resilience (days 10–20)**
- Client reconnect/backoff/heartbeat + **session-resync protocol** (server re-renders/replays on reconnect); `frameCount` sequencing + gap detection.
- Server-side batching (port the Rust `Batcher` time/size policy into Java), no-JS form-POST fallback.

**P3 · Enterprise hardening (days 20–35)**
- Observability (the SRE differentiator): Micrometer (Spring) + MP-Metrics (Quarkus) counters for sessions/events/frames/bytes/latency, health endpoints, structured logging, optional OpenTelemetry spans.
- Security: origin/host checks, `SameSite=Strict`+`HttpOnly`+`Secure` cookies, CSRF, rate limiting, CSP+SRI headers, JS decode bounds checks.
- Multi-instance: sticky-session + Redis (already there) + deployment/scaling docs (Nginx, WS, cookies, session TTL).

**P4 · A11y + forms + DX (days 35–50)**
- Form semantics: `<form>` + name/for/id pairing, autocomplete/required/maxlength, SUBMIT event, label pairing.
- WCAG 2.1 AA implementation on the HTML renderer (aria-live, aria-valuemin/max/now, menu keyboard/focus, alt, focus mgmt).
- Docs: getting-started, **"migrate from htmx" guide**, enterprise deployment guide; README visual (the screenshot/video from your earlier message) + hosted demo.

**P5 · Evidence & positioning (days 50–60)**
- Initial benchmarks vs htmx and JSON+SPA (payload/latency/memory).
- Spring demo becomes the **flagship production-shaped reference app** — the live evidence for both the README and the grant.

## Re-scoped grant (the "improve-after" layer)

Each WP is a *living artifact* that keeps improving as the product evolves:

| WP | Deliverable (re-scoped) | Why it's "improvable after" |
|----|-------------------------|------------------------------|
| WP1 | `spec/README.md` index + consolidated property-key registry | Registry grows with every new component/property the product ships |

## A. Positioning — "HTMX replacement" → "BFF + Rich Frontend paradigm replacement"

Broadens the pitch: today's enterprise stack is **BFF (a JSON API tier) + Rich Frontend (SPA with client state, hydration, bundle)** — duplicated models, API churn, client complexity, a11y/SEO bolted on via JS. Pathland replaces the *whole pattern*: the server defines the entire UI declaratively in the backend's own language, emits binary deltas; clients are thin (hydrate + apply + send raw events), and the same view works on native renderers (GTK) too. HTMX stays the closest analogue in the prior-art comparison; the SRE angle (server-driven = observable, testable, no client surprises, metrics on the opcode stream) becomes the headline.

**Note**: _Since there are variants, a comma indicates that we also want the `plain` class name version. So, request `grid-cols-{1..12}` even without a variant. If we don't add a comma after `sm, md, lg, or xl`, then the `plain` version won't be included in the compiled CSS, only the `sm, md, lg, and xl` variants will be._
...
A new syntax has been introduced that makes it easy to list numbers. This uses another pair of curly braces, where you specify the start and end points, and as a third value, the step size. For example, `{100..900..50}` means that you want every number from 100 to 900 in steps of 50; i.e., `100, 150, 200... 850, 900`.

content.text:
Research confirms the Tailwind-on-Rust story is real and current: **Tailwind v4 is the official Rust compiler** (`tailwindcss`/`tailwindcss-oxide` crates), and v4.1 reintroduced safelisting via `@source inline("...")` with brace-expansion/ranges (e.g. `@source inline("{m,p}{x,y,t,b,l,r}-{0..100}")`) — exactly the mechanism Pathland's class safelist needs. Config in v4 is CSS-first (`@theme`, `@source`), which maps cleanly to "default config out of the box + developer override."

Here's the integrated plan.

## 1. Architecture decision: single Rust HTML renderer, reused via C ABI

- **Rust `pathland-render-html` becomes the only HTML renderer.** It already owns a retained tree + `apply_frame`; it's fuller than the Java one (IMAGE, ZSTACK, password, ARIA).
- Expose it as a **`cdylib` with a C ABI** (`pathland_html_*` — create/apply_frame/render/render_fragment/css/destroy), mirroring the existing `pathland-core-capi` + `pathland-render-gtk` pattern.
- **Java `com.pathland.render.html` becomes a thin FFM shim** over that cdylib (same approach as `com.pathland.view.ffm`), so the Spring/Quarkus demos keep their API but the rendering is Rust. This *kills the Java/Rust divergence permanently* — there is one renderer, any language. C#/Swift later just bind the same ABI.
- The `pathland-core-capi`/FFM native-lib packaging story already exists; we add shipping the renderer cdylib per-platform with the Java artifacts.

## 2. Tailwind integration (in the Rust renderer)

- **Embed the Tailwind v4 Rust engine** as a crate. At startup the renderer:
  1. Loads the **default config** (bundled: `@theme` with **Inter** `--font-sans`, default palette) — a versioned, self-hosted Inter woff2 asset.
  2. Merges the **developer override** (a CSS/config file or string passed at startup — v4 CSS-first model).
  3. Injects the **Pathland safelist** as `@source inline(...)` (brace-expansion of every structural class the renderer can emit: `flex flex-col`, `gap-[Npx]`, `p-[Npx]`, `items-*`, `justify-*`, `text-[Npx]`, `rounded-[Npx]`, `border`, `opacity-[N%]`, `w-/h-*`, …).
  4. Compiles once, caches the CSS, serves it (`/tailwind.css` or inline `<style>` in SSR).
- **Renderer emission switches from inline styles to Tailwind classes**: stacks → `flex flex-col gap-[Npx] items-center`; padding/spacing → arbitrary `p-[Npx]`/`gap-[Npx]`; text → `text-[Npx] font-bold`; semantic tokens (design tokens) → theme colors (`text-primary`); borders/radius/opacity/size → utilities.
- **The color tension** (the one real design decision): Tailwind only generates classes present in content/safelist, and protocol colors are runtime-arbitrary hex. Options:
  - **A (recommended):** Tailwind for all *structure/layout/semantic-color* classes (safelistable), and *literal* runtime hex colors emitted via a bounded theme mapping + inline `style` fallback (so `bg-primary` stays Tailwind; a random `#A2B3C4` from a signal uses a CSS var/style). Zero recompiles, robust.
  - **B:** render the full retained view tree at startup, collect the *exact* emitted classes (incl. literal hex), inject them into `@source inline`, compile — all Tailwind, no inline styles; new colors at runtime need a (cheap, cached) recompile.
  - I lean **A** for determinism; **B** is more purist-Tailwind. Worth your call.

## 3. Updated roadmap (replaces the old P1 "Java parity")

- **P1 · Renderer foundation** (largest workstream): Tailwind class emission + safelist in Rust renderer · embed Tailwind engine + default config/Inter + override + compile-at-startup · C ABI (`pathland_html_*`) · Java FFM shim (Java module keeps its API) · demos switched to the shim · HTML golden vectors against the single renderer.
- **P2 · Transport:** as before (reconnect/resync, server-side batch coalescing, no-JS fallback) + client class-toggle support for STATE/SELECTED deltas.
- **P3 · Enterprise hardening:** observability, security, JS bounds — unchanged; plus native-lib packaging for the Java artifacts.
- **P4 · A11y + forms + SEO + DX:** now implemented *once* in Rust (Tailwind + ARIA); docs bundle incl. "migrate from htmx / BFF+SPA"; README positioning (BFF + Rich Frontend framing).
- **P5 · Evidence:** benchmarks (adds a Tailwind-CSS-size vs inline-style dimension — a nice SRE/caching story) · production-shaped reference apps · README visual + hosted demo.

## 4. Issue/milestone cleanup (additions)

New issues under the `Enterprise SRE · HTMX & BFF replacement` milestone: renderer Tailwind conversion + safelist · Tailwind engine embed + config/Inter + compile-at-startup · renderer C ABI + Java FFM shim + demos · native-lib packaging · client class-toggle · HTML golden vectors. The old "Java renderer parity" issue is replaced by "replace Java renderer with Rust C ABI shim."

## 5. Grant implications (re-scope stays "after," but structure now reflects this)

- **WP2 conformance** now targets the *single* reference renderer (golden HTML vectors incl. Tailwind class mapping) — cleaner and stronger.
- **WP3 fuzz** adds the Tailwind config/safelist parsing + class-mapping surface and the renderer C ABI (FFI/string safety).
- The **"one reference renderer reused across languages via C ABI"** becomes a headline interop/sustainability story for the proposal (improvable after, forever).
- Budget stays acceptance-driven (lean, cost-recovery).

## 6. Questions before execution

1. **Color strategy: A (theme + inline-style fallback, recommended) or B (render-at-startup to collect exact classes, all-Tailwind)?**
2. **Developer override form:** a v4 CSS/config file passed at startup (recommended), or a `tailwind.config.js`-style JS/JSON object?
3. **Java binding via FFM shim over the Rust cdylib** — OK to keep the Java module name/API but replace internals with the shim?
4. **Content scanning:** should the developer's own custom classes come from standard `@source` globs in their override (recommended), plus the Pathland safelist — or safelist-only?
5. Confirm **Tailwind v4** engine as the embedded compiler (it's the official Rust one — matches "its Rust library")?

Once you answer, I'll fold these into the final roadmap and start with the milestone/issue cleanup + P1.

All decisions are in — here's the **final consolidated plan**.

## Direction
Make Pathland a credible **enterprise-SRE replacement for HTMX and the whole BFF + Rich Frontend paradigm**: server-driven UI, thin client, binary deltas, observability/security/a11y as first-class. Full speed Sept–Nov 2026; grant re-scoped afterward to the standardization layer (decision ~Dec, submit **Nov 3**).

## Target architecture (the core change)

**Single, stateless, streaming Rust HTML renderer reused everywhere:**
- `pathland-render-html` becomes a **`cdylib` exposing pure functions** — zero retained state, zero cross-call state:
  - `pathland_html_render(batch, len, root) -> char*` — renders a **self-contained full snapshot batch** to a full HTML document in one streaming pass (decode map is transient; HTML appended straight to the buffer; no DOM, no retained tree — Option A).
  - `pathland_html_render_fragment(...)`, `pathland_html_free(ptr)`.
  - `pathland_tailwind_compile(override_css, content_sources) -> char*` — pure function called **once at startup**; the host caches and serves the CSS.
- **Tailwind v4 (official Rust engine)**: bundled default config (`@theme` with **Inter** + default palette, self-hosted Inter woff2) · developer override as **v4 CSS passed at startup** · content = **developer `@source` globs + Pathland safelist** (`@source inline(...)` brace-expansions of every structural class) · structural/layout/semantic-token → Tailwind classes, **literal runtime hex colors → theme mapping + inline-`style` fallback** (decision A).
- **Java `com.pathland.render.html` becomes a thin FFM shim** over the cdylib (module/package kept, internals replaced — old retained `Node`/`applyFrame` removed). Spring + Quarkus demos keep their code. C#/Swift bind the same ABI later.
- **Demo/session flow changes**: per-session full snapshot batch cached (emitter produces it at mount); SSR/resync/no-JS form-POST re-render via `pathland_html_render(cached_batch)`; WS deltas go to the client as PLPL (unchanged). The per-session Java renderer instance and `endFrame`-applies-to-renderer path are replaced.

Good requirement — it materially shapes the shim design. Here's how I'd handle Java 17+ for the HTML renderer shim, plus one flag you should decide on.

## The shim: JNA, not FFM, targeting Java 17

- **Why:** FFM (`java.lang.foreign`) is only final from Java 22. On 17/21 it's the `jdk.incubator.foreign` incubator module with a *different, per-version-shifting API* (`CLinker` vs `Linker`, packages changed, `Arena` only appeared in 19). Writing dual-path FFM code across 17/21/25 is genuinely painful and brittle.
- **JNA solves it cleanly:** works identically on 17/21/25, zero version-conditional code, and — importantly — **the repo already uses JNA** for the GTK renderer (`pathland_gtk_run` via JNA). So the HTML renderer shim follows an established pattern.
- **Concretely:** `com.pathland.render.html` becomes a JNA binding over the Rust `cdylib` (render + fragment + tailwind compile + free), compiled with `--release 17` (single jar runs on 17/21/25), native lib bundled per-platform (JNA extracts/loads it), and **CI tests the shim on Temurin 17, 21, and 25**.
- This replaces the FFM approach for this module; the FFM ring interop in `com.pathland.view.ffm` is unaffected (see flag below).

## Flag: the rest of the Java stack is Java 25 today

`com.pathland.view` (the DSL) currently requires **Java 25** (`ScopedValue` is final in 25, JEP 506) and uses FFM (22+) for the ring. So a "run it on Java 17" story is only coherent for the *shim* right now:

- If **shim-only 17+ for now** (my assumption): nothing else changes; the demos (which need the DSL) still target 25, but `pathland-render-html` is 17+ consumable standalone.
- If **full-stack Java 17+ eventually**: that's a separate, larger workstream — replace `ScopedValue`-based `ButtonStyle`/Environment (→ `ThreadLocal` or explicit `Environment` passing) and switch the FFM ring interop to JNA (or keep FFM with a 22+ floor). That's a real DSL-core change worth its own issue.

## Plan updates

- **P1 shim workstream** now reads: Rust `cdylib` C ABI · **JNA-based Java shim at `--release 17`** · native-lib packaging · **CI matrix Temurin 17/21/25** for the shim.
- **New issue** under the product milestone: "Java 17+ support for the HTML renderer shim (JNA, --release 17, CI matrix)."
- **Grant/CI note:** multi-JDK CI is a concrete enterprise-readiness evidence point; the 17+ shim also makes the "any language, one renderer" story stronger.

One question: is **17+ shim-only for now**, or should I plan the **full-stack Java 17+ workstream** (ScopedValue removal + ring interop) as part of the Nov-3 roadmap too?
Before we decide anything, what makes most sense? To support older LTS version or just focus on 25 LTS?

Honest strategic answer: **for the goal you've set, Java 25-only is the wrong bet — but the right floor differs by layer.** Here's the reasoning.

## The market reality
- Your target is **enterprise SRE teams replacing HTMX/BFF** — Spring/Quarkus shops. Spring Boot 3.x and Quarkus both run Java 17+.
- Enterprise LTS adoption lags ~2–3 years. Java 25 shipped Sept 2025 — it's **one year old** as of today. The overwhelming majority of your target audience runs **17 or 21**. A "drop-in replacement for HTMX" that requires bleeding-edge Java fails the first adoption test.
- Practical tell: **you can't even run the demos locally** (your machine maxes at JDK 22, which is why they're CI-only). If the author can't run the stack, enterprises certainly can't.

## But the cost differs completely by layer

| Layer | Cost of 17+ | Verdict |
|-------|------------|---------|
| **HTML renderer shim** | ~free: JNA (already used for GTK), `--release 17`, one CI matrix | **Do it. No debate.** JNA is version-agnostic; FFM would be a per-version-incubator mess on 17/21. |
| **`com.pathland.view` DSL** | Bounded: the *only* 25-only dependency is `ScopedValue` (ButtonStyle/Environment). Replace with `ThreadLocal` or explicit `Environment` passing — the render is a synchronous one-time mount, so ThreadLocal works. Plus JNA-ify the ring interop (FFM is 22+). | **Worth doing — but as a dedicated workstream.** |

So the real decision is: **shim-only 17+ (cheap, strategically hollow)** vs **whole-stack 17+ (bounded, strategically aligned)**.

## My recommendation
Go **whole-stack Java 17+**, sequenced:
1. **Shim 17+ now** (trivial, P1).
2. **DSL 17+ as an early dedicated workstream** (P1–P2 window): `ScopedValue` → `ThreadLocal`/`Environment`, ring interop → JNA, `--release 17`, CI matrix **Temurin 17/21/25** across the Java modules.

Rationale: your entire differentiation ("server-driven UI that drops into your existing enterprise stack") collapses if the flagship Java DSL requires Java 25. The refactor is contained (one mechanism swap in the DSL core), and it doubles as a **strong grant/enterprise-readiness evidence point** ("runs on every LTS from 17").

The only scenario where 25-only makes sense: if Pathland were positioning for *greenfield 2027 modern stacks* rather than *replacing HTMX in existing enterprises*. That's not the direction you chose.

## P1 · Java 17 whole-stack + unified native binding (first — quick win)

9: ## Overview

11: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
12: multiple renderer backends. It offers a declarative, retained-mode view API
13: (SwiftUI-shaped in ergonomics) designed to be **language-agnostic** and
14: **platform-agnostic**.
15: 
16: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
17: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
18: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
19: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
20: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
21: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
22: 
23: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
24: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
25: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`).

27: The **16-byte opcode engine is transport- and process-agnostic by design**. The
28: ring buffer is a plain region of shared linear memory, so the engine runs
29: wherever the producer and consumer can exchange bytes — no assumptions about
30: where the application lives. The same engine spans **embedded systems**
31: (FreeRTOS dual-core queues passing opcode slices between cores), **pure
32: in-browser client-side apps** (a WASM Web Worker producing into a
33: `SharedArrayBuffer` that the main-thread DOM renderer consumes), and
34: **server-driven enterprise architectures** (Java/C# backends emitting opcode
35: frames over WebSocket or gRPC). Transport and process boundaries are details of
36: delivery, never of the protocol.

39: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
40: change detection is fine-grained and signal-based — a signal bound to a node's
41: text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas, so only the things that
42: actually changed emit opcodes and an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.

## Enterprise positioning — replace the BFF + Rich Frontend paradigm

For server-driven web teams, Pathland is positioned as a replacement for the
**whole BFF + Rich Frontend stack** — and for libraries like **HTMX** that patch
around it. Today's enterprise stack pays for a JSON API tier (a BFF), a
client-side state model, a SPA framework, and a build pipeline, all to render UI
the server already owns. Pathland removes that layer: the backend **is** the
application. It declares the entire UI in its own language (Java, Rust, C#, …),
emits **binary deltas** over WebSocket, and the client is a thin hydration layer
that applies them and reports raw input back — no BFF contract to maintain, no
client state model, no SPA framework, no separate frontend team.

- **Server-driven, like HTMX — but a protocol, not a script tag.** The web
  client is a small vanilla-JS hydrator that decodes self-contained `PLPL`
  batches and applies opcode deltas in place; everything else lives in the
  backend, where enterprise teams can test, observe, and secure it.
- **Native elements everywhere.** The same opcode stream drives GTK4 widgets on
  desktop, DOM elements in the browser, and SSR HTML — one view definition, any
  renderer, any language.
- **Binary and diff-based.** Fixed 16-byte opcodes, zero emission for an
  unchanged tree, self-contained frames over the wire.
- **Enterprise-ready by design** (see Project Status): Java 17+ across the whole
  stack, a single Rust HTML renderer reused by every language, WebSocket
  resilience, metrics/health, security hardening, and WCAG 2.1 AA.

10: import java.lang.foreign.MemorySegment;
11: import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
12: 
13: /**
14:  * An {@link OpcodeSink} that writes opcodes zero-copy into the Rust SPSC ring via
15:  * FFM. Strings are allocated into the shared bump arena (absolute offsets). This is the
16:  * desktop/embedded path; the frame path uses {@code FrameOpcodeSink} instead.
17:  */
18: public final class RingOpcodeSink implements OpcodeSink, AutoCloseable {
19: 
20:     private final PathlandCore core;
21:     private final MemorySegment handle;
22: 
23:     public RingOpcodeSink() {
24:         this(PathlandCore.instance());
25:     }
26: 
27:     public RingOpcodeSink(PathlandCore core) {
28:         this.core = core;
29:         this.handle = core.create();
30:     }
31: 
32:     /** The opaque native handle (for direct ring access). */
33:     public MemorySegment handle() {
34:         return handle;
35:     }
36: 
37:     @Override
38:     public void beginFrame() {
39:         core.beginFrame(handle);
40:     }
41: 
42:     @Override
43:     public void endFrame() {
44:         core.endFrame(handle);
45:     }
46: 
47:     @Override
48:     public void createNode(int id, int component) {
49:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0);
50:     }
51: 
52:     @Override
53:     public void deleteNode(int id) {
54:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0);
55:     }
56: 
57:     @Override
58:     public void insertChild(int parent, int child, int index) {
59:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index);
60:     }
61: 
62:     @Override
63:     public void removeChild(int parent, int child) {
64:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0);
65:     }
66: 
67:     @Override
68:     public void moveChild(int parent, int child, int newIndex) {
69:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex);
70:     }
71: 
72:     @Override
73:     public void setText(int nodeId, String text) {
74:         int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
75:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, ref, 0);
76:     }
77: 
78:     @Override
79:     public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
80:         int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
81:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
82:             int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((String) value).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
83:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ref);
84:         } else {
85:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b,
86:                     ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
87:         }
88:     }
89: 
90:     @Override
91:     public void setDate(int nodeId, int days, int millisOfDay) {
92:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
93:     }
94: 
95:     private void push(int category, int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
96:         core.push(handle, new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c).toBytes());
97:     }
98:

100:     public void close() {

102:     }

1: package com.pathland.view.ffm;

3: import com.pathland.view.Button;
4: import com.pathland.view.Categories;
5: import com.pathland.view.Commands;
6: import com.pathland.view.Environment;

8: import com.pathland.view.VStack;
9: import com.pathland.view.View;
10: import com.pathland.view.emit.Emitter;
11: import com.pathland.view.emit.Opcode;
12: import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assumptions;
13: import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
14: 
15: import java.lang.foreign.MemorySegment;
16: import java.lang.foreign.ValueLayout;
17: 
18: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
19: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;
20: 
21: /**
22:  * Proves the desktop/embedded path: the Java DSL pushes raw 16-byte opcodes into the
23:  * Rust SPSC ring via FFM (zero JNI, zero-copy). Skipped when {@code libpathland_core}
24:  * is not on {@code java.library.path}.
25:  */
26: class RingOpcodeSinkTest {
27: 
28:     private static final int OFF_RING_OFFSET = 0x06;
29:     private static final int OFF_SLOT_COUNT = 0x0E;
30:     private static final int OFF_WRITE_CURSOR = 0x22;
31: 
32:     @Test
33:     void pushesOpcodesIntoTheSharedRing() {
34:         PathlandCore core;
35:         try {
36:             core = PathlandCore.instance();
37:         } catch (Throwable t) {
38:             Assumptions.assumeTrue(false,
39:                     "libpathland_core unavailable on java.library.path; FFM ring test skipped: " + t);
40:             return;
41:         }
42: 
43:         try (RingOpcodeSink sink = new RingOpcodeSink(core)) {
44:             Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
45:             emitter.mount(
46:                     VStack.of(Text.of("Hi"), Button.of("Go", () -> { })),
47:                     Environment.DEFAULT);
48: 
49:             long len = core.ringLen(sink.handle());
50:             MemorySegment ring = core.ringPtr(sink.handle()).reinterpret(len);
51:             byte[] buf = ring.toArray(ValueLayout.JAVA_BYTE);
52:             assertTrue(buf.length >= 64, "full linear memory buffer (header + rings + arena)");
53: 
54:             int ringOff = readIntLE(buf, OFF_RING_OFFSET);
55:             int slotCount = readIntLE(buf, OFF_SLOT_COUNT);
56:             int writeCursor = readIntLE(buf, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
57: 
58:             boolean sawCreate = false;
59:             boolean sawSetText = false;
60:             for (int i = 0; i < writeCursor; i++) {
61:                 int slot = i % slotCount;
62:                 int base = ringOff + slot * 16;
63:                 Opcode op = Opcode.fromBytes(java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(buf, base, base + 16));
64:                 if (op.category() == Categories.TREE && op.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE) {
65:                     sawCreate = true;
66:                 }
67:                 if (op.category() == Categories.STYLE && op.command() == Commands.Style.SET_TEXT) {
68:                     sawSetText = true;
69:                 }
70:             }
71:             assertTrue(sawCreate, "CREATE_NODE written into the ring");
72:             assertTrue(sawSetText, "SET_TEXT written into the ring");
73: 
74:             // The SET_TEXT string ("Hi") lives in the shared arena (absolute offset).
75:             int arenaOff = readIntLE(buf, 0x12);
76:             String text = new String(buf, arenaOff + 4, 2);
77:             assertEquals("Hi", text);
78:         }
79:     }
80: 
81:     private static int readIntLE(byte[] buf, int offset) {
82:         return (buf[offset] & 0xFF)
83:                 | ((buf[offset + 1] & 0xFF) << 8)
84:                 | ((buf[offset + 2] & 0xFF) << 16)
85:                 | ((buf[offset + 3] & 0xFF) << 24);
86:     }
87: }

content.text: Classic issue: the processor module auto-discovers its own `META-INF/services` processor during its compile. Standard fix is `proc=none` for the processor's own build:

input.newString:
<dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- This module ships the processor itself (META-INF/services); running
                         its own processor during its compile would fail on a clean build. -->
                    <proc>none</proc>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

179: The **hand-written, zero-dependency Java 25+ DSL** (no codegen). It is the
180: SwiftUI-like authoring surface shared by desktop, Spring Boot, and Quarkus
181: apps. Components and modifiers:
182: 
183: - `View` is an **open interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
184:   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button(View label, Runnable)` +
185:   `Button(String, Runnable)`, `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, and
186:   application code (Quarkus/Spring/desktop) defines its own views by implementing `View`.
187: - **SwiftUI-style `body()`**: composite views declare `View body()` (their subtree);
188:   the library's primitives override `render(Environment)` to materialize a
189:   `PathlandNode`. `body()` is evaluated **once at mount** — reactive values come from
190:   signals (`View.text(Signal)`, `Signals.computed`), not from body re-evaluation, so
191:   the emitter keeps its fine-grained `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` deltas.
192: - **Constructor props** (structural/layout: `alignment`, `spacing`) are
193:   constructor args, never chainable; **modifiers** (`padding`, `color`,
194:   `background`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `frame`, `opacity`, `border`,
195:   `visible`, …) chain on any view. No standalone width/height — use the
196:   compound `frame(width, height, alignment)` modifier. Typed enums
197:   (`Alignment`/`TextAlignment`/`FontWeight`/`Truncation`), not raw ints.
198: - **Environment scoping via `ScopedValue`** (Java 25+): `.buttonStyle(ButtonStyle)`
199:   injects a style down the whole child tree; `ButtonStyle.makeBody(Configuration)`
200:   with built-in `PlainButtonStyle` / `BorderedButtonStyle`. Custom wrappers via
201:   `ViewModifier.body(View)`. The `Environment` also carries the session's
202:   `PersistentState`.
203: - **Reactivity (Angular parity)** in `com.pathland.view.signal`:
204:   `Signals.signal/computed/effect/untracked` — lazy+memoized computeds,
205:   glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression, error caching, write
206:   discipline (`allowWrites()`), circular-dependency detection.
207: - **Persisted view state** (`com.pathland.view.state`): a `State<T>` field (e.g.
208:   `State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);`) is auto-wired to the session's
209:   `PersistentState` (keyed by field name, or `new State<>(0, "key")` for an explicit
210:   key) by the `pathland-view-processor` annotation processor, which detects `State`
211:   fields by type and generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per view class. Each view

12: - **Construction is `.of()` only**: every concrete view/control exposes a
13:   static `<ViewName>.of(...)` factory (`Text.of`, `VStack.of`,
14:   `Button.of(label, action)`, `Slider.of(binding, min, max)`,
15:   `DatePicker.of(mode, days)`, …); constructors are private and the former
16:   `View.*` static-factory surface is **removed**. `Slider`/`Stepper` are
17:   binding-first (initial value read from the signal); `Toggle` also offers the
18:   SwiftUI-closer `of(label, isOn)` overload; `Color.of(int)` alias.
19: - **One modifier mechanism — no sugar on `View`**: core modifiers are
20:   `ViewModifier` values (`Padding.of(16)`, `ForegroundStyle.of(color)`,
21:   `Border.of(color, width)`, `FrameMod.of(w, h, align)`, …) applied via
22:   `.modifier(...)` (single) or `.modifiers(...)` (several, innermost-first);
23:   the `View` interface has no per-modifier factory methods. Built-in and
24:   application-authored modifiers share the exact same surface (spec `DSL.md`
25:   §5.6); `buttonStyle` is the `ButtonStyleMod` value. Reactive overloads
26:   (`ForegroundStyle.of(Signal)`, `Background.of(Signal)`, `FontSize.of(Signal)`)
27:   re-emit only the bound node. Enum-collision modifier names use the `Mod`
28:   suffix (`FontWeightMod`, `TextAlignmentMod`, `TruncationMod`, `TextCaseMod`,
29:   `FontStyleMod`, `FontDesignMod`, `ControlSizeMod`); `FrameMod` avoids
30:   `emit.Frame`.

32:   (transparent container, maps to a `VSTACK` node today), `Text`, `Image`,
33:   `Color` (dual identity: a `COLOR` view *and* a value passed into style
34:   modifiers), shapes (`Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Capsule`, `Ellipse`,
35:   `RoundedRectangle`, generic `Shape.of(ShapeKind)` — all `SHAPE` nodes),
36:   `Button`, `TextField`, `Spacer`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
37:   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Divider`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVStack`,
38:   `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker`,
39:   `DatePicker`; `body()` composition; `ButtonStyle`/`ViewModifier`/`Environment`
40:   (ScopedValue).
41: - **Component IDs**: synced to the spec's grouped ranges (`Components.java`:
42:   `TEXT 0x01`, `IMAGE 0x02`, `COLOR 0x03`, `SHAPE 0x04`, `DIVIDER 0x05`,
43:   `SPACER 0x06`, `PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07`, `GAUGE 0x08`, `VSTACK 0x10`,
44:   `HSTACK 0x11`, `ZSTACK 0x12`, `GRID 0x13`, `SCROLLVIEW 0x14`, `LAZY_*`,
45:   `BUTTON 0x20`, `TEXT_FIELD 0x21`, `TEXT_EDITOR 0x22`, `TOGGLE 0x24`,
46:   `SLIDER 0x25`, `STEPPER 0x26`, `DATE_PICKER 0x27`, `PICKER 0x28`,
47:   `MENU 0x29`, `COLOR_PICKER 0x2A`, `COMMENT 0x7F`, …) — frames are spec-valid
48:   and cross-language correct.
49: - **Value controls**: `Toggle`/`Slider`/`Stepper`/`Picker`/`ColorPicker`/
50:   `Menu` bind to writable signals and route `VALUE_CHANGED` through the
51:   emitter's value-input registry; `TextEditor` mirrors `TextField`.
52:   `DatePicker` emits `STYLE::SET_DATE` (and re-emits it on signal change via a
53:   node-level date binding) and routes `DATE_CHANGED` through a dedicated
54:   date-input registry (`RenderResult.dateInputs`).
55: - **Events**: the full catalog round-trips — pointer, `KEY_*`, `VALUE_CHANGED`,

58:   (`Commands.Listeners`). `FrameCodec.decodeEvents` decodes all of them.
59: - **Modifiers** (modifier values applied via `.modifier(...)`/`.modifiers(...)`,
60:   chainable on any view): `Padding`, `ForegroundStyle(Color)` (no `.color()`),
61:   `Background(Color)`, `Tint`, `Opacity`, `FontSize`, `FontWeightMod`, `Border`

64:   `FixedSize`, `LayoutPriority`, `ZIndex`, `AspectRatio`/`ScaledToFit`/
65:   `ScaledToFill`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `FontStyleMod`/`Italic`/`FontDesignMod`/
66:   `FontWidth`/`Kerning`/`Tracking`/`BaselineOffset`/`LineSpacing`/`LineLimit`/
67:   `TextAlignmentMod`/`TruncationMod`/`TextCaseMod`/`Underline`/`Strikethrough`/
68:   `FontFamily`, `CornerRadius`, `Shadow`, `Blur`, `Saturation`/`Contrast`/

70:   `Clipped`/`ClipShape`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect`, `Disabled`,
71:   `AllowsHitTesting`, `ControlSizeMod`,
72:   `AccessibilityLabel`/`AccessibilityRole`/`AccessibilityState`, `ImageSource`,
73:   `PointerEvents` (OR-in), `ActionId`/`BindingId`, `TapGesture` (onTapGesture),
74:   `ButtonStyleMod` — `Color` is never a modifier.
75: - **Value types**: `ValueTypes.forProperty` mirrors `value_type_for` —
76:   `COLOR` family → `COLOR`; `VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`/`UNDERLINE`/
77:   `STRIKETHROUGH`/`COLOR_INVERT`/`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`/`IS_SECURE`/
78:   `IS_INDETERMINATE`/`FIXED_SIZE_*`/`SELECTED` → `U8`; `LINE_LIMIT`/`SELECTION`/
79:   `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS`/`BORDER_EDGES` → `U32`;
80:   `LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY`/`IMAGE_SOURCE` → `STRING`; enum-valued
81:   properties ride as `F32` holding the numeric enum code. `FontWeight` uses the
82:   spec's numeric 100–900 scale.
83: - **Signals** (`com.pathland.view.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
84:   `untracked` — glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression,
85:   circular-dependency detection.
86: - **Emitter** (`emit`): mounts once, stable ids, node-level binding effects
87:   (a signal change re-emits only that node), `FrameOpcodeSink` /
88:   `RingOpcodeSink`.
89: - **Wire codec** (`transport`): `FrameCodec` — self-contained `PLPL` frames
90:   both directions, `encodeEvents`/`decodeEvents` (host→guest events with
91:   `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section offsets).
92: - **FFM ring interop** (`ffm`): lazy `libpathland_core` binding, zero JNI.
93: - **State** (`state`): `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`, auto-wired by
94:   `pathland-view-processor`.

```

Naming agreed, and your styling question is exactly the right one — it's the crux. Here's how they connect.

## Naming: `@pathland/dom-renderer` (yes, it fits)

In Pathland's own vocabulary, a **renderer** maps opcodes onto native elements. The web client is the **DOM renderer** (the client-side counterpart to the GTK renderer and the SSR HTML renderer). So `@pathland/dom-renderer` + served `pathland-dom-renderer.js` is the consistent name. Confirmed.

## The styling question — and why it's the crux

Once the client supports **TREE deltas** (your call: include), it must *construct styled elements at runtime* — a `CREATE_NODE` + `SET_PROPERTY` sequence arrives and the client has to build a `<div class="flex flex-col gap-[13px]">`. But the Tailwind class mapping lives in the Rust renderer. So there are two honest ways to keep the mapping **single-sourced** (the project's core principle):

- **Option B — server-resolved style tokens (recommended).** Add one small STYLE command (e.g. `SET_CLASS`, pre-1.0 protocol change, allowed) whose `B` field points into the arena; the **Rust renderer resolves each style delta to a class token** (`gap-[20px]`, `bg-primary`) **or an inline-style token** (literal hex, per decision A). The client is maximally dumb: `el.className = …` / `el.style.cssText = …`. The mapping lives in exactly one place (Rust), the DOM renderer never duplicates it, and TREE-created nodes arrive fully styled via the same channel. One conformance vector + a paragraph in `spec/OPCODE.md`.
- **Option A — hybrid client mapping.** The client holds a small, golden-tested property→class map for the handful of structural props, inline-`style` for literal colors, and **CSS variables for semantic tokens** (Tailwind v4 theme tokens *are* CSS custom properties, so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` → `setProperty('--color-primary', …)`, zero class juggling). No protocol change, but the mapping is duplicated (bounded, golden-tested against Rust) and TREE-created nodes need the client map.

**Recommendation: B.** It matches the project's DNA ("one renderer, one mapping, dumb consumers"), keeps the DOM renderer trivial, and the wire is still 16-byte opcodes + arena strings. It's a small spec change while we're pre-1.0. A is the faster stopgap if you want to defer protocol changes.

Either way, the *static* SSR surface is Tailwind classes (server-compiled CSS, served at startup), and `STATE`/`SELECTED` class/ARIA toggles are a tiny bounded map in the client (already planned).

2. Confirm: `@pathland/dom-renderer` / `pathland-dom-renderer.js`, TREE deltas included, copy-to-demos, Node-in-CI.
1: A, as B is web specific and the protocol is not. 2: Confirmed

Locked. Option A is the right call — and your reasoning is the load-bearing insight: **the protocol must stay transport/renderer-agnostic**; web-specific class resolution belongs in the DOM renderer, exactly as GTK styling belongs in the GTK renderer. A `SET_CLASS` opcode would pollute a cross-platform protocol with web-only semantics. The DOM renderer owns the mapping, like every native renderer owns its mapping.

# @pathland/dom-renderer

The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A small, vanilla-TypeScript
hydration client (zero runtime dependencies) that:

- **Hydrates** the server-rendered DOM by `data-pathland-id`.
- **Decodes** self-contained `PLPL` opcode batches (bounds-checked) and applies
  them in place: `STYLE` deltas (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_DATE` / `SET_PROPERTY`) and
  **`TREE` deltas** (create/delete/insert/remove/move — runtime structural
  updates without a full reload).
- **Reports raw inputs** back over WebSocket as `EVENT` batches (pointer up,
  value/text/date changed), guest → host (flags `0x0000`).
- **Negotiates** the protocol version (mismatch → reload) and **reconnects**
  with exponential backoff.

Styling is **Option A**: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic; the SSR HTML
carries Tailwind classes (server-compiled), and runtime style deltas are applied
as inline style (overriding the current value), with literal colors inline and
semantic design tokens as CSS variables. The DOM renderer owns the bounded
property → style/class map (`src/classes.ts`).

## Layout

```
src/
  constants.ts   protocol constants (mirror spec/)
  plpl.ts        bounds-checked batch parse + string decode
  format.ts      f32/ARGB/date/float formatting
  elements.ts    component → DOM shell factory (TREE create)
  classes.ts     Option A style/state appliers (inline style + ARIA + CSS vars)
  apply.ts       delta application (STYLE + TREE) over the id → Node registry
  events.ts      guest → host EVENT encoders
  transport.ts   WebSocket connect/reconnect/version negotiation
  index.ts       bootstrap (hydrate + connect + listeners)
```

## Build & test

```bash
npm ci
npm test          # vitest (happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE apply, transport
npm run build     # tsc --noEmit + esbuild -> dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js (IIFE, minified)
npm run copy-to-demos   # copy the bundle into both Java demos' static dirs
```

## The bundle

`dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` is served by the Spring Boot and Quarkus demos
as `/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (copied into each demo's static resources by
`npm run copy-to-demos`).

## Transport resilience (P3)

`src/transport.ts` already reconnects with exponential backoff. Session-resync
and `frameCount` gap detection are the next step (the `onBatch` hook is the
seam) — see the "Web client: reconnect/resync" milestone issue.

# @pathland/dom-renderer (lib/typescript) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 1, 2026

The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A vanilla-TypeScript hydration
client (no runtime dependencies) that is the single source of the client,
replacing the two duplicated `app.js` files in the demos. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Single source, unified**: `src/` is the one client; `npm run build` emits
  `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (IIFE, minified via esbuild), and
  `npm run copy-to-demos` copies it into both the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos'
  static resource dirs. Both demos serve `/pathland-dom-renderer.js`; the old
  duplicated `app.js` is removed.
- **Hydration**: builds the `data-pathland-id → element` registry from the SSR
  DOM.
- **PLPL decode** (`src/plpl.ts`): bounds-checked batch parse — magic/version
  validation, truncated-opcode/string rejection, length-prefixed string reads.
- **Delta application** (`src/apply.ts`):
  - **STYLE**: `SET_TEXT` (text fields/editors/label spans), `SET_DATE`,
    `SET_PROPERTY` — strings (`LABEL`, `PROMPT`) and numerics (`SELECTED`,
    `VALUE`, `SELECTION`, `COLOR_VALUE`, `ENABLED`, plus structural style).
  - **TREE**: `CREATE_NODE`/`DELETE_NODE`/`INSERT_CHILD`/`REMOVE_CHILD`/
    `MOVE_CHILD` — the element shell factory (`src/elements.ts`) creates nodes
    at runtime and structural deltas apply in place (no full reload).
- **Event encoders** (`src/events.ts`): guest → host (flags `0x0000`)
  `POINTER_UP`, `VALUE_CHANGED` (f32 or raw bits), `DATE_CHANGED`,
  `TEXT_CHANGED` (string section).
- **Transport** (`src/transport.ts`): WebSocket connect, protocol-version
  negotiation (mismatch → reload), exponential-backoff reconnect, and a
  defensive per-batch try/catch.
- **Styling (Option A)**: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic. The SSR HTML
  carries Tailwind classes; runtime style deltas are applied as **inline style**
  (`src/classes.ts`), literal colors inline, and semantic design tokens as CSS
  variables. `STATE`/`SELECTED`/`ENABLED` toggle a bounded class/ARIA set.
- **Tests** (`test/`, vitest + happy-dom): codec round-trips (incl. a byte
  round-trip through `parseBatch`), TREE/STYLE application, event byte layouts,
  Option A style appliers, and transport (fake socket) — 38 tests.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Session-resync + `frameCount` gap detection** on reconnect (P3): the
  `Transport.onBatch` hook is the seam, but the client does not yet request a
  full snapshot or sequence batches.
- `ALIGNMENT`/`STATE` runtime enum semantics are applied best-effort; exact wire
  bit semantics need golden vectors (grant WP2 conformance).
- `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is not decoded yet (the Java DSL has no token helper; the
  CSS-variable path is designed but not wired).
- The element factory's base inline layout styles for runtime-created nodes are
  functional but not yet golden-tested against the Rust/Java renderers'
  class mapping (drift guard TODO).

## Verified by

`npm test` (vitest, 38 tests) + `npm run typecheck` (strict TS). CI runs the
web-client job (typecheck + test + build + copy-to-demos drift check).

Here's the full spec-vs-client gap analysis. Short answer: **no — it's a deliberate subset** (parity with the old client + TREE deltas + reconnect), not a full-spec client. Here's exactly where it stands.

## 1. Commands (spec/OPCODE.md:108–350)

| Category | Command | Client | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| TREE | CREATE / DELETE / INSERT / REMOVE / MOVE | ✅ **all 5** | `u32::MAX` APPEND sentinel handled naturally (index past end → append) |
| STYLE | SET_PROPERTY | ✅ | string (0x05) vs numeric; numeric appliers are a subset |
| STYLE | SET_TEXT | ✅ | text fields/editors/label spans |
| STYLE | SET_DATE | ✅ | days→ISO (`input[type=date]` only — no time/datetime-local) |
| STYLE | SET_DESIGN_TOKEN | ❌ | not decoded (token path in arena + value) |
| META | RESET / ENVIRONMENT | ❌ | not handled (server never sends today) |

## 2. Events — encodes **4 of 13** (spec/EVENTS.md:102–211)

| Event | Client | Note |
|---|---|---|
| POINTER_UP · VALUE_CHANGED · TEXT_CHANGED · DATE_CHANGED | ✅ | **POINTER_UP is partial**: sends target only, no `x/y` (f32) coordinates, no `POINTER_SECONDARY` flag |
| POINTER_DOWN / POINTER_MOVE | ❌ | no press/hover/drag |
| KEY_DOWN / KEY_UP | ❌ | no keyboard |
| FOCUS_CHANGED / EDITING_CHANGED / SUBMIT | ❌ | no focus/edit/commit for TextFields |
| SCROLL / WHEEL | ❌ | no ScrollView/scrollwheel |

Also: the spec gates reporting on **`EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005)** per-node — the client ignores the mask and reports pointer-up for every button.

## 3. Properties — applies ~21 of ~60 catalogued (spec/MODIFIERS.md:263–276)

**Supported:** `SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `PADDING` (+top/right/bottom/left), `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH/COLOR/RADIUS`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`, `WIDTH`, `HEIGHT`, `ENABLED`, `SELECTED`, `VALUE`, `LABEL`, `PROMPT`, `SELECTION`, `COLOR_VALUE`.

**Defined but not applied:** `SHAPE_KIND` · text (`TEXT`-as-property, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`) · layout (`OFFSET`/`POSITION`/frame/`FIXED_SIZE`/`LAYOUT_PRIORITY`/`ASPECT_RATIO`/`MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`) · `IMAGE_SOURCE` · typography (`FONT_SIZE/WEIGHT/FAMILY`, font-style/design/width, kerning/tracking/line-spacing, text-case/underline/strikethrough) · effects (shadow/blur/saturation/…/color-invert) · `ROTATION_DEGREES`, `SCALE`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `TINT` · `Z_INDEX`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_EDGES` · **`ROLE`, `STATE`, `EVENT_LISTENERS`** · `MIN_VALUE`, `MAX_VALUE` · controls (`STEP_VALUE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, **`IS_SECURE`** (no password input), `PROGRESS`, `IS_INDETERMINATE`, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `PICKER_STYLE`) · `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`.

## 4. Components — ✅ full shell coverage (28/28)

The element factory creates every primitive (TEXT…GAUGE, VSTACK…LAZY_HSTACK, BUTTON…COMMENT), so TREE-created nodes are structurally complete. Per-component *property* handling is partial (IMAGE ignores `IMAGE_SOURCE`; SHAPE ignores `SHAPE_KIND`; TOGGLE ignores `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants; STEPPER ignores `STEP_VALUE`; PROGRESS ignores `PROGRESS`/`IS_INDETERMINATE`). And the runtime shell can diverge from the SSR HTML (e.g. Rust renders `<svg>` shapes / `<input type=number>` steppers / `<input type=password>`; the client factory uses `<div>`/buttons) — a conformance/drift gap.

## 5. Value types (spec/OPCODE.md:137–144)

Client distinguishes STRING (0x05) vs numeric — fine for the F32/COLOR/U8 props it handles (raw `C` bits). Not special-cased: **ENUM (0x06, low byte of C)** and **DESIGN_TOKEN (0x08)**.

## The principled framing (important)

The DOM renderer **doesn't need to support every modifier** — only properties that can *change at runtime*, because static styling is baked into the SSR HTML by the server. So the real question is "which deltas can arrive at runtime, and which events must existing controls emit." By that lens the gaps divide into:

**A. Cheap + high-value (small, demo-visible, my recommendation to add soon):** the event encoders `FOCUS_CHANGED`/`EDITING_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`/`SCROLL`/`WHEEL` (trivial — no string payload), `IS_SECURE`→password, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`→time/datetime-local, `TOGGLE_STYLE` switch/checkbox variants, `PROGRESS`/`IS_INDETERMINATE`, `MIN/MAX_VALUE` on slider, `EVENT_LISTENERS` gating, `META::RESET`.

**B. Planned elsewhere in the master plan:** `ROLE`/`STATE`/ARIA class-toggles → **P5 a11y** (#65) and #61; `SUBMIT` + form semantics → **P5 forms**; `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`/`KEY_*`/`POINTER_MOVE` → **P3**; SET_DESIGN_TOKEN + CSS-var wiring → status.md already lists it.

**C. Large, low-value for the server-driven model:** full typography/effects/layout property application (the SSR HTML already carries them; runtime changes to these are rare).

# @pathland/dom-renderer (lib/typescript) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 1, 2026

The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A vanilla-TypeScript hydration
client (no runtime dependencies) that is the single source of the client,
replacing the two duplicated `app.js` files in the demos. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Single source, unified**: `src/` is the one client; `npm run build` emits
  `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (IIFE, minified via esbuild), and
  `npm run copy-to-demos` copies it into both the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos'
  static resource dirs. Both demos serve `/pathland-dom-renderer.js`; the old
  duplicated `app.js` is removed.
- **Hydration**: builds the `data-pathland-id → element` registry from the SSR
  DOM.
- **PLPL decode** (`src/plpl.ts`): bounds-checked batch parse — magic/version
  validation, truncated-opcode/string rejection, length-prefixed string reads.
- **Full delta application** (`src/apply.ts`):
  - **STYLE commands**: `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_TEXT`, `SET_DATE` (date/time/
    datetime-local), **`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`** (→ CSS variables, `src/tokens.ts`).
  - **TREE commands**: `CREATE_NODE`/`DELETE_NODE`/`INSERT_CHILD`/`REMOVE_CHILD`/
    `MOVE_CHILD` (`u32::MAX` append handled) — the element-shell factory
    (`src/elements.ts`) covers every primitive/control component.
  - **META commands**: `RESET` clears the DOM + registry; `ENVIRONMENT` accepted.
- **Full property applier** (`src/classes.ts`, table-driven): the complete
  spec/MODIFIERS.md + control/semantic catalog — layout (spacing/alignment/
  margins/offset/position/frame min-ideal-max/fixed-size/layout-priority/
  aspect-ratio/content-mode), text (align/line-limit/truncation/font-size/
  weight/style/design/width/kerning/tracking/baseline/line-spacing/text-case/
  underline/strikethrough), styling (color/background/border width-color-radius-
  edges/z-index/clips-to-bounds/padding*/tint), effects (shadow/blur/saturation/
  contrast/brightness/grayscale/hue-rotation/color-invert/rotation/scale/
  allows-hit-testing), semantic (role/state/enabled/selected/value/min-max/label/
  prompt), **structural control variants** (is-secure text↔password,
  toggle-style switch↔checkbox↔button, date-picker-mode date↔time↔datetime-local,
  picker-style/control-size as data tokens, step-value, progress/indeterminate),
  binding (action-id/binding-id as `data-*`), image-source, shape-kind.
- **Value types**: `U8`/`U32`/`I32`/`F32`/`STRING`/`ENUM`/`COLOR`/`DESIGN_TOKEN`
  handled (`enumCode`/`f32`/`isOn` decoders in classes.ts; token values in
  tokens.ts).
- **Full event encoders** (`src/events.ts`): `POINTER_DOWN` (x/y + secondary),
  `POINTER_MOVE` (x/y + hover enter/leave), `POINTER_UP` (x/y + secondary),
  `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` (keyCode + modifiers + repeat), `VALUE_CHANGED` (f32 or
  raw bits), `TEXT_CHANGED` (string section), `DATE_CHANGED`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`,
  `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL` — guest → host (flags
  `0x0000`).
- **`EVENT_LISTENERS` gating**: `src/index.ts` reads the SSR `data-event-listeners`
  mask (mirroring the Rust renderer's event attrs) and emits an event only when
  the node opted into it; absent attribute = permissive (no gating info).
- **Transport** (`src/transport.ts`): WebSocket connect, protocol-version
  negotiation (mismatch → reload), exponential-backoff reconnect, defensive
  per-batch try/catch.
- **Styling (Option A)**: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic; the SSR HTML
  carries Tailwind classes; runtime style deltas apply as inline style, literal
  colors inline, design tokens as CSS variables.
- **Tests** (`test/`, vitest + happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE/META
  application, design tokens, event byte layouts, and one golden assertion per
  property/enum — 73 tests.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Session-resync + `frameCount` gap detection** on reconnect (P3): the
  `Transport.onBatch` hook is the seam; the client does not yet request a full
  snapshot or sequence batches.
- **Canonical keyCode table**: `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` use the DOM `event.keyCode`
  convention; the renderer-shared canonical set lives in the conformance
  vectors (grant WP2) — cross-check on landing.
- **Visual tokens** (`PICKER_STYLE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`,
  `COLOR_MULTIPLY`) are applied as `data-*` attributes; their *visual* variety is
  renderer-styling-owned (Tailwind/theme), not the protocol's job.
- The element factory's runtime shells are functional but not yet
  golden-tested against the Rust/Java renderers' SSR markup (drift guard TODO).
- `STATE`/`ROLE` map to ARIA attributes; exact bit semantics should be
  cross-checked against the conformance vectors when they land.

## Verified by

`npm test` (vitest, 73 tests) + `npm run typecheck` (strict TS). CI runs the
web-client job (typecheck + test + build + copy-to-demos drift check).

Branch is pushed and tracking `origin` (4 commits: P0 positioning → P1 Java 17 → P2b DOM renderer → full-catalog pass), so CI is validating on origin.

**The next natural step is P2a — the renderer foundation.** It's the architectural crux of your stated requirements (single Rust renderer reused across languages + Tailwind styling), it's the largest remaining workstream, and the DOM renderer + Java-17 foundation you just built are its prerequisites. Everything else (P3–P6) builds on it.

## P2a breakdown

**0. Design spike (first, gates everything)** — pin the exact **Tailwind v4 Rust library API** (the riskiest unknown):
- Which crate exposes a usable library API (`tailwindcss` core vs `tailwindcss-oxide` napi vs third-party forks) · how to pass input CSS + config and get compiled CSS back · safelist via `@source inline(...)` brace-expansions for arbitrary values (`gap-[{0..N}px]`) · v4 CSS-first config-override merge · Inter font bundling (self-hosted woff2). Fallback if the library API is unstable: shell out to the `tailwindcss` CLI at startup (last resort — you asked for the embedded Rust library).

**1. Streaming stateless renderer rewrite** (`pathland-render-html`): retained-tree → one-pass `render(batch, strings, root) → String`; keep the fuller component/ARIA/event surface; switch emission from inline styles to **Tailwind classes** (component→class map) + literal-color inline fallback (Option A).

**2. Tailwind integration**: bundled default config (`@theme` + **Inter**) · developer v4-CSS override · Pathland safelist + developer `@source` globs · **compile-at-startup** (pure fn) · serve the compiled CSS.

**3. C ABI cdylib + JNA shim**: `pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` / `pathland_tailwind_compile` / `_free` (all stateless) · `com.pathland.render.html` becomes a thin JNA shim (removes the drifting retained `Node`/`applyFrame`).

**4. Demos switched**: per-session full-snapshot cache; SSR/resync/no-JS re-render from it via the shim; WS deltas unchanged; serve `/tailwind.css`.

**5. HTML golden vectors** against the single renderer; migrate the Java renderer tests to the shim; per-platform native-lib packaging; doc-sync.

**Risk to flag:** P2a touches the evidence layer (the demos must keep working through the swap), so I'd sequence the spike first and report its findings before committing to the full rewrite — the Tailwind crate feasibility shapes the approach.

## My recommended path
1. Confirm P2a as the next step.
2. Run the **spike now** (read-only research + a throwaway `cargo` probe under `/tmp`) and report findings — then we lock the approach for the rewrite.

Figure 1 (described textually): The v4 JIT compiler follows a 5-stage pipeline: 1) File Watcher (Rust-based, uses notify crate for cross-platform FS events), 2) AST Parser (parses HTML/JS/TS/Vue/Svelte files into a unified abstract syntax tree, extracts candidate class strings), 3) Class Validator (checks extracted strings against Tailwind’s utility registry, filters invalid classes, resolves variants like hover:, dark:), 4) CSS Generator (generates minimal CSS rules for validated classes, reuses existing rules via hash-based caching), 5) Output Writer (writes CSS to disk, injects source maps, purges stale rules). One of the most impactful changes in Tailwind CSS 4.0 JIT is the addition of a dedicated class validation stage, which was entirely absent in v3. In v3, the compiler would extract any string matching a utility-like pattern (e.g., bg-blue-500x) and attempt to generate CSS for it, leading to bloated output with invalid rules that browsers ignore. The v4 validation stage uses a preloaded utility registry from your Tailwind config to filter out invalid classes before CSS generation, reducing output size by up to 12% for projects with frequent typos or deprecated utility usage. To enable this, use the `tailwind validate` CLI tool (shipped with v4) to scan your project for invalid classes during CI runs, failing builds if unrecognized utilities are found. This catches issues early and ensures only valid classes make it to the final CSS bundle. For large projects with 1,000+ components, we’ve seen this step alone reduce CSS size by 180KB on average, as it purges years of accumulated invalid utility strings from legacy code. The validation also checks variant compatibility, so you won’t accidentally ship hover: classes for utilities that don’t support variants, which was a common source of bloat in v3.
...
Most v3 configs will work with v4 with minimal changes: the core theme, plugins, and variant config options are backwards compatible. However, v4 removes support for the legacy `purge` config option (replaced by the JIT `content` array) and deprecates several v3 utilities that were removed in v4. The `tailwind upgrade` CLI tool (shipped with v4) will automatically migrate your config and warn about deprecated utilities, reducing migration time to under 15 minutes for most projects.

 .scanner
 .scan_content(input.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect())
 }

 #[napi]
 pub fn get_candidates_with_positions(
 &mut self,
 input: ChangedContent,
 ) -> Vec {
 let content = input.content.unwrap_or_else(|| {
 std::fs::read_to_string(input.file.unwrap()).expect("Failed to read file")
 });

 let input = ChangedContent {
 file: None,
 content: Some(content.clone()),
 extension: input.extension,
 };

 let mut utf16_idx = IndexConverter::new(&content[..]);

 self
 .scanner
 .get_candidates_with_positions(input.into())
 .into_iter()
 .map(|(candidate, position)| CandidateWithPosition {
 candidate,
 position: utf16_idx.get(position),
 })
 .collect()
 }
...
#[napi(getter)]
 pub fn files(&mut self) -> Vec {
 self.scanner.get_files()
 }

 #[napi(getter)]
 pub fn scanned_files(&self) -> Vec {
 self.scanner.get_scanned_files()
 }

 #[napi(getter)]
 pub fn globs(&mut self) -> Vec {
 self
 .scanner
 .get_globs()
 .into_iter()
 .map(Into::into)
 .collect()
 }

 #[napi(getter)]
 pub fn normalized_sources(&mut self) -> Vec {
 self
 .scanner
 .get_normalized_sources()
 .into_iter()
 .map(Into::into)
 .collect()
 }
