content.text:
The spike has surfaced a **material finding** that changes the P2a Tailwind approach. Here's the evidence.

## Spike findings: there is no official Tailwind Rust *compiler* library

1. **`crates.io/crates/tailwindcss` and `/tailwindcss-oxide` → both 404.** The official Tailwind v4 Rust code is **not published as crates**.
2. **Tailwind's maintainers themselves** (discussion #16191, Feb 2025): *"Rust is used only for some code paths that are slower in JavaScript. Otherwise, the project is still mainly JavaScript-based."* And a 2025 PR note: *"The only place we use Rust (and NAPI-RS) is to traverse the file system and extract classes from your source files."*
3. So v4's Rust (`tailwindcss-oxide`) is the **class scanner** only — the **CSS compiler is JavaScript/TypeScript** (`@tailwindcss/core`'s `compile()`), distributed via npm/CLI, not a crates.io library.
4. crates.io "tailwindcss" search returns only third-party projects: `tailwindcss-to-rust` (codegen from compiled CSS), and **`encre-css`** — an actively-maintained (updated 2 days ago) *"TailwindCSS-compatible utility-first CSS generation library written in Rust"* — a **reimplementation**, not the official engine.

## What this means for the plan

The good news: **the safelist mechanism you specified (`@source inline(...)`) is CSS-level and works with any Tailwind compiler**, as do the default-config/`@theme`/Inter/override semantics. The decision is only *which compiler process runs at startup*:

| Option | Runtime | Tailwind parity | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Official CLI subprocess** (spawn `@tailwindcss/cli` or the standalone binary once at startup; feed it the assembled input CSS; serve the compiled output) | Node/standalone binary dep; ~1–2 s one-time compile | **100% official** — config override, `@source inline(...)` safelist, arbitrary values, plugins all work | Most faithful to "real Tailwind"; honors your functional intent (compile-at-start with safelist) but **not** "embedded Rust library" |
| **B. `encre-css` (embedded Rust)** | pure Rust crate, no subprocess | **Community reimplementation** — needs a parity spike (does it handle `@theme` tokens, `@source inline(...)`, arbitrary values like `gap-[13px]`, `@import "tailwindcss"`?) | Honors "run via a Rust library" literally, but compatibility risk + it's not official Tailwind |
| C. `tailwindcss-oxide` (official scanner) + hand-written CSS generator | — | infeasible: only the scanner is Rust | — |

**My recommendation:** **Option A** — it's the only way to guarantee real, current Tailwind v4 behavior (developer overrides, arbitrary values, plugins), and the user's "rust library" premise is based on a misconception the maintainers explicitly corrected. The architecture is unchanged (`pathland_tailwind_compile` stays a pure-function compile-at-startup with the safelist + override; only the subprocess replaces the "embedded lib" assumption). Option B is worth a **30-minute parity spike** (test `encre-css` against `gap-[13px]`, `@theme`, `@source inline(...)`) if you'd prefer an embedded, no-subprocess Rust dependency.

## Decision needed before I continue P2a

1. **A (official CLI subprocess — recommended) or B (embedded `encre-css` after a parity spike)?**
2. If B: want me to run the `encre-css` parity probe once we're out of plan mode?
3. Confirm the rest of P2a (streaming renderer rewrite, C ABI + JNA shim, demos switch, golden vectors) proceeds as planned regardless of this choice — the renderer's Tailwind-class emission and safelist derivation are compiler-agnostic.
Whta about https://github.com/cloud-shuttle/tailwind-rs. Is that any help?

`tailwind-rs` is in the same category as `encre-css` — a **third-party Rust-native reimplementation**, not the official Tailwind compiler — and it's actually a worse fit than `encre-css`. Here's why.

## What it is
From the earlier research: **"A type-safe, Rust-native implementation of Tailwind CSS utilities"** aimed at **Leptos/Yew/Dioxus** (Rust/WASM frontends). Its core (`tailwind-rs-core`) documents **"60+ CSS classes working perfectly"** with a `CssGenerator` (`add_class("bg-blue-500")` → `generate_css()`) and a `TailwindBuilder` (scan sources, config file, output CSS, tree-shake). It's a **curated subset** of Tailwind utilities built for compile-time type-safe class building — not the v4 engine.

## Why it doesn't fit Pathland's requirement
1. **No Tailwind v4 config compatibility.** Your requirement is the v4 CSS-first model: a default `@theme` config the developer overrides with their own v4 CSS. `tailwind-rs` has its own Rust `TailwindConfig` struct (`build`/`theme`/`responsive`/`plugins`/`custom`) and a file-scanner — it does **not** understand `@import "tailwindcss"`, `@theme`, or `@source`, so a developer's real Tailwind config/override wouldn't work.
2. **No `@source inline(...)` safelist.** Its class-selection mechanism is its own `config_file`/`scan_source` builder, not the v4 safelist syntax you specified.
3. **Coverage is a fraction of real Tailwind.** 60+ classes vs Tailwind's utility system (arbitrary values, variants, `@theme` tokens, plugins). Classes like `gap-[13px]` (arbitrary values) would depend on its own arbitrary-value handling — not guaranteed parity, and unmaintainable drift vs the real thing.
4. **Built for Rust/WASM frontends**, not for generating a CSS bundle for an SSR HTML renderer.

So it's the **least useful** of the three third-party options — same reimplementation risk as `encre-css` but with far less coverage and no v4-config story.

## Refreshed comparison
| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **A. Official CLI subprocess** (recommended) | Real Tailwind v4: `@theme` override, `@source inline(...)` safelist, arbitrary values, plugins — all work. Only the "embedded Rust library" premise is dropped (it was based on a misconception the maintainers corrected: v4's Rust part is only the class *scanner*). |
| **B. `encre-css`** (embedded Rust) | The only *serious* embedded-Rust candidate — actively maintained, "TailwindCSS-compatible", 24 releases. Worth a 30-min parity spike (arbitrary values + `@theme` + `@source inline(...)`); still not the official engine. |
| `tailwind-rs` | Not a fit — no v4 config/`@source` support, 60+ classes, WASM-frontend-oriented. |

**My recommendation stands:** **Option A** for real Tailwind compatibility, or **B (encre-css)** only if the "embedded Rust, no subprocess" constraint matters more than exact v4 parity — and I'd spike `encre-css` before committing either way. Want me to proceed with **A**, or run the **encre-css parity probe** (read-only research now, a `/tmp` cargo probe once we're out of plan mode) before deciding?
If we go with A, will it still be possible to deliver packages for the different languages that works out of the box? Fx for swift, java and .net

Short answer: **yes — Option A is fully compatible with out-of-the-box cross-language packages**, provided we treat the Tailwind compiler the same way we already treat native libraries: as a **per-platform binary bundled with the Rust renderer package**.

## How it stays "out of the box" for Java / Swift / .NET

The catch with "subprocess" is *which* subprocess:
- **`@tailwindcss/cli` via Node** → requires Node on the host. ✗ Not out-of-the-box.
- **The official Tailwind standalone binary** (self-contained, ships its own runtime; Tailwind Labs publishes per-platform builds — the `topcoat-tailwind` crate already downloads exactly this). ✓ This is the key.

So the packaging strategy is the **same pattern we already use for native libs** (JNA for the ring, cdylib for the renderer):

1. **Bundle the Tailwind standalone binary per platform** (`linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `macos-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `win-x64`, …) as a platform artifact alongside the Rust `pathland-render-html` cdylib.
2. `pathland_tailwind_compile` (the pure-function C ABI) **spawns the bundled binary** with the assembled input CSS (`@theme` default + developer override + `@source inline(...)` safelist + content globs) and returns the compiled CSS — compile once at startup, cached, served.
3. Each language package ships the platform artifact exactly as it already ships the dylib:
   - **Java** → binary extracted from the jar on first use (JNA's `Native.extractFromResourcePath` pattern; already how the ring dylib is located).
   - **Swift** → bundled as a framework resource (same as the cdylib).
   - **.NET** → shipped as runtime content (`RID`-specific), same as the native lib.

So any language that links the renderer package gets working Tailwind CSS **with zero extra install steps**, even offline (air-gapped enterprise SRE is a plus here — no network fetch at runtime). This is exactly how esbuild, SWC, and Tailwind's own `@tailwindcss/oxide` distribute native binaries (per-platform optional packages).

**Trade-off:** bundles grow (~10–30 MB per platform × matrix) vs **auto-download on first run** (slim packages, but needs network + a first-run delay — bad for the enterprise story). I'd recommend **bundling the host platform + a documented matrix**, keeping the jar/framework self-contained.

## The one real trade-off vs Option B

| | Out-of-the-box for Java/Swift/.NET | Tailwind parity |
|---|---|---|
| **A + bundled standalone binary** | ✅ no external runtime deps (binary rides with the native lib) | ✅ 100% official |
| **B (embedded `encre-css`)** | ✅ trivially (pure Rust in the cdylib) | ⚠️ reimplementation, needs parity spike |

So A costs one extra bundled artifact per platform but buys real Tailwind; B avoids the artifact but risks drift from official Tailwind (arbitrary values/`@theme`/plugins).

## My recommendation
**A, with the bundling strategy** — it keeps your "one renderer, any language, works out of the box" vision intact and uses the same per-platform artifact mechanism Pathland already relies on. The subprocess is hidden behind the C ABI; developers never see it.

My earlier "binary rides alongside the cdylib / Java extracts it" framing pushed too much onto the hosts. Let me correct it.

## Refined ownership: everything inside `pathland-render-html`

- **Build time** (`build.rs`): the pin-script downloads the pinned standalone binary for the target platform into `vendor/<target-triple>/`; the crate embeds it at compile time via `include_bytes!` selected by `#[cfg(target_os/target_arch)]`.
- **Runtime**: `pathland_tailwind_compile(config_css, safelist, ...)` (implemented in Rust) writes the embedded binary to a cache path on first use (executables must live on disk), chmods +x, spawns it with the assembled input CSS (`@theme` default + developer override + `@source inline(...)` safelist + `@source` globs), captures stdout → returns the compiled CSS. Cached; compile-once-at-startup.
- **Hosts stay dumb**: Java/Swift/.NET call the same C function and get CSS — they never locate, extract, or spawn the binary. The C ABI surface is unchanged.
- **Out of the box**: each platform artifact (the cdylib) is fully self-contained — one file, nothing else to ship. This is the strongest form of the "one renderer, any language, works out of the box" goal, and it works offline.
- **No `no_std` conflict**: `pathland-render-html` is a std crate (only `pathland-core`/`pathland-view` are `no_std`), so `std::process::Command` is fine.

## The one trade-off to confirm

Embedding via `include_bytes!` adds the binary's size to each platform cdylib (~10–30 MB — the dylib goes from ~1 MB to ~20–30 MB). The alternative is shipping the binary as a **sibling resource file** the crate extracts to cache on first use — smaller dylib, but two files per platform artifact.

| | Single self-contained cdylib (embed) | Slim dylib + sibling binary |
|---|---|---|
| Artifacts per platform | 1 | 2 |
| Dylib size | +~20–30 MB | small |
| Simplicity of packaging | simplest | slightly more |
| First-use | write embedded bytes to cache | ship + copy to cache |

I lean **embed** — the whole point is "one renderer, one self-contained artifact per platform," and 20–30 MB is a reasonable cost for a zero-config web renderer (esbuild/SWC ship similar native payloads). But if dylib size matters (e.g., embedding in app stores or tight deployment), the sibling-file variant is nearly as clean since the *crate* still owns the lifecycle.

# pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 1, 2026

The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming**
pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call
decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once,
and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer
Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)`
  / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML;
  the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed.
- **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy:
  `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`, `VSTACK`/
  `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/
  `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD`
  (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE`
  (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
  `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children + `SELECTION`), `MENU`,
  `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`.
- **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render
  the custom body wrapped in the native element.
- **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis flex), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
  `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL`/`HUG`), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
  `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
  `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`,
  `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA).
- **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` /
  `data-binding-id` attributes.
- `STYLE::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time).

## In progress (P2a)

- **Tailwind-class emission** (replacing inline `style` for structural/layout;
  literal hex colors stay inline per Option A) + safelist derivation.
- **Tailwind v4 integration**: embedded per-platform standalone binary (MIT,
  bundled per the pinned license), default `@theme` + Inter config, developer
  override, compile-at-startup (`pathland_tailwind_compile`), serve compiled CSS.
- **C ABI cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` /
  `_tailwind_compile` / `_free`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA shim).

content.text:
The collision is clear from the manifests.

## Root cause
- `pathland-core` → lib target `pathland_core`, produces `libpathland_core.rlib`.
- `pathland-core-capi` → lib target also named `pathland_core` with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` → produces **both** `libpathland_core.dylib` (needed by the Java JNA binding) **and** `libpathland_core.rlib` — the `.rlib` collides with `pathland-core`'s.

The crate already aliases its *dependency* (`plcore`) to avoid a dependency-name collision, but not its own *output* rlib.

## Fix (recommended): drop the rlib from `pathland-core-capi`

`crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` → `["cdylib"]`

**Why this is safe and minimal:**
- `pathland-core-capi` is the C-ABI facade for **foreign hosts** (Java via JNA) — it has **no Rust rlib consumers** (grep confirms: only workspace membership, no test dirs, no other crate depends on it).
- The load-bearing artifact — `libpathland_core.dylib` (what `PathlandCore.resolveLibraryPath()`/JNA loads by name) — is **unchanged**.
- CI's `cargo build -p pathland-core-capi` still builds the cdylib.
- One-line change, no Java/docs/AGENTS/status churn.

## Alternative (not recommended)
Rename the capi lib target to `pathland_core_capi` (→ `libpathland_core_capi.dylib`). Cleaner naming but **more churn**: the Java `PathlandCore.resolveLibraryPath()`, AGENTS.md, and status.md all reference `libpathland_core`, so they'd all need updating for zero functional benefit.

## Verification after the fix
1. `cargo build` at `lib/rust` — no `output filename collision` warning.
2. `ls target/debug/libpathland_core.dylib` still present.
3. `cargo test` workspace green (capi has no tests; the Java JNA ring test loads the unchanged dylib).

content.text:
Root cause found — and it's **not** the session cookie.

## Diagnosis

**The cookie is fine.** `IndexController.java:32` sets `session` on the `/` response (path `/`, same-origin WebSocket carries it), so the browser has it. Even if it were missing, the symptom would be coincidental, not causal.

**The real bug: the new DOM renderer's TREE application clobbers hydration.**

The flow that breaks:
1. Browser hydrates the SSR DOM → `byId` = the visible SSR elements.
2. On WS connect, the server **replays the full initial mount frame** — `CREATE_NODE`/`INSERT_CHILD` for the whole tree (SessionApp.java:78–84).
3. The client's `applyTree` (apply.ts:86–93) on `CREATE_NODE` **always creates a fresh, detached element** and `byId.set(id, el)` — **replacing** the hydrated element. `INSERT_CHILD` (102–112) then re-inserts the fresh nodes into detached parents.
4. Result: `byId` now points to **detached** elements; the SSR elements remain visible but orphaned. Every subsequent delta (`SET_TEXT`, `SET_PROPERTY`) targets a detached node → **events reach the server, state changes, deltas are sent, but nothing visibly updates.**

The old `app.js` **ignored TREE opcodes entirely** and applied STYLE deltas straight to the hydrated elements — which is why this worked before P2b introduced TREE support.

## Fix plan (`lib/typescript/src/apply.ts`)

1. **`CREATE_NODE`** — reuse the existing hydrated element when the id is already in `byId`; only create a fresh element when absent:
   ```ts
   let el = r.byId.get(op.a);
   if (!el) { el = createElement(op.b); if (el.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE) (el as HTMLElement).setAttribute("data-pathland-id", String(op.a)); r.byId.set(op.a, el); }
   ```
2. **`INSERT_CHILD`** — skip when the child is already inside the parent's container (`container.contains(child)`), making replay/hydration idempotent and preventing duplicates.
3. **Regression test** — hydrate an SSR DOM, apply a full mount frame (TREE + STYLE), assert **no duplicates** and that a later `SET_TEXT` updates the *visible hydrated* element.
4. Rebuild `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` → `copy-to-demos` → status.md note.

Genuine runtime structural changes still work: a real add arrives as `CREATE` for a **new** id (absent → created) + `INSERT` (not contained → inserted); a replace arrives as `DELETE` (removes + unregisters) then `CREATE`.

The emitter already keeps the retained tree and `emitNode(tree)` walks it, so a `renderFull()` that re-emits the whole tree on demand is straightforward. Here's the plan.

## The design (per your directive)
**The client's UI = the SSR HTML.** On WS connect the server sends **no** full tree; it only streams deltas. A full snapshot is sent **only when the client explicitly requests it** (a `resync` request).

## Server (Java demos — Spring + Quarkus mirrored)

1. **`Emitter.renderFull()`** (`pathland-view`): re-emit the complete retained tree as one full-snapshot frame (store the `tree` field; `emitNode(tree)` inside a frame boundary). Used by resync + no-JS/P3. Feasible — no state re-wiring, no re-mount.
2. **`SessionApp`**: remove the `pending` replay on connect (the mount frame is no longer sent; the client already has SSR). `connect()` just attaches the session. Add `resync()` → `emitter.renderFull()` (the sink's `endFrame` sends it).
3. **`PathlandSocket`** (Spring + Quarkus): handle a WS **text message** `"resync"` → `session.resync()`. (Currently binary-only handlers; adding text handling is small.)
4. `PathlandService`: expose the resync path (session lookup).

## Client (`lib/typescript`)

5. **Hydration-aware TREE reconciliation** (`apply.ts`) — still required so a resync'd full snapshot reconciles against the hydrated DOM without clobbering/duplicating:
   - `CREATE_NODE`: **reuse** the existing hydrated element when the id is already in `byId`; only create when absent.
   - `INSERT_CHILD`: skip when the child is already inside the parent's container.
6. **Resync on reconnect**: `Transport` sends a `"resync"` text message after a reconnect — the first concrete use of "when specifically asked" (recovers missed deltas). P3 formalizes gap detection; this makes reconnects correct now.

## Why this fixes the reported bug
No mount frame over WS → the client keeps its SSR-hydrated `byId` → deltas (SET_TEXT etc.) target the visible hydrated elements → UI updates. (The session cookie is correctly set by `IndexController` and remains the SSR↔WS session-aligner — it wasn't the cause.)

## Questions before I implement
1. **Resync request format**: WS text `"resync"` (pragmatic, no spec change) — recommended — or a protocol `META::RESYNC` opcode (protocol-first, small spec change + conformance vector)? I'd take text now, formalize an opcode in P3.
2. **Confirm**: remove the `pending` buffer entirely (mount frame never buffered/sent), and wire the client to send `resync` after reconnect as part of this change?
1: protocol first
1: protocl first. 2: OK. And tell me if it is not more performant to do it like this where we do not resync on connect

Protocol-first it is. Here's the finalized plan plus the performance answer.

## Performance: yes, this is more performant — and the reasons matter

Under the old flow the full tree was transmitted **twice** per connection: once as SSR HTML, then again as the WS mount frame. The new flow is strictly better:

1. **Bandwidth** — the WS mount frame was pure duplication of what SSR already delivered. For the kitchensink it's a few KB; for a real enterprise dashboard (the actual target) it's hundreds of KB × every connection. Removed.
2. **Latency / time-to-interactive** — the client is interactive immediately from SSR (progressive enhancement: it works even before/without WS); deltas apply to the already-visible tree the moment the socket opens. No waiting for a mount frame.
3. **Server CPU** — no re-encoding + re-transmitting the full snapshot per WS connection; and the per-session `pending` buffer goes away.
4. **Protocol coherence** — "Only Changes Matter" is the design contract; re-sending the full tree on connect violated it.
5. **Resync-on-demand** — the snapshot is sent only when the client *asks*, i.e. exactly when it's needed (reconnect after a missed gap).

**The one honest cost:** correctness after a silent reconnect now depends on the resync-on-demand mechanism + gap detection. For now the client resyncs on **every** reconnect (cheap and safe — it missed the deltas during the gap); P3's `frameCount` sequencing lets it resync only when a gap is actually detected. That's a small, well-understood trade — more performant happy path, recovery costs only when recovery is needed.

## Plan — protocol-first `META::RESYNC` (guest→host)

**Spec / protocol**
1. `spec/OPCODE.md` — add `META::RESYNC` (`0x03`, **guest→host**, A/B/C = 0): "the guest requests a full snapshot of the current tree" (reconnect/gap recovery, no-JS refresh). The host responds with a full-snapshot batch.
2. `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` — golden byte vector for the RESYNC batch.
3. `pathland-core` `constants.rs` — `meta::RESYNC = 0x03`; Java `Commands.Meta.RESYNC = 0x03`; Rust transport `encode_resync()` helper (symmetry).

**Server (Java demos, Spring + Quarkus mirrored)**
4. `Emitter.renderFull()` — store the retained `tree` field; re-emit the full tree as one snapshot frame (no re-mount, no state re-wiring).
5. `SessionApp` — **remove the `pending` replay on connect** (mount frame never buffered/sent); add `resync()` → `emitter.renderFull()`.
6. `PathlandSocket` — in the binary handler, check `FrameCodec.isResync(message)` → `session.resync()`; else dispatch events as today.

**Client (`lib/typescript`)**
7. `encodeResync()` — guest→host batch with one `META::RESYNC` opcode.
8. `Transport` — send `encodeResync()` after **reconnect** (not first connect, per the design).
9. **Hydration-aware TREE reconciliation** (`apply.ts`) — `CREATE_NODE` reuses an existing hydrated element; `INSERT_CHILD` skips when already contained — so a resync'd full snapshot reconciles against the hydrated DOM without clobbering/duplicating.

**Tests + docs**
10. Client: resync encoder byte-layout + hydration-reconciliation regression (hydrated DOM + full snapshot → no duplicates, deltas target the visible element). Java: `FrameCodec` resync round-trip + `Emitter.renderFull()` test. Rust: constants conformance.
11. status.md updates (`pathland-view`, dom-renderer) + AGENTS.md note (no-replay-on-connect + `META::RESYNC`).

Two confirmations: (a) `META::RESYNC = 0x03` (after `RESET 0x01`, `ENVIRONMENT 0x02`) — ok? (b) Include the Rust `encode_resync()` transport helper now (for symmetry), or defer to when a Rust server exists?
a: yes. b: include. And still do the fix. And create an issue that state that the META opcodes need to be revisited for refactoring

All decisions locked. One important correction from the direction analysis (which also justifies the refactoring issue): **`META::RESYNC` is `host → guest`, not guest→host.** In Pathland's vocabulary the host is the renderer (the client) and the guest is the application (the server) — so the DOM renderer requesting a re-snapshot is **host→guest**, the same direction as `ENVIRONMENT` and the `EVENT` category (client→server over the network). This is exactly the kind of muddle the refactoring issue captures.

## Final plan — no-replay-on-connect + protocol-first `META::RESYNC`

**Spec / protocol**
1. `spec/OPCODE.md` — add `META::RESYNC` (`0x03`, **host→guest**, A/B/C=0): *"the host (renderer) requests the guest (application) to send a full snapshot of the current tree"* (reconnect/gap recovery, no-JS refresh). The guest responds with a full-snapshot batch.
2. `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` — golden byte vector for the RESYNC batch.
3. `pathland-core` `constants.rs` — `meta::RESYNC = 0x03`; Java `Commands.Meta.RESYNC = 0x03`; Rust transport **`encode_resync()`** (included per your call).

**Server (Java demos, Spring + Quarkus mirrored)**
4. `Emitter.renderFull()` — store the retained `tree` field; re-emit the full tree as one snapshot frame (no re-mount/state re-wiring).
5. `SessionApp` — **remove the `pending` replay on connect** (mount frame never buffered/sent); add `resync()` → `emitter.renderFull()`.
6. `PathlandSocket` — in the binary handler, check `FrameCodec.isResync(message)` first → `session.resync()`; else dispatch events as today.

**Client (`lib/typescript`)**
7. `encodeResync()` — host→guest batch with one `META::RESYNC` opcode.
8. `Transport` — send `encodeResync()` after **reconnect** (tracked via the attempt counter; never on first connect).
9. **Hydration-aware TREE reconciliation** (`apply.ts`) — `CREATE_NODE` reuses an existing hydrated element; `INSERT_CHILD` skips when already contained — so a resync'd snapshot reconciles against the hydrated DOM without clobbering/duplicating.

**Tests + docs**
10. Client: resync byte-layout + hydration-reconciliation regression (hydrated DOM + full snapshot → no duplicates, deltas target the visible element). Java: `FrameCodec` resync encode/detect round-trip + `Emitter.renderFull()` test. Rust: constants conformance + `encode_resync()` round-trip.
11. status.md updates (`pathland-view`, dom-renderer) + AGENTS.md note (no-replay-on-connect + `META::RESYNC`).

## Issue to file on exit (Backlog milestone)

**Title:** `Revisit META opcodes for refactoring`
**Body:** META currently mixes directions and host/guest semantics are confusing over the network (host = renderer/client, guest = app/server): `RESET` (0x01) is guest→host ("host clears output"), `ENVIRONMENT` (0x02) and the new `RESYNC` (0x03) are host→guest. Proposals to consider: split META into direction-tagged command sets (e.g. a guest→host control category vs host→guest environment/resync), clarify each command's host/guest meaning over the wire, decide whether `RESET` should subsume/trigger a resync, and document the full-snapshot response semantics. Protocol change → spec/OPCODE.md + CONFORMANCE vectors + cross-language constants in one pass.

**Performance note (already established):** yes, this is strictly more performant — no duplicated full-tree transmission per connection, faster TTI from SSR, less server CPU, aligned with "only changes matter"; the one cost (recovery after a silent reconnect) is handled by resync-on-reconnect now and `frameCount` gap detection in P3.

This is ready to execute. On exit from plan mode I'll: file the issue, then implement spec+constants+codecs (Rust/Java/TS), then `Emitter.renderFull()` + demo changes (Spring + Quarkus), then the client (encodeResync, transport-on-reconnect, hydration-aware TREE), then tests + rebuild/copy + docs, verifying at each checkpoint.

Done and committed as `839f4be`. The fix addresses your original hypothesis with the better design you directed.

## What was wrong
Your cookie theory was the red herring — the cookie is correctly set. The real bug: the server **replayed the full mount frame over WS on connect**, and the DOM renderer's `CREATE_NODE` always built a fresh detached element, so `byId` pointed at clones while the visible SSR DOM stayed orphaned → events reached the server, deltas were sent, nothing updated.

## The fix (protocol-first, per your directive)
**The server never replays the full tree on connect** — the client already has the UI from the SSR HTML. A full snapshot is sent **only** when the client explicitly asks via the new **`META::RESYNC`** opcode.

- **Spec**: `META::RESYNC` (0x03, host→guest) in `spec/OPCODE.md` + golden vectors (opcode + host→guest batch) in `CONFORMANCE.md`.
- **Rust**: `meta::RESYNC`, `encode_resync()` (host→guest).
- **Java**: `Commands.Meta.RESYNC`, `FrameCodec.encodeResync`/`isResync`, `Emitter.renderFull()` (re-emits retained tree as a snapshot); both `SessionApp`s dropped the `pending` replay + added `resync()`; both sockets detect `isResync` → resync.
- **Client**: `encodeResync()`; `Transport` sends it **after reconnect** (never first connect); **hydration-aware TREE reconciliation** (reuse hydrated element on CREATE, skip already-contained on INSERT) so a resync snapshot reconciles without clobbering/duplicating.

## Verified
- **TS: 77 tests** (resync bytes, hydration reconciliation, resync-on-reconnect) · **Java: 35** (+resync codec, renderFull) · **Rust workspace: 25 suites** · bundle rebuilt + copied to both demos (drift-matched).

## Also
- **Issue #74** filed (Backlog): *"Revisit META opcodes for refactoring"* — it captures the host/guest direction muddle (`RESET` guest→host vs `ENVIRONMENT`/`RESYNC` host→guest) that surfaced during this work.
- Performance confirmed: this is strictly more performant than the old replay — no duplicated full-tree transmission per connection, faster TTI from SSR, aligned with "only changes matter." Recovery after a silent reconnect is handled by resync-on-reconnect now; `frameCount` gap detection is P3.

## Where we are
The web/renderer foundation is in strong shape: Java 17+ whole-stack, unified TypeScript DOM renderer with full-catalog conformance + hydration-safe resync, and the Rust renderer now **stateless-streaming + C-ABI** (the cross-language surface). The one unfinished line in the enterprise-SRE milestone is **P2a's Tailwind integration** — the biggest remaining architectural piece.

## Recommended next: finish P2a — the Tailwind-class emission + embedded-binary integration

This is the logical continuation of the renderer work you already committed, and it completes the two requirements you stated explicitly at the outset (single Rust renderer reused across languages **+ Tailwind styling with default config/override/safelist**). Concretely:

**A. Tailwind-class emission** (`pathland-render-html`) — the highest-churn step:
- Replace inline `style` with Tailwind utility classes for structural/layout (`flex flex-col`, `gap-[Npx]`, `p-[Npx]`, `items-*`, `text-[Npx]`, `rounded-[Npx]`, `w-/h-*`, …), keeping literal hex colors inline (Option A).
- Derive the **safelist** (`@source inline(...)` brace-expansions) covering every class the renderer can emit.
- This rewrites the emission + ~22 test assertions.

**B. Tailwind integration + embedded binary**:
- `build.rs` embeds the pinned per-platform standalone binary (`include_bytes!` by cfg, MIT-bundled).
- Default `@theme` config with **Inter** (OFL woff2), developer v4-CSS override, developer `@source` globs.
- `pathland_tailwind_compile` (C ABI) spawns the embedded binary at startup, returns compiled CSS; serve it.

**C. JNA shim** for `com.pathland.render.html` (replace the drifting retained Java renderer), **demos switched**, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`, golden vectors.

## Alternatives (in case you'd rather change direction)
- **Push + PR what's landed** — 9 commits are already on origin; a PR-to-main would lock in the foundation and get CI feedback before the big Tailwind churn.
- **A transport P3 slice** — extend the client (`frameCount` gap detection, server-side batch coalescing). Smaller, independent of Tailwind.
- **Re-scope the grant doc** — deferred to late by design; premature now.

## A couple of decisions worth flagging before I start Tailwind
1. **Emission breadth**: full Tailwind conversion of every component/property now, or land structural (stacks/padding/spacing/size) first and leave decorative (fonts/borders/shadows) as inline style for a follow-up? *(I lean: structural first — it's the visible, demo-impacting 80% and keeps the change reviewable.)*
2. **Binary availability at build time**: since building the cdylib embeds the ~20-30MB binary, should the embed be **optional** (a feature flag `tailwind-embed`, default on) so plain `cargo test`/`check-wasm` CI stays fast, with the embedded build exercised only in the packaging/CI step that ships the artifact? *(I lean: feature-gated embed — keeps dev iteration fast.)*

## In progress (P2a)

- **Tailwind structural emission (Phase 1 — landed)**: stacks → `flex flex-col`/

  `p-[Npx]`/per-edge; width/height → `w-[Npx]`/`w-full`/`w-fit`; spacer →

  `z-[N]`; opacity → `opacity-[N]`; `VISIBLE=0` → `hidden`; position/offset →
  `absolute` + `left-[Npx]`/`top-[Npx]`; zstack → `relative w-full h-full` +
  `absolute inset-0` children. Literal hex colors stay inline (Option A).

  effects, text layout) remain inline (Phase 2).

  structural classes the renderer can emit (named utilities + arbitrary-value
  ranges) for the `@source inline(...)` compiler input; the class set is
  generated from the same table used by emission, so emission and safelist
  cannot drift. Runtime-collected arbitrary values complement it once the
  compiler is wired.
- **Tailwind v4 integration (Phase 3)**: embedded per-platform standalone binary
  (MIT, bundled per the pinned license, feature-gated), default `@theme` + Inter
  config, developer override, compile-at-startup (`pathland_tailwind_compile`),
  serve compiled CSS.
- **C ABI cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` /
  `_tailwind_compile` / `_free`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA shim).

# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 1, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`com.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
(the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `compileTailwind(override, classes)`
  returns the compiled Tailwind CSS via `pathland_tailwind_compile`; `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Full Rust renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render with
  Tailwind utility classes (structural + decorative), ARIA/event attributes,
  `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, and
  literal colors inline (Option A).
- **Demos use the shim**: `SessionApp` no longer calls `applyFrame`; SSR renders
  the mount frame through `HtmlRenderer.render(sink.frame(), rootId)`. The
  renderer is compiled once at startup.

## Not implemented / gaps

public class MediaType extends MimeType implements Serializable

A subclass of MimeType that adds support for quality parameters as defined in the HTTP specification.

This class is meant to reference media types supported by Spring Framework. If your application or library relies on other media types defined in RFCs, please use`parseMediaType(String)` or a custom utility class.

content.text:
Root cause confirmed. **Spring's `MediaType` has no `TEXT_CSS_VALUE` constant.** The Spring `MediaType` constants include `TEXT_HTML`, `TEXT_PLAIN`, `TEXT_XML`, `TEXT_EVENT_STREAM`, `TEXT_MARKDOWN` — but **there is no `TEXT_CSS`/`TEXT_CSS_VALUE`** (CSS isn't in Spring's curated constant list). The compile error is exactly that: `MediaType.TEXT_CSS_VALUE` doesn't exist, so `TailwindCssController.java:37` fails to compile.

## The fix

Replace `MediaType.TEXT_CSS_VALUE` with the literal string `"text/css"` in the `@GetMapping produces`:

```java
@GetMapping(value = "/tailwind.css", produces = "text/css")
public ResponseEntity<String> css() { ... }
```

And optionally simplify line 39 to use the same literal (it currently uses `MediaType.valueOf("text/css")`, which works, but for consistency):
```java
return ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.valueOf("text/css")).body(css);
```

This is a minimal, localized fix in the **Spring demo only** (`pathland-spring-boot-demo/.../TailwindCssController.java`). The Quarkus equivalent (`TailwindCssResource`) uses Jakarta's `@Produces("text/css")` string, which is correct — no change needed there.

## Note on why this wasn't caught locally
The demo modules (`pathland-spring-boot-demo`, `pathland-quarkus-demo`) are **excluded from the local JDK-17 test run and CI** (`-pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`), so this compile error only surfaces when actually compiling the demo — which is exactly what you're doing. That's a recurring gap (CI doesn't build the demos); worth a follow-up to make the demo modules compile in CI too.

## Plan
1. Edit `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/java/com/pathland/spring/TailwindCssController.java` line 37: `produces = MediaType.TEXT_CSS_VALUE` → `produces = "text/css"`.
2. (Optional) unify line 39's `contentType` to the `"text/css"` literal for clarity.
3. Rebuild the Spring demo to confirm it compiles.
4. Commit as a small fix; push to `feature/enterprise-sre` (updates PR #75).
5. Consider adding a follow-up issue: **build the demo modules in CI** so this class of compile error is caught.
